reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is worth the trip even in the rain. Take the Icelandic advice and DO NOT get close to the surf. The waves here are ferocious and they do not behave in a predictable manner.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, but dangerous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely one of the most spectacular places in Iceland, with soaring basalt rocks, caves, black pebble beach, seastacks ... but also treacherous and dangerous "sneaker waves" that have been the cause of death of several visitor in recent years.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is absolutely beautiful! Plenty of photo opportunities! It can get crowded though I would love to come back closer to sunset next time!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: black sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible rock formations and black sand. A nice walk to take in the coastline and the variety of eroded rock.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It’s crowded and nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s ok for the fun stones and a view back towards the dyrholaey. But it looks way too crowded for this view which is good but not outstanding like the rest of the places in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Uniquely Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Despite a nasty wet breeze blowing off the ocean, I made the trek down to the beach to view as much as I could.  It is a gorgeous location with cliffs of interesting shaped rocks, the "trolls" offshore, a cave area and puffins and sea birds flying all about.  I was fascinated by it all and was so disappointed we didn't have better weather in which to enjoy the beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must See in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Said to be the world's most beautiful non-tropical beaches.  I’ve seen black sand beaches in Hawaii, but Reynisfjara takes the cake.  Unparalleled.  Caves to wander among.  Of course, you can see the iconic basalt stacks of Reynisdrangar.  Depending on the season, you can see puffins roosting in the cliffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely worth a stop for this unique view.. the most dangerous beach in iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and rock formations…interesting is the most dangerous beach in iceland because of sneaker waves?!  We stopped here in the rain and mist but still managed good photos.  Decent coffee shop with free toilet for customers, 200isk toilet for non customers (hot chocolate is 500isk)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach, great basalt pillar cliffs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Make sure you abide by the warning signs, this beach is dangerous but fantastic to visit. Especially in the evening with the Puffins flying from the cliffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: NOT OVERRATED! Amazing Cave!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had mixing feelings coming to Vik... thinking that many places may be overhyped and overcrowded at the same time - but as I learned about many stops along the way in the first couple days before arriving to Reynisfjara Beach, not only all those places are as amazing as people say but also they aren't that terribly overcrowded - and we visited in the middle of summer! The black beach, the basalt columns, the cave, the size and scale of this place... it's just a serene experience and almost hard to believe it's made by nature - it looks almost as if some some alien mammoth type of creature lived in that cave - stunning view!There are indeed many people here, but they are in many areas of easy access attractions of Iceland, but everyone takes turns at their "picture moment" and people were generally respectful of one another - plus this place is huge - look how small we all are against the cave :) TIP: there is a cute Black Beach Restaurant right by the parking lot upon arrival - not sure why people review it so poorly here on TripAdvisor but we stopped there for a coffee to warm up after crazy winds at Dyrholaey and we enjoyed it a lot - outside tables are available, "free restrooms" (looks like normally you need to pay but they were broken/unlocked) and there is also a hot dog stand - otherwise right around the mountain going east there is a cute town of Vik with more choices for food

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Puffin paradise!,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 2 magic things not to miss here….  First the Puffins living on the side of the cliffs. Magical how there launch into to see with wings flapping wildly😀We lucky because of guide told they should have migrated by now (late August). I guess the amazing warm weather persuaded them to stay while.Secondly the rock columns formations are fascinating. Great place to visit with a decent restaurant on site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular!  Beautiful basalt formations, and puffins!  Don't miss this.  The black sand beach is incredible to see, and the offshore columns are spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A unique place to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After watching several sneaker waves at this beach via YouTube, it was neat to be there. The beach is certainly unique. I was so happy to see the puffins were still there. That made my entire Icelandic travels!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not to be missed.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Tough to walk on the beach, but certainly a highlight to see.  The rock formation along and in the water are really amazing.  Just don't get too close to the water or turn your back on the sea as it has claimed many lives.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the highlights of our trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black beach, huge waves, basaltic columns, caves, plenty of opportunities to take the most memorable photos of your life

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand is amazing and the basalt columns make for a nice backdrop.  We went in the evening and their were many puffins coming in with fish for their nests.  There are signs regarding the dangers of the ocean here that must be heeded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful black sand beach with basalt columns
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand beach with basalt columns and striking rock formations.  A must-see.  A bit overcrowded during the day, but worth a stop when driving the south road in and around Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible beach to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an incredible place.The rock formations are something I will remember forever. The scale! They are massive and look otherworldly. It is busy here, but it is worth the drive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Completely worth the drive and the crowd!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Along with Dyrholeay on 218 off route 1, this is the other “come on, you really have to see this” in South Iceland.  We drove past 218 to start here, where in the distance you can indeed find a gorgeous view of the Dyrholeay arch and islands.  But Lord.  Do mind the signs—the waves even on an incredibly calm and windless day we’re very strong—but the basalt formations here are simply mind blowing, from 200 yards or 2 inches.  We even saw some puffins swimming a hundred yards off shore.  Yes yes there are people milling around here, but it is worth the crowd.  The little restaurant there supplies a WC if you need one, and the sandwiches were really very good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Commercialized tourist trap
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This plane was once a beautiful, serene spot in nature but over the years it’s been heavily commercialized, a restaurant put in, and is now teeming with hundreds of people. Sad to see what it’s become. Be prepared for masses of tourists coming here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are comparing black sand beaches in Iceland, this one is better than the one in Vik.  It has everything: black sand, sneaker waves, basalt columns, plenty of parking.  There is a restaurant there (we didn't go in) with a pay toilet attached that appeared to take only coins.  Was a little crowded in mid-June, so I'm sure it gets worse as the summer progresses.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular Scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the most spectacular natural areas we have ever seen!  The area hiking was fantastic as well. In addition to the amazing scenery, we saw a seal hunting and then resting on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for photos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to this beach very early in the morning (around 5am) just to feel the atmosphere and to look at the famous Halsanefshellir Cave there. The morning light makes the sea and surroundings very atmospheric, and the black sand really does have silvery streaks in it. I think this beach is a must-see if one is around Vik. We enjoyed taking photographs there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a short drive to the beach from the ring road. Its very pretty. and worth a stop , we did not walk far but took lots of photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful beach. The sand is so black. Make sure to stroll the left end of the beach and you will be able to get away from some of the tourists. The basalt columns are cool. The only downside is the Instagrammers all clamoring for their epic shot. It is really obnoxious. Some will get upset if you sit to long. The views in both directions is quite stunning. Take your pictures and put your camera away and take time to just enjoy the beach for what it is

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see in the area for beautiful black sand, black rock pearls and vistas. Quick drive from Vik, easy parking. Windy. Beware of the surf, distraction of views and photo taking will land you with shoes full of water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing nature
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The free parking is right next to the beach and is therefore convenient. The scenery of the lone rocks (Reynisdanger) is simply amazing. Everything is black in sight. The column rocks are the main photo spots. There are many review warning against the sudden waves. I cannot over emphasize it as we were almost victims of this.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Much busier than the black sand beach lots of Instagrammers here. Nice beach if you are in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous and magical beach! This is a must stop on your tour of Iceland! The basalt salt columns are so neat and fun for the kids to climb on. The caves are so cool! It is a beautiful destination!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my favorite spots in all of Iceland!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: During every trip out to Iceland - I have always spend time on the beach admiring the beautiful waves and ever-changing sky.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant visit 30 min but can stay long
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good free parking. Restaurant on sight. You will need change ISK for toilets.Beautiful views, nice long walk - very photogenic.Beware waves really do sneak up on you fast and sharp.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was so beautiful however it was pouring with rain/ very windy when we visited so didn't get to truly appreciate it. The parking was free and only a 5 minute walk away. Definitely worth a visit but just check out the forecast beforehand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I've seen many beaches in the world, but this one is amazing! The beauty of this place is breathtaking, and the power of the ocean makes you feel like one of the grains of black sand... Mother Nature made a huge, huge job!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was awe inspiring but also demonstrated mother nature’s intensity. You do need to be aware of your surroundings for the every 9th or 10th wave the comes up a little higher. This is where the Atlantic is very powerful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sitesee ing.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is awesome. Like many attractive places in Iceland it is free. The black sand beach was amazing. Such awesome views and great for photography and creating memories. It should not be passed up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Otherworldly place!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most spectacular black sand beach I’ve ever seen! What a stunning otherworldly place!! This is the place where you can experience the incredible beauty and the immense power of nature all at once!💙🤍🖤

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had to visit this beach especially as we stayed nearby. Luckily we had a great morning visit. It was bright but very cold. The Black sand really stood out against in the sunlight and snow.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dramatic and wild but beware!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cold windy wild day on this beautiful beach. We saw the signs for sneaker waves but really weren’t prepared for how quickly and high up they come. We were fine but since visiting I’ve seen plenty of examples of people taken out so read the signs and take care especially if you have young kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stormy weather a bonus
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably one beach you don’t want good weather for…the black sand and rock formations work best in stormy weather.Visited on a windy day, briefed on the sneaker waves, but still saw people getting caught out by the freak waves. Be careful.Plenty of great photo opportunities and a good on-site restaurant

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the black sand beach today as part of the south Iceland tour and it was wonderful. From the ferocious sea with waves that crash with such force, wind so strong it blows black sand at your face, the amazing rock formations created by lava forming in that shape and obviously this being part of a Game of Thrones set makes it a must visit place in the south coast.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful spot outside of VIC not a bad drive to get to
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a wonderful place to stop and visit. Doesn’t have to be a perfect day to enjoy the scenic view! The little restraint there is tasty and the bathrooms are clean, walk along the beach and have fun, but I did see a bunch of dummies getting to close to the water and not only get soaked but one got sucked out into the water! She sat on the beach for a second to catch her breath, but there’s definitely a rip rise out there, don’t play in the super cold water!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really Cool
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a super windy day, but the waves were huge!! Super cool to see in person, would definitely recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing sights
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Some of the best photos I took on my Iceland trip were from this beach. The basalt columns were so large and wonderful and the black sand beach was amazing. They have signs warning you about 'sneaker waves" that will come out of nowhere and they are not kidding. I guess it has killed some tourists who weren't paying attention. I did accidentally get my boots wet but luckily I wore waterproof boots (recommended for all of Iceland).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not the only black beach in Iceland, as you can suspect, but it is beautiful with soft finely ground sand and smooth pebbles.  The sea stacks are dramatic and beautiful, and the cliffs with birds were very scenic.  Unfortunately, we were not there for the puffin season, more the pity.  But we spend a good couple of hours roaming around and enjoying the windy day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach late at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited here between 12am-1am in summer (July). Still very bright outside even though the sun was below the horizon.Super cool black sand beach, with basalt pillars and a cave, plus unique rock formations just off-shore in the water. Splendid place for photography.Plenty of parking and what appeared to be a building or two that sells drinks and food, but of course were closed given how late it was when I was there.Be careful of the water if you decide to go in and even if you just get close to the water - people die in this area due to rogue-waves / sneak-waves appearing out of nowhere. Signs in the parking lot warn you of this.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive Geological Features
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The volcanic lava features on the beach are very impressive so this is well worth a short stop. The waves are extremely powerful here so be careful with young children or the elderly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous black beach, lava beach. The rock columns are amazing, so is the cave. Enough parking space. Dangerous beach because of the waves, there are enough warnings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went here early in the morning at around 8:30 and it was beautiful - there’s a crazy wind tunnel at the beach - we almost felt like we will be blown away. We were finding it difficult to walk! But it’s worth going to

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a wonderful place to visit along the Ring Road. The striking black sand, the basalt columns, the birds flying amongst the cliffs and the powerful waves all make for a wonderfully sensorial experience.  Easily accessible from the parking lot - just ensure you don't go close to the waves. Signs about that warn of creeper waves. They aren't kidding.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magic place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were lucky, with excellent sunny weather while visiting Rynisfjara beach. Magic place! We spent there 2 hours feeling like seals on hot rocks :-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach to Appreciate the Black Sand, Rock Formations, and Birds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I visited Reynisfjara Beach while exploring the southern coast and it was a beautiful stop! The black sand is mesmerizing and we enjoyed watching the waves of all different sizes washing up on the shore. The columnar basalt formations are amazing to see in person, and we enjoyed the offshore formations as well.We arrived in the late afternoon and there were a ton of other people in the area. It may be best to go early if you want a more quiet visit.We didn't see any signs prohibiting drones so my husband used his drone and we saw several others operating drones in the area but have since learned drones are not permitted. Parking was convenient but a bit packed. It was packed on the first day that we tried to visit, so we returned the next day and managed to get a space.This is definitely worth a stop if you're in the area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited while it was cold, rainy and grey and it was still one of my favorite stops on our trip! The cave, the basalt columns, and the view of Dyrhólaey make for some amazing photos. Be careful near the water, but don't miss this stop!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant surprise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a cool place. There’s an alcove, soon to be cave. There’s basalt columns or haystacks near shore, basalt columns and black sand beach. There’s a little cafe nearby to watch life go by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A little busy, but very beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As the saying goes, the earlier you can stop by, the less crowded it will be. Unfortunately we didn't roll through until around noon, so we were competing for photos with several other tourists and a full parking lot. This did take away slightly from the experience, but Reynisfjara is so beautiful that it didn't matter, it was still an amazing stop and we got some amazing photos! The majestic earth shooting from the powerful waves, the ominous and breathtaking basalt columns, and the dark and piercing black sand... It was well worth the stop! There is a restaurant here (didn't eat at it) as well as well as restrooms, but there is a small fee for the restrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing but be Careful of the Waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a popular and stunning beach with interesting basalt lava formations and offshore stacks. Be careful on the beach though as apparently tourists drown every year swept out to sea by the powerful waves.There is a restaurant/cafe with good facilities next to the car park. Fully accessible spot without need for 4WD.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Never saw a beach like that, black sand and pebbles. Beautiful and with an outstanding view.Free parkingEasy to reachParking in the beach, walk only 3min

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach - and nearby Basalt cave
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Weather wise - It was not best of the day. However the beach was so different from what we are used. Beautiful with contrasting white waves

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See For Any Trip To Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Impossible to describe.  One of the fascinating outdoor attractions in Iceland.  Definite tour stop for a tour of the Ring Road, but also worth driving to as an excursion from Reykjavik.  Unfortunately, it has become a stomping ground to tourists and tour buses, so congestion and parking are now issues.  Many ignorant tourists think it's fun to photo themselves at the ocean's edge despite all the warnings of "creeper waves" claiming other ignorant tourist's lives in the past.  The caves, basalt columns, sea spikes, black sand, puffins, all combine to make this a uniquely Icelandic natural attraction near the southern town of Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: arresting views in all directions, but quite crowded....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: short detour from Ring Road, crowded given proximity to Vik; turbulent surf, varied rock formations....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent black beach. Got to be a bit wary of the sneaker waves that could come up to you without much warning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awe and Wonder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: How often can you see something you had never imagined?  These black towering basalt formations will inspire the feeling of awe and wonder.  Driving from the main road follow the sign along a curvy side road, past a picture perfect church, which will lead you to a crowded parking lot.  There is a cafe and bathrooms.  The restaurant requests you pay for the restrooms if you are not a patron.  It is a short walk to the black sand beach.  Crawl onto the columns. Attempt self-ies.  No need to hurry in August.Reynisfjara is not Reynisdrangur or Reynisfjall or the geothermal river named Reykjadalur.  Be careful when programing GPS in your rental.  Or double check your entry on your cell phone.  An auto-fill feature can be disastrous.  It is a 2.5 hour drive from Reykjavik. However,  it actually took me 4 hours to arrive because I stopped at Dryholaey and several waterfalls on my way.   After visiting these grand natural temples,  I was disappointed visiting the beach at Vik.  Dryholaey, Vik and Reynisfjara are all different, yet, very close together. They seem to share the same shore on the south of Iceland.  The hardest part of this adventure is trying to take a picture to truly capture its magnificence.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The basalt columns at the end of the beach are dramatic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a rather showery and very cloudy day when we drove up from Vik.  Usefully, there is a quite large café/restaurant on the edge of the car park and close to the beach.  We did have a good coffee there.  The beach itself is quite spectacular with its steeply shelving black sand.  Visitors are warned about the surprise rogue (sneaker) waves which have been known to carry off unsuspecting tourists to a watery grave.  Beware of this and don’t turn your back.  We saw a couple of tourists do this and a wave covered their ankles.  The incredible and very tall basalt columns at the end of the beach are the main attraction and they are worth a pose and photo or two, perhaps with the towering Reynisdarngur sea stacks framed in the background.  Again, this attraction should not detain you too long.  Allow a maximum of 15 to 30 minutes on the beach and more if you are visiting the café/restaurant.  Seemingly, this place can be very busy in normal years and the advice is to come early or late.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach to spend peaceful 1-2 hours. The black sand and rock formations are interesting to see, but it also should be noted that the area has some more beautiful places to visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular black sands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing basalt rock formations and endless black sand beach. Great for a long walk; kids enjoyed climbing the rocks and playing with pebbles. Puffins and sea gulls resting on the rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black dragons live here - I know it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love it. On a misty day this was super cool. The basalt columns are crazy, there are puffins everywhere, allegedly there are killer sneaker waves, looking at those two spikey islands in the distance, you are sure a black dragon is going to swoop in....Love this beach, stop for 30 mins, perfect

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique and stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand is beautiful. The rock formations are like something out of another world. Do watch the waves - don’t stand too close as the sneaker waves will get you and make you wet or worse drag you out to sea. Loads of birds to watch too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: outsanding - don't miss!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: stunning unique black sand beach. easy access from parking lot, amazing photo opps with the large rocks in the ocean, black sand, amazing basalt columns, and white flowers peeking though the rocks. could have spent so much time here but it was windy and cold. really beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Out of this world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I mean this place is gorgeous and surreal at the same time, mystifying black sand, black carved rocks, cave with unique ceiling. It is like you are on another planet, the scenery is so out of this world. Parking nearby is free and so is the experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning! The beauty of this beach makes this a must see in my opinion. There is a small cafe and a toilet, but you must have Icelandic coins to use it! The waves can get a little high, so use caution. The sand and the rocks are beautiful. If you look up, you can see the puffins. I have never seen anything like this beach and my experience here will stay with me!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Yes!  Stop and see this beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Out of this world gorgeous.  The basalt columns, the rock stacks out at sea, the caves - this place is amazing!  I got a tip from our Airbnb host to go out to the cliffs at 10pm to see the puffins leave their nests - it was fantastic!  My first time seeing puffins in the wild.  This is a peaceful place that is absolutely worth stopping to see.  FREE but worth so much!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must-see in Vik!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous, dramatic, other-worldly beach with black sand, basalt columns, green cliffs, and a cave.  Easy walk down the beach; great photo opportunities!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dramatic black beach and rocks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When we visited it was very misty and the lack of visibility added an eerie aura to the black sand and dramatic rock formations.Sadly we couldn’t see the rock stacks in the sea but the beach was still very dramatic and well worth a visit.We also saw a few puffins which finished off the visit nicely.There is a well sized car park, cafe and it is free to visit the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning place. Unique and otherworldly!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are driving the ring road, do not miss this. It's only a 4km detour. There's a lot of black sand/pebble beaches in Iceland, however the basalt columns and offshore rock formations really make Reynisfjara a unique stop. Definitely heed the warnings of sneaker waves and don't turn your back on the ocean. However, it's not a dangerous place as long as you are reasonably careful and stay a few meters from the high water mark.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was raining when we visited but you must walk this beach to see the iconic rock formation from a far. There are fields of surrounding flowers that look like lavender but are Alaskan flowery plant:

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take my breath away
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After living in Iceland for 53 years, I FINALLY got to Reynisfjara and it was totally worth the wait.  The batter between the forces of people vs ocean, the view to Dyrhólaey, the black sand and the amazing rock formation took my breath way

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nothing special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was one of the most crowded attractions in the whole Iceland during our stay. However, i have to say that for us it was nothing special and could be avoided.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful for a short visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful view with impressive basalt rocks.It is not safe to swim but it is nice to just walk along the shore.All tiny black rocks over the entire beach which makes the beach very special.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool - but keep at least 10m from the water, this is a dangerous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were lucky that our tour guide took us here, more on what to see below. DANGER: The warning signs about "creeper waves" are no joke. . Occasionally and without warning a large wave can come, and the current is extremely strong. Our guide informed us how people die here every year and of actual fatalities and near misses they had witnessed in their company. So: Just keep a good 10m away from the water's edge - seriouslyReally loved seeing the basalt columns and cave, the many puffins nesting in the rocks. Great view of the cape if you have a clear day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beach with stunning views - be aware of big waves!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very big black beach with stunning views - lots of puffins and impressive geologic formations. Beware of extremely dangerous waves - not too close to the water and children away from the water, even if the many beautiful pebbles invite you to play!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Trolls or just basalt
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing nature and you may wonder if it is really trolls who made these basalt cliffs. Anyway photogenic and goes well with the extremely fine black lava sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black beach with rocks. The light there at the end of the dag is beautiful. When you're in Iceland you have to go there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Come early or late in the day to beat the crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is worth the drive. Large blackbeach with interesting stone- and rock formation. During summer, the birdcliffs are populated with serval birdspecies - including puffins. Do pay attention the warnings concerning the potentially deadly waves: This is the North Atlantic, people!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful Beach for 30 min visit. But remember to go to nearby Dyrholey which has longer walks and beautiful views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited with the kids. Must see place, and a great spot to take some family photos, but you must truly watch out to not go too near the ocean as the waves can me treacherous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful in March Late Afternoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view was stunning of the large volcanic rock formations cresting out of the ocean. We saw a group of horseback riders on the beach. Our tour guide told us about the myth of the tri-masted ship and the two female trolls, adding to the mystery of the setting. Beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning and wild place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The contrast between the black sand and the white foamy surf is amazing, and the power of the waves is stunning. It was cold and wet and wild. A natural wonder

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came to this beach at the end of the Iceland winter. There was still plenty of snow it can be quite cold and windy. I strongly recommend that you come early between the hours of 6am-10am (the latest) this place has a restaurant close to the beach and attracts massive amounts of tourist and tourist busses. If you’re into any kind of photography, I highly recommend you get to the car park at first light. Also the beach is drone friendly so feel free to throw your drone up and get a different perspective. However, keep an eye on the wind and the basalt columns which can cause a magnetic interference to your drones GPS if you get too close. Also keep an eye on the ocean, the waves can catch you out if you’re not carful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A true beauty !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjar is a beautiful, small, black sand beach. It was created by lava flowing into the ocean which cooled, as it touched the water. Also happens to be one of the shoot locations for Game of Thrones series. I only remember the beach for 2 things – the powerful sneaker waves, and the huge Basalt columns with some rock formations. The ocean looks quite calm and inviting but these sneaker waves can appear, when least expected. There are number of signs on the beach warning tourist to be cautious.  So enjoy your stop her but always be cautious !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An immense experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited in January, there were high winds and a hail storm with vertical hale and we completely loved it. It was an absolutely unique situation to be in, like visiting another planet. The black sand against the white of snow and of the waves was beautiful. The pinnacles and rock formations on the beach were stunning. Beware when walking round the rocks to the cave that you could get cut off by waves. Waterproof clothing is a must. The toilets separate from the ones in the cafe have a card payment option but this does not always connect, much better to use the loos in the cafe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely tidal area on the black sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large tidal area with an isthmus of curving black sand currently covered in snow. Lovely towering rock buffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated, and dangerous sneaker waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are nicer black beaches in Iceland, and the cave itself, while magnificent, was rather shallow. There were many warnings about the sneaker waves but as usual, tourists ignore them. The waves were the highlight of the visit, watching people get soaked in the cold Atlantic waters was fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful views, but watch for Sneaker Waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We viewed a beautiful sunset from Reynisfjara beach, which is an ideal time to be there.  You will have lots of other folks with you, but just walking down the beach a couple of minutes will take you out of the crowd.  If you choose to walk up by the stacks (in every picture ever taken here),  please be aware of the water.  Large waves can break unexpectedly and you'll find yourself at best wet - and at worse  being swept out to sea by the wave. Three days before our arrival, the Icelandic Monitor reported the rescue of two boys who were caught in a Sneaker Wave.  So enjoy the beauty and be mindful of nature

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful surroundings
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is wonderful: fine black  sand beach, restless waves, tall bazalt columns, clear blue sky! I fell in love with this place! A spot which definitely deserve a stop on your trip to south Iceland!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Horseback Riding - Viking Tour Express
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a Great Tour. Picked up promptly and taken to the stable.. outfitted and went over all the safety rules. Then it  was on to the ride. The Icelandic Horses were amazing.. well behaved with enough spirit to make the ride unforgettable. Highly recommend this tour package to everyone. Once you get the hang of riding these horses (almost immediately), it’s simply something you will never forget.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is gorgeous.  Be sure to round the corner - you will miss alot if you do not.  The only word of caution keep an eye on the see..the waves move up the beach quickly...we saw several very spendy cameras go under water as the users turned  away from the water to take pics..the boom water ruled.  The cliffs, sea, and sky are gorgeous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really great view. Parking was around $7 but that is the only expense. We enjoyed seeing the basalt column cliff and walking up and down the beach. It is very beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place, but don't turn your back on the sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a beautiful black sand beach with columnar basalt and a sizable cave. When I was there, the place was crowded with selfie-seekers, several of whom got soaked by large waves when they stopped paying attention to the ocean. The waves here are quite large and are irregularly sized, so it pays to maintain situational awareness. It's a beautiful place.I visited via a bus tour from Reykjavik; wish I'd had more time to explore Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Check out the cave!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A worthwhile stop. What I liked most here at Reynisfjara, was the Hálsanefshellir sea cave and Gardar cliff. The Reynisdrangar sea stacks were also cool to see. Amazing rock formations! Many photo ops.We spent about an hour here.This was one of the most crowded stops on our South Coast tour.Recommended!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Raw Nature
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked along the beautiful black lava sands, this was February and the winds were blowing strongly and the sea waves were pounding the beach and outcrops.  This was nature giving a taste of its power.  There were plenty of birds in the cliffs, but they were not venturing far from their nests in the high winds.  Beware of the waves, every now and then there is a particularly strong breaker that will soak your feet and ankles, and can knock you over, if you stray too close to the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Raw and rugged
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited on a rainy day so the waves were really high.  It was very atmospheric.  The cave and cliffs are stunning and the beach is gorgeous, just wish I could have seen it glittering in the sunlight.  Be careful, the waves are dangerous so stay well away from them but aside from that, this beach is well worth a visit and I believe it's where some of the Eastwatch by the Sea scenes were set from Game of Thrones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: LOST MY PHONE IN THE SEA
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So i got to close to the crashing waves and my phone fell out of my pocket into the sea. I didn't realise until i started walking back tot he car.  A must see, however, dont get too close to the waves lol

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is just beyond beautiful and a must visit when in Iceland. Very easy access but beware of the waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beware of deadly sneaker waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, pitch black sand (or pebble) from gradually wave eroded volcanic material. The sand/pebbles get gradually bigger as one moves up the beach, and the beach stretches out all the way to Dyrhólaey in the distance, where one can see the stone arch. On the left when you walk onto the beach is a dolomite cave with the interesting geometric stone columns.As is to be expected, the beach is relatively crowded with tourists, getting an “unoccupied” photo is difficult. There is a restaurant nearby. Well worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As dangerous as amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with pitch black sand and small rocks. Basalt columns, or trolls, caves and shaped rocks create stunning views expecially on sunset time.Cons? Extremely touristy. You cannot take a pic without tens of people passing by.But it definitely worth to see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As dangerous as beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A huge sign anounce the death of a turist pulled by waves. Well, no more than 3 minutes after we arrived, a wave almost took a boy of 8 years the same way. The parents were too distracted by the stone formations and the boy was walking into the sea without no adults around. If you go, try to do it very early in the morning to enjoy a bit of peace taking your pictures before the mass of turist buses arrive. After you could be pushed for an urgent picture

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, different to any other beach I have seen around the world. Iceland being volcanic I guess it’s no surprise .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has a little bit of everything; there are pillars in the water, columns on the beach that you can climb, and a cave that shields you from the rain/wind & makes an awesome backdrop for photos. Be careful that you don't get soaked by a wave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An absolute must when doing the Ring Road
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful! Its about a 5 minute walk once you park to get down to the beach and to get close to the basalt columns. The sheer power and force of the waves is both exhilarating and terrifying at the same time. You can feel the rumble when the waves break and come crashing on the beach. There were many tourists who were not watching and got soaked by a wave that came in quick and fast. Which is not fun for them as it was very windy and quite cold.We had a very scary moment when an elderly Chinese woman was trying to get a selfie and went a bit too close to the water and was knocked down and dragged about 10 meters towards the ocean before being able to regain her footing and be helped by others around her.The magnificence of this place should be enjoyed thoroughly, but also respected as it can easily take your life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome place. Remember to stay far from the water if you don't want to get wet! The waves are unpredictable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are driving along the south coast I’d highly recommend turning off for Vik, and driving down to this beach. We went just as it was starting to get dark, there wasn’t as many tourists as I was expecting. I couldn’t believe the colour of the sand, I had read reviews but I didn’t expect the sand and pebble stones to be pure black! The sea can be very unpredictable on this beach though so I would be very careful. We saw a few people get soaked feet unexpectedly.In my photos it shows the contrast between the sand and the sea foam.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Reynisfjara is not just another black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara is more than a magnificent black sand beach.  Here you will find some towering basalt columns that make up the rock formations adjacent to the beach.  There are also basalt columns that make up a couple of rocky sea stacks off shore that are called Reynisdrangar.  There is one legend that these stacks were once trolls who tried to trick sailors to sail there ships to shore at night, however, they stayed out too long and the sun appeared at dawn and the trolls were frozen into rock.  The Reynisdrangar can be seen in Game of Thrones Season 7 in scenes "north of the wall."  The beach can be dangerous and there are numerous signs warning about "sneaker waves" which can carry people out to sea if they are unaware of the situation.  Visitors are advised to never turn their back on the waves, and keep a safe distance of at least 30 meters.  It is, however, a beautiful place and one of the outstanding black sand beaches in the world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be careful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Look out for the sneaker waves and don't stand too close in the middle of winter as we saw a lot of people get soaked and fall over. The beach is great to see, but wrap up warm in winter.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must if doing the Ring Road
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with the highly unusual basalt stacks. Easy side trip off the Ring Road. Tends to get rather crowded, but still worth the trip. Additional bonus is a quaint little church along the road to the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short stop with nice view!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand beach is beautiful and has its own charm for is formations. The wave can come crashing onto the shore alot further in then you think, so be mindful and keep safe distance from the water. The waves can be dangerous due to the currents. The basalt formations on the side is a good place for a photostop as well. The wind is super strong there due to the open waters so remember to dress warm and enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with great rock formations and caves, many tourists but nonetheless it was still a fantastic thing to see and experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Drive there yourself
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very beautiful beach with its black pebbles and square basalt rocks. We drove there ourselves, which we can only recommend since we had the possibility to stay for a bit longer, and take some great photographs without being disturbed by the other tourists arriving by bus - Most where there for 30 minutes, before leaving again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Have a seat and listen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another stop during our trip around the south of Iceland. Free entry and car park, there was actualy a cafe right on the beachfront selling various cold to hot foods. The beach in the evening was beautiful, with the waves crashing, stillness of the rock face and the ancient basalt columns and the lone trolls in the background.It wasn't as crowded during our visit as it was getting dark. Do practice caution as rogue waves do happen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Deamonic place during a winter time.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Place where to go for Northen sea feeling. Amazing black sandy/peable a long beach end. Beach is finished with a reef and rocks with a caves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Surf Among the Trolls
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach. I find it best to sit among the stones and photograph it in context with its troll cliffs, tumbled, worn boulders, scattered farms and scenes of struggle, decay and survival. The mountain is full of stories. I like to give myself time to let them soak in. What is especially fun beyond that is to take pictures of people meeting the surf coming in from the open Atlantic. There is no foreshow. The waves are just there, smelling of ozone. It is humbling. Take your time. A quick visit does the place no justice. It's stillness that the place can best offer, and it rewards it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Black Sand Beach (But Crowded)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the beach with our Troll tour guide. The views and cliffs were jaw dropping but unfortunately it is very crowded and busy. Check out our Youtube video GoPro HD: Icelandic Layover - (Amsterdam and Brussels) for more info.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: More dangerous than it looks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: People have apparently been pulled into the sea by rogue waves. Black stone pebble beach. Another interesting wilderness spot to stop and appreciate.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful rocky beach along majestic rock formation on the coast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand beach with stunning and sharp rock formation and caves that are jagged in shape coming out of the mountain beside it.  Ocean waves floating in seem to bubble like soap over the black sand. The sand itself feels more like soft rounded stones than sand and it's not fine at all.After a short walk along the beach heading east, you'll find impressive rock formations that make for beautiful photography.There are warnings to not get too close to the waters edge as the waves have much force and can suck you into the ocean very deep if one is not careful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unbelievably Stunning BUT Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking one of a kind place. This is a must see if you are visiting Iceland. The beach itself is unreal. No matter which direction you look it is incredibly stunning. I was blown away. The one HUGE unfortunate problem is the throngs of tourists that are bussed in to this place. It is crawling with people of all ages from all over the world that appear to be there just to get a million pictures and selfies. I get that tourism is extremely important for their economy but ruining world class gems like this by allowing tour companies to transport literally thousands of people a day to this beach (even in off season) isn’t going to end well. I cannot even imagine what it is like in the Summer. If you can manage to ignore all the people and just take in the scenery, you will not be disappointed. Bathrooms and food available. Be aware of the sneaker waves that creep up. 70% of the people there ignored the warning signs and were to wrapped up in their photo shoots and got smashed and soaked by the waves. Fairly dangerous if you don’t pay attention.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Despite the masses of tourists, this is a beautiful stop.  It was crowded with tourists and tourist buses, but it was worth the stop to see the off shore formations and basalt cave.  The weather changes unpredictably in Iceland - the wind was blowing hard the day we were that.  Have your camera and be ready for crowds.  Oh, and watch out for sneaker waves - this beach is dangerous if you don't pay attention.  There is a small cafe/restaurant next to the beach which we did not try.  The beach is made up of black pebbles, which can make walking difficult if you have mobility issues.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is unlike any other I've been to. Here you can see unique rock formations, both in the water and on land. The waves may get pretty big and reach far, so be careful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very unique place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Reynisfjara Beach as part of our South Coast tour. Immediately upon arriving, the tour guide warned us about the “sneaker-waves”, they are very dangerous that can take you very quickly out to the ocean where you have absolutely no chance to break free. As she said, “there is nothing between Iceland and the South Pole”. Aside from the humor, you do need to exercise extreme caution. The black sand beach is absolutely stunning against the waves crashing on the shore. Add to that, the basalt columns and cliff pillars of rock and this beach is absolutely stunning. I must have got bitten by sand fleas here as the next few days both my legs and back were incredibly itchy. Could have happened when leaning against the pillar wall for pictures. Very unique place and totally worth the stop here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Extremely gorgeous and dangerous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This black sand beach and piano-organ-style cliffs with swirling flocks of resident gulls above treacherous "sneaker" waves is a must-visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mother Nature
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The landscape was gorgeous, the sea was windy and those colours, not to speak about the beach. Mother Nature shows just another face in here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful black beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A warning about rogue waves was visible right at the entrance so I was cautious.  But the landscape was stunning, to the point of surreal. I would definitely visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, windy and can get crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was here by myself during dusk and the crowd was almost gone.  It was a nice sight to see the black sand and the rock formations.  I can do without the brutal winds blowing in my face and pushing me around though.  I also came back here with my wife and toddler during the day and it was crowded. There were tourists climbing the rocks all to try to get a picture that was marginal at best.  I can't imagine how crowded this place gets during the peak seasons.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Classic Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One or the more busy beaches but you’ll see why when you go. Beautiful beach with beautiful basalt columns and “caves” to get some great pictures of, or in. Wait out the crowds to get some pictures alone. Also, the restaurant had surprisingly really great food, don’t be afraid to order the fish options or burger

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When I show others my video of this beach they think I've filmed in black and white!  With cloudy skies, black sand and grey ocean, the whole scene is grey or black.  An eerie and unique beach.Visit the Soup Company in Vik after your visit to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Extraordinary !!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A visit to Reynisfjara Beach was one of the highlights of our Iceland vacation.  I feel a visit here is mandatory for anyone visiting Iceland.  It has overwhelming beauty and character on many levels.  We were mesmerized by hexagonal columns of the volcanic rock which was simply beyond words.  Also stunning was the black sand on the beach as well as the amazing rock formations off shore.  Overall, this was a visit which will stay with me forever.  One word of advice - try to get there early in the morning since the tourist size will be minimal at that time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do keep an eye on the shore and don't go  near also keep a look on strong winds as you are on the beach it will feel so much colder but the view is worth it, specially if you visit the light house.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach - Basalt Cliffs - Unique & WINDY!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walk on the black sand beach and enter the basalt caves to touch the rock - it's columnar here, smooth there - very interesting.  This is an awesome beach with great vistas and cliffs that you'll want to run into if the wind picks up as it did when I visited.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful stop along the way
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On a long day trip, we stopped at Reynisfjara beach. I've never seen black sand before. Perfect for a quick stop to grab a few photos & explore the cave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you see nothing else on the South Shore of Iceland, you have to see the incredible natural beauty of the Reynisfjar Beach.  Very serene, despite the power of the waves crashing onto the shore.  Made for stunning photos.  Great memories!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit, it is absolutely stunning!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: OK i went during winter, and the vibe was different. The clouds low, the sky grey, freezing rain and winds that could lift a small child.  This beach is a must, stay a little longer and wait for the crowd to die down to take some stunning pictures. It was a little too windy to fly a drone but i did it anyways. Why? because its a beautiful place and i wanted to capture it from all kinds of angles. lol dont get close to the waves as they look dangerous, also be careful how you park your vehicle... saw this ladies driver door swing open and break the glass among almost knocking her over. The winds here are no joke. so be very careful!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Leprechaun with a pot of gold!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the world famous Reynisfjara black sand beach. We got lucky and saw a double rainbow. The beach is also famous for its dangerous “sneaker-waves” and visitors are advised to never turn their back on them. The Icelandic folklore have interesting stories to tell about these basalt columns.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but windy place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved seeing the beautiful beach and the rock formations. It was very very windy and cold with the sand whipping up into our eyes so dress warm. Be very careful of the waves. We saw one idiot looking down at his phone who was knee deep in water a few moments later. You will die if you get swept out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very popular beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very popular beach with tourist so ideally go early. Free parking, cafe and toilets. Nice cave, basalt columns, pillars of rock, black sand, stunning views. Simply fantastic. Great place to watch the sunset or sunrise.  Avoid 10-4pm due to tourists and drones.  Beware sneaker waves which will wash you out so look after children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Eerie and stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With its unique rock formations, black sand, and crushing waves, Reynisfjara feels otherworldly. Make sure you check tide schedules-- try to get there at low tide so you can walk far along the coast and at a time when the tour busses are gone. Also, the waves really come out of no where, so don't be an idiot and get too close to the water. I saw one spectator nearly knocked to the ground by a rogue wave..he was lucky there were others around to help him.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning! I don’t recommend swimming here since it’s Iceland’s most dangerous beach but it’s beautiful to look at and walk on. Also a must see if you are a Game of Thrones fan as parts of it was filmed here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spent longer here than we thought we would
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We made this our first stop for a day of driving around the south coast and golden circle. It was cold, windy, and there was a mist in the air, but it was all tolerable. We missed all the tour buses with our timing, so it really wasn't that crowded at all. We had never seen anything like this beach and it was fun just to see the wonder on my boys' faces. We enjoyed our time just walking around, picking up the "sand", looking for cool rocks, checking out the basalt columns, and taking lots of photos. If you go here though, please heed the warnings about sneaker waves. We saw way too many people close to, in, and/or not paying any attention to the water. Even my boys were prepped ahead of time and knew to stay far away from the water. It's dangerous and there are warnings for a reason.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Defies description!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a short drive from Vick and just south of Highway 1, you'll find this incredible beach.  The “sand” is black due to the lava formations everywhere.  That’s amazing in itself.  So are the heavy, pounding waves that can rush up onto the beach without warning.  But, the most amazing sight to us was the lava formations behind the beach.  The entire cliff wall looks like stacked pencils, some of which are large enough to stand on, others are smaller and twisted.  It’s astounding the various forms lava can take!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I decided to stop here on our anniversary trip! It was crowded even in October! The waves are intense! We decided to walk around and see a cave right next to the main part of the beach, MISTAKE. we almost got trapped in there because the waves were coming in so fast and they were rough and scary! We had to make a run for it and get out of there! That’s what my husband gets when he has stupid ideas ! After our hearts were done racing we walked down the beach the other way and it was very melodramatic. The beach and views are OK and if you are a game of thrones fan you’ll want to stop here but other than that it was just alright.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must. The black sand is beatiful and the cliffs are worth seeing. Parking is free and there is a restaurant on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely Worth Seeing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black sand, caves and awesome rock formations.  This area is definitely worth the short detour from the Ring Road.  When we were there the wind was howling and the sand was hitting us pretty hard.  It was even hard walking.  But, it was still worth seeing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Easy stop near Vik, very cool beach and rock formations.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you read black sand beach, this is literally black sand.  There is a basalt rock wall worth seeing and a walk to the west will give you views of the arch rock formation located offshore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Underwhelming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A bit like Tenerife or Fuertaventura only without the sun!Nice rock formations in the sea, a bit like the 12 apostles but without the sun!Basalt columns and rocks in the cliffs were interesting.Cold wet and windy, could be ok on a sunny day with blue skies!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MESMERIZING ICELAND - VIK - REYNISFJARA BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara BeachINFO :- A place of stark, wild beauty, this black-sand beach on the south coast is one of Iceland’s most photogenic locations. Here, roaring Atlantic waves batter the Reynisdrangar sea stacks, the black pebble shoreline, and the pyramid-like cliff of basalt columns known as Garðar, where puffins and guillemots can be seen.WHAT TO EXPECT :-Escape the crowds and explore Iceland, marvel at natural wonders including the Sólheimajökull Glacier, with its turquoise streams, the obsidian sands of Reynisfjara Beach, and the historic town of Vik. See, too, the Skógafoss and Seljalandsfoss waterfalls and enjoy the convenience of round-trip transport from your Reykjavik hotel. Note:- Carry boxed lunch and Juice/water is recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Smaller then expected
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nearly every attraction in Iceland exceeded my expectations, Reynisfjara beach did not meet them. I mean, at 4 stars it was still pretty cool and I’d 100% say you should go, but I was expecting to be blown away by this awe inspiring otherworldly black sand beach. Instead, I was met with a surprisingly small beach. Also very busy, even in the mid to light rain we were getting. (the photos look empty because I’m great at timing them)The cave that Jesse and I were both so excited to see from Game of Thrones, was actually more of an indent. I wouldn’t call it a cave. But, it’s still a filming destination so that was cool. All in all, a solid 4 stars. Cool, worth checking out, definitely not as epic as TV would make it appear. Which surprisingly isn’t the case for most of the other filming destinations in Iceland, they look just as amazing as you’d hope.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't Miss Scenic Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't want to pass up the black sand beach, basalt columns, or the rock outcroppings with waves crashing against them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incrdible!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped at this beach for a quick stop and I am glad we did. I have visited black sand beaches in Hawaii, but this texture seemed different. It was otherworldly. I was told that this beach was also used in Game of Thrones, so if you're a fan, it would be fun to see where the filmed. The pictures you take here are very dramatic, and it's certainly worth the stop. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beatiful black sand beach and basalt columns
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyed our visit to Reynisfjara Beach. It was a very windy day, but we enjoyed the gorgeous black sand and beautiful basalt columns. It is an easy walk and a quick visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great stop along the drive in the Ring Road. Be prepared as its always busy. Great views and wonderful place for people interested in photography.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit with friends!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Plenty of folk visiting. From parking lot (black sand beach cafe easily accessible), couple hundred feet to beach.  Basalt columns to left. The light hits them differently if you edge around to cliff face facing ocean..they reflect sun differently, just saying. Plenty of folk about, you have to be strategic to get photo b.c. without folk. Good view of arches down the beach. Climbing arches for that special shot more difficult than you might imagine. Please take your trash out, and be aware of sneaker waves. People die here needlessly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning even in the RAIN!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see part of the Vik beach area. Turnoff is marked with a small yellow sign. Road is after Dyrholaey and before the town of Vik where the Black Beach is located. Do the Vik Adventure Horse riding on Black Beach. Beach is Awesome with the Basalt Rocks.Need 200isk for toilet by Dyrholaey.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great visit and got to see late season puffins
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach with incredible columns.  Got to see a seal in the water just off the beach and the puffins were still there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dramatically Windy and Scenic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited on a day when the Icelandic weather was in full force; very windy and sideways rain. We enjoyed the experience. Even though the weather was a bit rough, we enjoyed seeing the rock spires, the angular basalt cliff and cave hollow, and the expanse of the black sand beach. A coffee in the cafe was a convenient way to warm up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Secure your loose items
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cold and Windy. You get to witness the might of the sea, powerful winds to accompany. Take a nice stroll along the shore if you are prepared to work against the winds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A fascinating beach with black sand.  Well worth exploring the caves at the back with the rock columns.  Be careful of the ‘sneaker waves’.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most famous beach in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The reason for the sand at Reynisfjara being black is that it is formed from heavily eroded volcanic rocks (also known as extrusive igneous rocks), which are black (or obsidian) to begin with as they have been formed from cooled lava which turns black as it cools and hardens. (Ranked in 1991 as one of the ten most beautiful non-tropical beaches in the world.)Reynisdrangar is the name given to the freestanding sea stacks.A MUST SEE!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unmissable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cliffs with convoluted strata and hexagonal columns. Crashing waves. Black sand beach. Sea stacks in the sea - a tall column and a squatter large outcrop. Very well worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand beach with basalt columns, caves and a view of the "Vik trolls". Kids enjoyed listening to the troll legend and watching puffin nests on cliffs. It doesn't look dangerous but be careful as there are warnings everywhere about sneaker waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see from different vistas.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is a great view from Vik waterfront but you should go a few miles west on #1 and turn left toward the ocean. More promonitaries  can be seen from there. Reminder of the California and Oregon coasts. Also an interesting black sand beach in VIK

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spray and thunder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ravishingly raw nature where you will struggle to take a bad photo. The black sand arcs around crashing Atlantic rollers where the elements rule supreme. Get there early to avoid the coach crowds and to better enjoy the nesting seabirds wheeling overhead. Take care NOT to enter the water or get too close to the water's edge as sneaker waves could sweep you away in a heartbeat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All the reviews say the same thing- amazing and gorgeous. It is breathtaking and I recommend checking it out if you can. I saw some people getting really close to the water, even with the signs telling you how dangerous that is. There is a sign that literally shows you how someone died. So enjoy the nature and be smart. It is so beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another extraordinary sight near Vik
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara is a beautiful beach, with powerful (and dangerous) seas. It is definitely well worth the visit. It is one of the few natural sites around Vik that has a small restaurant, so consider planning this visit for lunch time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An easy, must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara Beach Is right off the Ring Road, free, and offers spectacular scenery with the black Sandy beaches, the huge rock outcroppings and amazing basalt columns! It was voted one of the top 10 non-tropical beaches in the world! It can be crowded and there’s a little café at the parking lot area. It’s easy to get to, not a lot of walking and the pay off is well worth while! Don’t turn your back to the waves, as they can sneak up on you and drag you in!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Black Sand Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand beach with basalt columns and a cave.  Not a very far walk from the parking lot but there are a lot of people there, if you want to get a good photo just be patient. Beautiful setting!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So much natural beauty, but be cautious!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is so special, but please, for the love of god be careful. There are plenty of signs warning people not to turn their back on the ocean due to very dangerous & powerful waves and we still saw many people way to close to the water taking photos and not paying attention. Also, it would be great if all the tourists could stop climbing the column cliffs. Yes, the basalt columns are really cool, but stand at the bottom and take your photo so you aren't in everyone else's photos and don't fall and get hurt. It's amazing to be standing on a beautiful black sand beach and then turn around to see a glaciar opposite it. Definitely go, but respect the ocean and the beautiful natural surroundings...take your garbage with you and don't get hurt.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was an impressive black sand beach.   The basalt column rock formations were very unusual.  There were a few puffins nesting in the cliffs.     Restrooms available for a fee.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stunning! but please be careful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is one of the places you must consider visiting.Basalt columns, tha big cave and the sea togeter mix and match perfectly.ùPlease be aware that waves can get pretty dangerous and even deadly cometimes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very different beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very different beach and a special type of beautiful. I believe this beach is where the Game of Thrones East watch by the sea was filmed. The black sand and the lava formations makes this beach an awesome place for photography and videography.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go there when there is low tide so that you can walk around the big boulder. There is a huge cave but it is crowded so go there early or very late.I suggest to walk through all the beach, it takes 1 our to reach the other side and no one do it , everybody stops at the caveThere is also a small cliff behind the boulder where you can see puffins, but to get there you have to take the car and go up to that side , there is a park( f road).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Big waves. Black sand.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great to feel the power of giant waves on jet black sand. Can take pictures with rock stack formations too. Good spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Impressive. Honestly! I loved this beach. If you're into Game of Thrones, don't even think about missing out on this spot. Even if u don't like this series, it's still incredible. You should maybe go there quite early in the morning or quite late in the evening since it's super crowded around midday but you'll still be able to take a few nice shots and enjoy it. This beach's a must!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a short stop!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped by here, since it's right off of Ring Road, and it's a nice way to stretch your legs. We took some photos along the cliffs too. It's a very popular stop with tour groups so it's crowded.They charge you 200 ISK to use the restroom but it's free if you buy something from the cafe located here. The wind is super strong so don't turn your back on the sea and bring a rain jacket, hand gloves and a beanie. A great photo opportunity, check it out!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Make the 5-10 min stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a cool beach with interesting columns but as you went east the beach of blocked off and it was over crowded. Definitely go earlier before the tour groups start to show up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dramatic beach but the most dangerous in Iceland so be careful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very dramatic with the black volcanic sand and columnar basalt caves but I cannot stress enough to be very careful here.  Read the warning signs as you go onto the beach and take heed of what they say.  I have visited several times with school groups and have had students literally blown off their feet. Do not go too close to the sea and never turn your back on it.  This August when I was there with my husband I walked to the end of cliffs and was taking photos when I heard rumbling.  There was a rock slide and large pebbles upto 15 cms long where falling from the cliff onto the beach.  Luckily everybody in the vicinity managed to run away and nobody was injured as it was a relatively small rock slide but still big enough to have killed somebody.  I read that the police had subsequently closed to beach while it was investigated further.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Somethingvway out of the ordinary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I read several reviews where people thought this was average.  Are you kidding?  Maybe in bad weather most of the enjoyment evaporates.  I was is there in good conditions..  the top ten black sand beaches in the world was just published.  Vik from Iceland was on the list. Vik Is a joy and very worthy, but this beach is around the headlands that separate the two beaches and is better that Vik.  The number one blacksand beach was Punalu u  on the Big Island of. Hawaii where I live. It cannot hold up against Reynisfjara.  You must experience both ends of the beach to get the whole idea.  The most popular is the end where the sea stacks are and the basalt rises right out of the black sand.  Standing on the cliff at the other end you look down on a fabulous seastack and get a vista of the whole beach.  If you do this I believe you will have adequately experienced the finest black sand beach in the world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t skip, it is a short visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the view.Weather was cold and wet in August.We’re colorful jackets for great pictures.Short walk from the car parking lot.  Less than .25 mile.Free parking.  Just a short drive off the main road.The black color of the sand and rocks combined with the great view of the North Atlantic was special.A restaurant is on site.  We did not eat.Warning:  Avoid car rental company called Procar.  What a mess that was.  40 minute wait in the airport for their shuttle.  Then 35 minutes in line at their rental office.  Then 40 minutes waiting for them to get our car ready.  2 hour wait after flying in on a red eye flight was ruff.  And then having to agree for them to put a hold on our credit card for 2900 bucks because we declined their high pressure insurance.  That was our big mistake of the trip.  Avoid Avoid Avoid Procar auto rental.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Striking sight, but cold and windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a short walk on the beach with our guide.  The black sand crunching underfoot is beautiful in its own way.  There are cliffs, rocks and waves and, today, a howling cold wind.  The fog and mist off the sea gave an eerie atmosphere.  The most striking feature are the basalt columns, well worth a visit, though just a few minutes are enough on a cold day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Skippable if you are short on time.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The day we visited it became very windy with some pelting light rain.  Since we made the drive, we visited the beach but only spent 5 minutes here.  The black sound is pretty cool but if you are short on time, looking at pics on the internet would suffice.  We did not find this to be in our top attractions but the weather could have influenced our experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Neat beach, be careful of the weather changing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a really neat black sand beach with some awesome geological features, like the basalt columns.  When we visited the weather had changed really fast and it went from sunny to gray and drizzling and super windy within the span of 5 minutes.  The waves picked up and it was actually pretty intense with all the wind, so we didn't linger long.  You mostly go to take some photos and enjoy the view for a minute and then continue on, but it is a must see if you're driving the South Coast.  There's a small cafe here if you want a snack, and if you purchase something at the cafe the restroom is free.  We got coffees, which were much appreciated with the sudden change in weather.  If it's a windy day prepare for this to suck a bit, it was so windy when we went that sand was blowing and the rain was making the wet black sand stick all over our shoes.  I would definitely not have wanted to go near the water as the waves were getting crazy and unpredictable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful and the black sand and rocks are absolutely amazing. When we were there it was extremely windy and raining, so I would love to see it when sunny (or at least not raining).  Definitely worth the trip to see the basalt columns and cave

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Black Sand Beach and Rock Formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful!  We saw some puffins in the water!  I wish we could see them a little closer though.  Be careful with the waves, it's true what they say that they can come up quickly and surprise you.  There's also a cool cave and rock formation here where you can climb up.  Also, there are some legends associated with this place, that the rocks in the water are trolls frozen in time.  When we went it was very crowded, and hard to get a picture without a bunch of neon jackets, but we did manage to get some. If coming from the north, you may want to stop at the natural bridge (Dyrhólaey) first.  We had to backtrack because we went here first.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk to the end of the beach
