reviewsWithKeywords.text: The South of Iceland surprised us with its different terrain, I have been on Black beaches before but this was truly spectacular. It has a strange eery quality to it , and the stacks are super for photos. I would have liked to look properly in the caves but they were overrun with tourists so we walked to the far end of the beach and enjoyed a bit more solitude. The crashing waves and seabirds on the cliff gave it all a great atmosphere. I will remember this beach for a long time, just slightly spoiled by silly girls with selfie sticks .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The cliff formations are outstanding.  I was on a tour and the parking lot was jammed. There are lots of warnings about the current. The cliffs look like sheered off lava and are amazing. I loved it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Went to see cliff formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went to look at the cliffs and wasn’t disappointed. The black sand is unusual but not surprising and the deadly waves didn’t look so bad. Definitely swam in worse at home. Surprisingly busy even at the early part of the day but pretty good if you wait for the idiots climbing on the cliffs to shift. Sea birds a bit limited in the autumn but not a shock either. Hexagonal shapes in the cliffs very interesting. That’s what I went to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach with lots of scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the first blach sand beach I saw. It is beautiful especially when was used to looking at white sand beaches. The beach is covered with sand and instead of sea shells on the beach there are black smooth rocks all over it. You can see cool rock formations in the water and the Dyrholaey in the distance. There is a cave that you can walk in and take pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning.  Breathtaking.  Majestic.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As we walked along the black-sand beach towards the spires, the huge waves were crashing, and the opportunities for photographs with several of my lenses were endless!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We saw Reynisfjara Beach on two different days......coming into Vik October 3rd on a blustery rainy afternoon and headed back to Reykjavik two days later on a bright sunny warmish day.  First visit was dramatic with the wind swept surf and second visit felt peaceful and calm. The basalt columns on the cliff face are something to be seen and a great photo op .   However, heed the warnings to keep far back from the water due to sneaker waves.  It is a spectacular spot, not to be missed.  There is a cafe there, but we didn't go in. It's a hop, skip and a jump  outside Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Majestic Experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most striking views I witnessed in Iceland.  As you gaze at the basalt columns while the icy wind is whipping around you, and hear the deafening crash of the waves beating against the black sand beaches, you will behold a truly majestic experience. Be careful, the waves are treacherous and it is very cold. Was also happy to learn that this was Eastwatch by the Sea in a few episodes in season 7 of Game of Thrones.  There are various views of this beach around the Vik area and each one is simply stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Other worldly place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach truly makes you feel like you’re on another planet and it’s no wonder so many films use this location for inspiration. Being able to watch the brilliantly ice blue waves crashing on the shores of the black sand is an experience I will never forget. This was a pretty easy drive along the coast to get to since the weather was working in our favor that day. Convenient parking lot and cafe located right along the beach. If you don’t feel like making the drive yourself, there are tours from Reykjavík that will take you there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, but crowded.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hard to get the picturesque views of the rocks in the back due to the many other people here.  But totally worth the stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Group tour.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unbelievable beach. A must see if your in Iceland. Bring warm wind proof jackets and warm coats. North Atlantic blows cold and strong here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth the trip. Beautiful beach with black sand, ocean view and interesting rock formations. During our trip in october it was very windy. But it made it feel even more magnificent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just as incredible as expected but be aware of the waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's quite something, to see your first black beach, with a looming cave and basalt columns. My tour guide stressed that it was very, very important to never have the water behind you, and I got to see first hand why. The freezing wind was howling the day I visited the beach and the waves were high and mighty, crashing upon the black sand. What was particularly astounding about the waves were how fast they lapped at the beach, and how far the waves would rise up the shore. There are warning signs as you descend the beach to be careful of the waves and not to get too close to the water, and it's important that the signs are taken seriously. The black sand is very very soft; as water runs through the sand, your footing is very precarious at best. A few tourists have lost their lives here as a result of being dragged into the sea; moral of the story is- enjoy the view of this spectacular beach don't flirt with the water!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Different and intriguing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an unworldly place.  The surf is up with pounding, dangerous waves, the beach is all black with shiny diamond-like sparkles, and the pencil-like black columns of lava rock have to be seen to be believed.  Then add the driving wind and numbing chill, which can be only lessened by standing next to a blocking column, you have a place to remember forever.It is a strange feeling to want to leave and yet want to stay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see in South Iceland easy access beautiful views and great little sandwich shop with top line coffees (Kaffi)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very cool to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This black sand beach and basalt columns are great photo opportunities. Some weird things wash up on the beach . See my pics. They also have a little place to eat here if your hungry. The parking lot is not big enough for all the traffic, and there is no fees here either.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What everyone has said about the crowds is true. So if you go knowing that, it's not so bad. We went during low tide, so the waves weren't as bad, though we were still careful. The cave and basalt columns were crowded when we first got there. However, the crowd thinned and we were able to get some great pics, walk the beach to the rock formations and truly enjoy the view. It really is amazing and the black sand beach was stunning. Definitely go, just be prepared for the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like no other beach I’ve seen!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is quite touristy but it’s definitely worth a visit. The beach has black sand and incredibly powerful waves. But it’s the rock formations that are truly amazing. The basalt columns are so beautiful and just around from that is a wonderful cave with these stunning rock formations.  Definitely not to be missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Eerily Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow! Incredible beach with so much to see! The rock formations and caves are impressive, as is the beach itself - the waves are so powerful! Make sure you walk to the end of the beach and climb over the rocks to go to the next beach over....you'll get a completely different view of the rocks in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was one of the sites on our 9-day trip that totally blew me away. The power of the waves, and the beauty of the rocks was amazing. This was one of the more crowded sites, but absolutely worth the stop. Walk all the way down to the curve in the rocks for less crowds. Free to park, paid WC.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lot of people complain that this spot has gotten too touristy, but I  think it is worth the stop. The basalt columns, black sand, Hidden caves and amazing landscape make putting up with the crowds worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing black beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful. The basalt columns are really cool and the little cave is fun to stand in and admire. The waves are beautiful but strong so don’t get too close. Beautiful scenery especially in the evening close to sunset. Stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Rock Formation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So much to experience in this one area; black sand beach, sea stacks, dark basalt columns and a stunning sea cave. Very popular tourist stop making it difficult to get pictures with no one in them.Rogue waves are common. Its hard to imagine that the next landfall south of this point is the Antartica. That's a lot of ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beach with black rocks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with black sand. Many tourists. Parking place is attached to the site. In late afternoon you can get some pretty nice photo shots. Not a must see if you are running out of time, as there are other black beaches on the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What You See Only in Television
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black sand beach? How would it look like?? Was curious before stepping in the zone and after that it was just amazing. They say it’s a dangerous place during high tide since the water enters the land to few hundred meters. So a proper tour guide is a must. We went by the day trip provided by Viator which is really convenient. Once in a life time visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful at sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: very picturesque with several unique rock formations and caves.  Going at sunset gives some beautiful photos.  Be careful of the sneaker waves which can soak you, or throw you off balance. Moderately busy but not as crowded as some places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!! But stay awares
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My favorite beach in Iceland, out of all that we visited!! I will return to south Iceland and visit this area again for sure.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold place with magical atmosphere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you visit this cold island it's good to see its southern point with this black beach. It is a windy point with special atmosphere but interesting to see it. It's advisable to take a good quality raincoat and good shoes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Basalt columns stair step here.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While this is the same as the black sand beach the sands here are some of the most unique I have ever encountered. Unlike fine sands these here are more coarse, almost like cat litter. While here we marveled at the basalt columns and climbed around for a time while watching the sun rise ever higher in the sky from morning. While searching the sea for some time we even caught sight of some kind of whale, which made the trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Implausible Experience..!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Undoubtedly the best sight to view in Iceland. Black Sand Beach with incredible basalt.It was raining the day we visited the beach, we hung out for a while in car for the rain to stop. To our shock the sky cleared in matter of 5 minutes. From the parking lot it is about 300 meters walk. Disappointed at first since the first section is swamped by people,  but we managed to find our little joy in finding places to photograph. Moments later we walked further to Reynisfjara Beach there were far less number of people which gave us time to absorb the beauty this place has to offer. Basalt, caves, black sand, tiny smooth black pebbles, gashing waves and the froth that waves was leaving every time it hit the sand...everything was a wonder in itself. And then you start to photograph the beach and one cant get enough of it. It rained again and this time we took shelter in the cave, which was a sight in itself. Towards the end of the beach one can just take a deep breath looking at the waves hitting the rocks and you know how the shapes are formed. We had such an incredible time at the beach and all the memories are just floating in front of the eyes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous view with Basaltic structure on a black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Truly mesmerising. Really loved the place in spite of being crowded. But as you pass the cave with unusual 3D effect structure ... and walk towards the basaltic formations there is less people and the view gets very dramatic ... with waves splashing across rocks and sand. Great opportunity for photographers.The access is very easy , free parking, restaurant and bar nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black sand beaches are rare to begin with, but one with such beautiful features of sea stacks, cliffs, caves, oh my!  Much worth a quick stop on a clear day when you can see it all and pause to enjoy it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing basalt and black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not as stunning as the basalts of the “Giants Causeway” in Northern Ireland but they are still a sight to see. Beware of the traffic camera on the road in to the park. There is a restaurant here as well to grab a bite to eat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love visiting Reynisfjara! Even though it was overcast and misty-- nature has a way of being stunning in any condition. The black sand beach and caves were a wonder. I could have easily spent the day here walking along the shore. Just beautiful. Even with the large number of tourists, you can find places and time where you can experience a peaceful sense of awe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like in Game of Thrones!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went there early in the morning to be less crowded, and it was worth it! The view is spectacular, and when you get closer to those rocks, you can watch the incredible wildlife of Icelandic birds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique beach experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with black sand , interesting geological structures, picturesque  views for photos!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Superb rock structures, great views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is free parking close to the beach. After a short walk across black sand will get you arrive at some dramatic basalt rock formations which in places seem to defy gravity and a short walk past this is a cave which presents a weird 3D effect and great for photos. A little further on still and you arrive at some dramatic cliffs. Look out to sea for incredible sea stacks also caused by volcanic activity with views all the way to the Dyrholaey promontory.The place does get quite busy with tourists but is much quieter the further down the beach you walk and for dramatic views, it is a must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: If you hadn't seen basalt columns yet, stop here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can see basalt columns all over Iceland, but they have some of the best ones here.  You can walk on the beach right next to them.  The black sand beach is so pretty.  Bring a small bag with you and take some home.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Where can you see a glacier driving in, green pastures with grazing sheep, a black beach, Atlantic Ocean ALL in one place?  Here!  A great drive into this beach.  We arrived at sundown, and it was awesome!  Lighting is fabulous for photos (reddish-golden hues) that make the water, and black basaltic columns really pop!  We even got a rainbow by the two rock islands.  It was not crowded so very nice.  Go toward sundown for good lighting and photo ops!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing but be prepared for a crowd
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is like no other I've ever been. The rock formations are stunning. The white sea spray against the black sand is otherworldly. It's just breathtaking. The only thing that bothered me was the CROWD! My husband and I went at about 6-7 p.m. on a Sunday and it was very crowded. Most of the people seemed to be just tourists like us but then there were also weirdos like girls in prom dresses (literally) preening and trying to get the perfect Instagram photos. It ruined some of the atmosphere and provided a decent distraction. But it was still an amazing place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This place is awesome as part of our South Coast Day tour - Got to see a bunch of Puffin birds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was an excellent stop as part of our South Coast Day tour.  We got a little bit of everything on the weather side, heavy rain, sunshine, sprinkles, high winds in the short period of time we were there.  The black sand is pretty cool and easy to walk on.  The surf was interesting to watch, sometimes the surf came in towards you while walking.  We also got see a bunch of Puffin birds in their nest above the caves and flying around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very neat black sands Beach with rock formations and caves.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one place that was a must on my travel to Iceland. It was an overcast day but the Black sand was made up of small black and red Lava rocks.  The ocean was quite rough which made it even more beautiful.  There were 2 rock formations, Dyrholaey and Reynisdrangar and 2 caves.  There were also beautiful basalt Columns.  This is the Atlantic ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing black sand beach and incredible / unusual rock formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara Beach is another "must see" on your drive around Iceland - it is only a 5 minute or so drive from The Dyrholaey Nature Reserve.  The walk along the beach is incredible, but take notice of the warning about rogue waves - they truly do come out of nowhere.  We saw one man getting totally drenched with no warning at all that a large wave was coming, so walk a "safe" distance away from the water.  The rock formations are unbelievable to see in person.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Watch out for Sneaker Waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: At Reynisfjara beach, we were warned of sneaker waves - and how these deadly waves have claimed the lives of tourists at Iceland's most dangerous beach.  This is a black sand beach backed by stacks of basalt columns at the foot of the mountain Reynisfjall.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful quick stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful black sand beach with some great rock features! Beautiful views and a quick stop unless you want to spend a long time taking photos. I would not miss this stop if you are in Vik, as the black sand is unique and the views are good. It does get busy, like most sights in Iceland. We saw some sneaker waves coming up that nearly caught people - be careful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Parking was right at the beach, this place had so many interesting things including the black sand, to the basalt columns that my teenagers climbed, to the cave, puffin nesting and diving in for fish, which I hear are there only until the end of August so we were lucky to see them at the end of August when we were there. I brought home some of the flat rocks that are all over this beach. Perfect for photographers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beach with ton of tourist
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a quite interesting site with rock and cliff formation on the beach. parking is close by but you want to walk on the beach to enjoy the beauty. Even there is a warning to stay away and careful about sudden waves, some people did not pay must attention. Just stay safe and enjoy this beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Once upon a time ranked amongst the most beautiful nontropical beaches this site has beauty worth beholding. It has an amazing basalt rock formation in stacks. It has thousands of nesting sea birds seen along the formation. Amazing rock structure also can be visualised from the shore. It is easily accessible and a great photo stop

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Possibly the most incredible beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Simply amazing beach. Free parking right next to the beach. This really is black sand beach. It is unbelievably black. As soon as you get to the beach there are a lot of amazing hexagon columns, right next to them is another cave with a completely different rock formation. Then further along the beach there were more different rock formations. At the end of the beach there were some big rocks at the edge of the water. There were also a lot of nesting puffins above the rock formations. And to make the beach even more special you can see the rock formations of Dyrhólaey in the distance. This is an essential visit. The first bit of the beach was very busy and there were people all along it so if you want a secluded beach this isn’t the one for you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The highlight of Vik
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara Beach is a must-see when visiting the Vik area. The black sand beach is beautiful and unique. You do need to stay away from the water as the waves are unpredictable and dangerous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very interesting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black sand, rock formations i.e. columns and cave are amazing. Free parking nearby. Many people but it is possible to take some good photos. Time to spend: 30 min

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with lovely views of the rock formations - different from the black beaches nearby but still worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the Black Beach area. The waves are mesmerizing and the power of these waves incredible. Be careful of the waves. If the tide is low you can go further down the beach which is safe but make sure the tide is not coming in.  The waves come fast so you can get soaked if you are not careful. Lots of puffins in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Beautiful, Very Crowded.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you make the trek to Iceland and opt to leave Reykjavik (which you definitely should), you might as well stop here at this beach. It's very pretty with it's rock formations and black sand, but in my opinion, there are more beautiful places in Iceland and this one is so overcrowded with tourists taking photos. I came during semi-off season in September, and the beach was by far the most crowded place we visited including places in Reykjavik. You could not get a picture without someone else in it. If you drive out to see it, make sure to also stop at Gulfoss, Skogafoss, and Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Puffins & beautiful basalt columns
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one place in Iceland that I would consider a must-see.  The beach is beautiful.  The basalt formations are stunning.  And, during the summer months it is a great place to see puffins.  The beach is made up of larger black stones instead of sand.  It takes a bit of an effort to walk across, but it is worth the time.  You may recognize the location from movies or shows such as Game of Thrones.  They were filming something while we were there, but I'm not sure what it was.  Beware of the sneaker waves that can catch you off guard & take you out to sea.  I would give myself at least an hour to explore this area.  Honestly, I could spend most of an afternoon here enjoying the setting.  There is a small restaurant & bathroom on site too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most amazing black sand beach. To one side are the fascinating geometric basalt columns, together with a large cave which provided welcome shelter on a very wet and windy day; on the other side is the ocean, complete with atmospheric rock stacks but beware - at the entrance to the beach there are rather sobering signs which highlight the danger of the 'sneaker' waves and the fact that several tourists have lost their lives here being caught unawares and washed out to sea. You need to avoid being distracted by the beauty of the place (which is very easy) and not keeping an eye on the shore line. We loved it here - a photographer's paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Different
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I will use that word to describe this black sand beaches, but not too appealing to me for an special visit. If in the are do it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a great experience! This black sand beach is epic—I really found it beautiful and captivating!  The black stones at the water’s edge are incredible. Free parking-but pay toilets-ugh.  Bring your camera!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beach, puffins, great views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black beach is .... well black of course, it also has a number of caves and square profile forms of basalt in the side of the cliff, formed from when soft lava rock has been worn away. There is a perch above where loads of puffins are flying in and out (save teh cost of a puffin watching expedition). This is not a bathing beach due to the waves (sneakers) being very dangerous, it is also very windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved it here. It's a definite must see in Iceland. The cave is breathtaking and the columns are fantastic. The beach itself is just the most magical place. Walk along to the end if you visit. Handy tip - get here early especially if you want photos. I was on this beach for about 2 hours, I loved it so much but after 12, there are coach loads of tourists and getting a picture without a shiny yellow jacket in it will be a challenge.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique and worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is such a cool thing to see. I had been to the black sand beach in Santorini and it was ok, but this one was amazing. It really has black sand along with some black rocks in sections. And the rock formation lining the back of the beach is unique and cool to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The closest you can gget to view the fantastic crystalite basalt columns.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is like a surprise package. Where you park your vehicle, there is noting visible except a mound and the beach. When you finally get around, the basalt columns show up and then its a show window of the most amazing formations of rock. There is a beautiful cave which has these formations allover the surfaces, like Gaudi's architecture. No surface is plain. A beautiful array of textures and grey tones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great view of the ocean and the rock formations. Parking was reasonable and there was plenty of space on the beach to walk around. A cool experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breezy beach with great sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very cold and breezy but it was March.Good to see and got some great sunset photos.Basalt columns but maybe Ireland does them better.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You won’t see anything like this at home
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What nature or whoever sculpts this stuff had done to the black basalt is like nothing we had seen. There’s the tormented spires that stymie understanding of just how they got built. And not far distant it turns into walls of basalt blocks neatly stacked until suddenly their direction turns and they go into swirls – as though some giant child you really don’t want to meet got tired of orderliness and decided to introduce a wholly new pattern. We were there on a rainy day but there were still fulmars adding some recognizable life to a grotesquely beautiful landscape. I was a dandy walk even in the rain.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Black Sand Beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here to see the black sand beach and basalt columns.  This is a beautiful place (and a Game of Thrones filming location).  Very dangerous surf so keep back from the waves when visiting.  Fun to climb up on a column and take some pics!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Strangely enough, Reynisfjara Beach in the Katla Geological Park, about 25 km west of Vik, reminded me of Hac Sa Beach in Coloane Island, Macau, except that Reynisfjara Beach is better kept..... The beach is of black sand and stones, which reminds you of the volcanic activity in the area and the proximity of Mount Katla... There are also geological rock formations that remind me of Hong Kong Geopark outside Sai Kung... and this beach is a good place to watch puffins, which must nest in the cliffs above the beach...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must see off the Ring Road in the south of Iceland, just about 20 minutes west of Vik. You can actually walk on the Black sand beach, with towering basalt columns next to you. You can even climb up and sit on a few of the pieces of basalt for a great photo opportunity. There are spectacular and interesting rock formations out in the water, but be aware that the crashing waves are very strong, so it’s recommended to stay a good distance from the shoreline. There are some small caves around as well, and in season apparently puffins frequently fly around here. My husband and I went on our honeymoon in September, so we were a little bit late for puffin viewing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Stone Beach, Rock Structures, & Puffins
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black Sand Beach is listed as #1 in Vik for attractions, and this is the same place. It is more of black stone beach varying in all sizes, although there is some black sand as well. The waves here were quite strong so watching them crash onto shore as well as onto the large rocks farther down the beach was fascinating. You have some unique rock structures out in the water, basalt columns (like the Giants Causeway in Northern Ireland), and some jagged caves. All along the cliffs, there are puffins who swoop out over the beach to the water and back. We probably spent an hour here walking down the beach and looking at the puffins. I'd recommend a rain jacket here as Vik receives ~85" of rain per year. There is a cafe with sandwiches, drinks, and snacks as well as restrooms you can pay to use if you aren't buying anything. Vik is also 15 minutes east with a large store, restaurant, cafe, gas station, etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Your hair stands up!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the places I went and will forever be kept in my memory as a dark, creepy, dramatic place! All we heard was the sound of strong waves crushing. The way that the waves were building up in slow motion was unbelievable. You cannot miss this experience!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!! But watch out for sneaker waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You don’t want to miss the basalt columns on Reynisfjara beach. This can be a quick stop if you’re doing a day trip. However, keep in mind that this is a place to look at rocks, not a place to sit on a beach. There is a multitude of signs warning about sneaker waves, which can come up out of nowhere and catch you unaware, pulling you out into a rip tide. Don’t mess around with the ocean here—but DO go look at it an enjoy the incredible scenery. Also, while we were there the weather changed from sunny/blue skies to impenetrable fog in about 90 seconds. It was startling, but beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Eerie, beautiful and unforgettable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must see.  Great place to unwind on a summer day. The cave-like structures create great photogenic moments in the Evening or morning sun.  By the way: one wouldn't expect a beach that is not made for sun bathing to be a good place for people watching, but this one certainly is.  There are always people who want to be seen no matter weather, location, etc. etc...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun black sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great spot for small kids. Can be windy and cold. Restaurant is located near by. Pictures are also great here with rocks to climb and carved out sides of the mountain.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a beautiful sight!  The black beach was an incredible place to visit!  The basalt columns were very cool as well!  I am planning on returning this trip to enjoy again!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Columnar basalt, caves and pinnacles.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Columnar basalt towers out of the beach forming a huge cave in a church like arch. Just off the beach there are 2 pinnacles of rock. I was lucky to see a whale blow and broach just off shore. Great shore landscape and very beautiful in sun. Car park takes you quite close.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning.This is a must go while visiting Iceland.black sand beach,basalt columns,rocks formation.Is windy and a little crowded but you will enjoy the real nature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful site but oh so crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As other reviewers say, this is a beautiful site and mother nature at its best. What bothered us is how the tourists are climbing all over the beautiful structures to get pictures of themselves sitting on the rock formations. Isn't it enough to just photograph the beauty? You really need to climb up on it? It was impossible to get a photo without other people in your photo so I had to step back very far away to capture this image. Parking in this area was very difficult. There are other beaches in this area that are easier to access, and a hike above will give you fantastic views!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing structures!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you visit Iceland, make sure this is one of your stops! It was so neat to see the basalt columns and the different directions the lava flowed at different times. Stunning!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the highlight of our trip to Vik.  The black sand beach, the puffins, other sea birds complimented by rock formations that are truly a marvel make this a worthwhile drive from Reykjavik.  The beach is split by the rocks so make sure exit to the black beach side that is prior to arriving in the town of Vik.  The wind was strong the day we visited, dress appropriately and realize conditions can change quite rapidly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A stop is it worth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had this stop on our tour across the ring road and it was amazing, I can’t tell you how awesome the Mother Earth in Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: one of my favorite destination spot.Such natural beauty and no park fees to enter.must see during summer.the sand in the beach is so different and texture is something my kids loved.awesome pic opportunities.during summer its breath taking

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another worthy stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is another good stop along the road.  Beautiful black beach with sea stacks out in the water.  Great photo ops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolute must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach would be amazing early or late with less tourists but even crowded with tourists it was amazing.  Between the basalt columns and black sand, it was spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite place in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved the black sand, vestiges of rock, the fantastic caves, and watching the puffins flying in and out.  Worth the trip!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go early or late
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The experience at 7am was so much nicer than at 7pm, when there were multiple busloads of people, all trying to take a picture with the caves or the basalt columns (while not heeding any of the warnings about sneaker waves). It is beautiful, and more so when relatively empty :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: (Black sand beach) Nice to walk around
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is easily accessible. Lots of tourists. The sand is nice and it's a nice walk up and down the beach. There is a cave and cliffs - a very popular photo op. There is a restaurant onsite with bathrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful geology
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gotta love nature. Great basalt columns. Wonderful rocks jutting up from the sea near the shore. Easy walk from the car park. No cost.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So pretty.  This beach is popular but you can walk and be by yourself.  The sand is clean, the ocean very dangerous (so no swimming) but very, very picturesque.  A must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beatiful but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ok let's start saying that the place is fantastic. The beach is black made of sand/pebbles. The rocks fantastic and on the horizon a great natural arch.The but it's only that it is so popular that there were too many buses.But the beach deserves a toir from the ring road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A tourist hot spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A popular tourist hotspot, and for good reason. The geography is drastic and stunning. About a 2.5 hour drive from Reykjavik, we arrived at the beaches at about 5:30 pm in the evening, and the beaches were still swarmed with tourists. We spent about an hour here, and we didn't even walk the full length of the beach. You could easily spend ~3 hours here if you wanted to explore. There is parking, and there is a visitor centre/cafe/restrooms on site (restrooms either cost money or are free if you purchase something at the cafe). Obey signs to be careful around the water; sneaker waves (wave that are disproportionately large in size and sneak up on you) have sucked several tourists out to sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful... but busy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach itself is an amazing wonder of the world! Huge waves hit the black sand and striking cliffs. It is truly a place to see while in Iceland! Which is why it seemed half of the tourists population was there... if you walk further down the beach away from everyone you may get a moment of solitude! We climbed over one of the rock walls (carefully!) and were alone on a side. Even saw some puffins flying around!! My only complaint was that the bathrooms cost 200 krona :(

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another Awe Inspiring Icelandic site!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Part of an over ten hour tour of the south coast. After seeing pictures of this online my visit to Iceland would not have been complete without going here. Absolutely beautiful. The volcanic formed basalt columns, sharp rising cliff, black sand beach-all amazing. Pay attention to the warning signs at the beginning-this is a beautiful but dangerous beach if you do not pay attention to the guidelines. There is a small cafe and gift shop on site, but I preferred spending the time here on the beach. If you go to the town of Vik you will be able to get a better view of the three trolls formation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Basalt and beach and islands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome basalt rock formations on side of mountain.  Can wonder aimlessly on this wonderful beach.  Ver cool rock formations in ocean.  Too many tourists... ruins photos

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice walk on the coast with spectacular rock formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ample parking, even though it's a fairly large tourist site.  Pebble rocks mostly to walk on, however, if you get closer to the water you can enjoy some sand.  Super cool rock features and short walk to reach the end.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach along the coast in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I came here as part of a day-trip with other tourists, we stopped by this beach and I walked along it, also towards the rock formation part. It is very nice, but very cold, much different to the sandy, hot beaches in Australia where I am from. Still, it is a landmark tourists should visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach and rock formation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another beautiful spot in Iceland which one must visit and admire the beauty. But be mindful of mass tourism.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No one walks the Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is another crowded tourist spot with tons of ppl taking pictures of rock formations. No one was exploring the rest of the beach. My husband and I took the opportunity to walk the length of the beach with our baby in solitude, it was quite lovely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An absolute must visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing scenery.  Yes there are alot of tourists but with good reason.The black sand beach is cool, but it's the basalt rock formation that's the real star, it was incredible, and climbable (which my kids loved, including my 18 year old who is usually too cool for stuff like that).  Interesting caves, birds nesting in the crevices including puffins (although to be honest more gulls than puffins).  Less than 10 minutes off the main road so very easy to get to, if you are in the area you absolutely must stop and see it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped at the beach as part of our Southern Tour. The beach has beautiful black and (or whatever it is that you are walking on). Nice caves too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is surreal with coal black sand and towering cliffs comprised of rectangular rock formations. Wear your hiking boots!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand and basalt columns all in one!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was so cool! We saw black pebble sand and basalt columns on this beach. This is also where we saw puffins hanging out on the cliffs!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourist beach, but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A friend and I spent some time at Reynisfjara Beach while staying in Vik. The locals refer to it as the beach for the tourists, so expect a crowded parking lot and beach, but it is definitely worth a stop... especially since there is not much to do in Vik. We would recommend coming at off times to avoid heavier crowds. The beach is unique with the black sand and rock formations. There are some caves and some rock formations that tourists can climb on to take pictures. There are crashing waves, and signs warn people from swimming as it can be dangerous. It is most beautiful on a clear summer day, when you can relax on the sand and feel the sun beaming on you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Trolls turned to rock
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were lucky to have a beautiful sunny day for this amazing place.  The black beaches, basalt columns caves and of course Reynisdrangar (the big rocks), the story goes that there were three trolls who were trying to pull a boat ashore.  When the sun came up they were turned to stone.  Free parking with a wee restraint (toilets).  My children aged 10 & 11 really enjoyed this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place in an amazing town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Vik is not to be missed...one of our fave stops in all of Iceland. The variety of black sands and rock formations in this area are amazing, and bird life is plentiful and easy to view if you have binos or a scope. Take your time and try to avoid the crowds--midnight sun was great for us. I definitely want to spend more time in this area, and on this beach, on future visits.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful view of rock structures and beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a wonderful beach with amazing topography. It's worth a stop on your trip through Vik to see the rectangular columns that line the beach. You might catch a glimpse of a puffin as you are in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 7 years ago we tried visiting this beach but couldn’t because it was puffin nesting season (late May, early June). This year we were able to visit in late June and it was worth it! We went about 9 pm and it had quite a few tourists. I definitely recommend going at odd hours if possible to avoid the busses. It was just a fun place to explore, take photos, enjoy nature, look for cool rocks, and watch for Puffins up high on the rocks. A must-see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the crowded parking lot! Walk away from the crowds for better perspective - and bring gloves. Did not eat here there is food, WCs, and picnic tables.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We absolutely loved our time at this beach.  We were able to spot puffins and walk around to take pictures.  As Game of Thrones fan, it was fun to see where some scenes have been shot.  We also ate a late dinner at the restaurant on the beach - great fish/chips!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Volcanic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Same Review for the Black Sand Beach.Practice saying the name!Come early or after 5pm to avoid tourist buses and walk the whole beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Photos of a Unique Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been disappointed visiting black sand beaches in other parts of the world, but this one was large and wide and actually sandy!  There are unique geologic views in all directions and I took so many pictures hoping to capture the beauty of this diverse place.  If you head west on the ring road and take the turnoff to the lighthouse area (but do not go up the steep dirt road), you can see this beach from a distance and you get a whole new perspective on the beach area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Totally different from everthing I have ever seen! The landscape is absolutely amazing and wowing! There is free parking and a visitor centre with foods and drinks!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brace yourself for daytime crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We first arrived in the late afternoon but couldn’t even get into the car park for all the tour busses. We came again in the late evening (after 9pm) and it was still crowded but at least there was space to park. The amazing basalt cliffs are so worth seeing that it’s worth the struggle to take a selfie without hundreds of other tourists in the shot. You’ll need a minimum of 30 minutes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unlike Any Other Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quite the natural wonder with the black sand (more like small pebbles), jagged rocky outcrops, and basalt columns.I would recommend going off hours as this spot is crawling with tourists and you likely won't get a nice pic of the sea stacks because everyone is climbing all over them. Regardless, you need to check it out!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very special place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is like no other beach I have seen. Black sand with tons of nice rocks. The surrounding mountain is just spectacular. Be careful with the waves though, don't go too close. Now and then someone had to run towards the inner side of the beach not to get wet.Free parking close by.A must visit if you are in the area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just simply beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The scenery is unbelievable.  Lots of tourists, but it's a must seen.  The road getting there is also beautiful.  The waves are dangerous, so don't come too close to the water because it'll pull you out to sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular, Unique scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand/pebbles, the trippy basalt columns, the dramatic seascape with the two iconic pillars rising out of the ocean..just really incredible. Cafe serves good food/coffee/hot chocolate too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Viking Ship
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Can't miss it from the Black Sand Beech.  It truly looks like a Viking Ship.  It's only 3 minutes off the Main Road so don't miss it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for a walk after dinner and happened upon this amazing beach! Just about had it all to ourselves. The scenery is spectacular. It was so different from our earlier experience at Dyrholaey which was super crowded. Maybe it was the time of day but we felt very fortunate to have discovered this hidden gem.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic rock formations along the coastline
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand beach with huge outcroppings in the water, and some amazing rock formations along the beach itself. Great backdrops for photos, but beware the power and reach of the waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iceland’s own Giant Causeway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous long stretch of black sand with stunning cliff face and piped display of hexagonal rock columns. Extremely photogenic, don’t miss. 10 minutes from Vik. Facilities available.Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice, but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a picturesque black sand beach, close to Vik.  There is a parking lot, and a cafe.  There is also pay WCs.It’s worth a quick stop to snap some pictures, but good luck getting ones without people in them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to see nature at its best!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This spot is another one of Iceland's don't miss stops. It has many natural wonders, the basalt columns of the cliff, the immense waves breaking on the black stone beach, the puffins all show the power of nature. Listen to the signs regarding the waves - could easily see someone getting in trouble at high tide if trapped in the area just past the columns.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my favorite days in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I visited Iceland for an extended weekend and one of the days, we rented a car and drove to Vik.  We stopped off at a couple of waterfalls the were absolutely beautiful but my favorite experience of that day was Reynisfjara Beach.  It reminded me of a trip to the Grand Canyon, pictures can't capture what is so special about this place. (Even though I will include some!)  The basalt cliffs are just so massive and just rise straight up from the beach.  The beach isn't sand but tiny black pebbles that have been worn down over the millennia. Don't just stay in Reykjavik.  Get out and see Reynisfjara Beach and the sights along the way.  You will be so happy you did!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not your average beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is definitely not your average everyday go-to beach. Not only is the color of the sand black instead of yellow, it is also Iceland’s most dangerous beach, due to its unforeseen gigantic waves. Although this beach and it’s scenery is to be enjoyed with caution, the stone carvings in the cliffs which the waves have created over the decades are definitely worth it. We really enjoyed ourselves, and if you’re nearby, a stop here is worthwhile!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I love this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This really is not your typical beach. From my understanding you will not be able to swim here because of the sneaker waves.  The waves were very large and fun to watch break into the shore.  They also have the basalt columns to climb on which is fun.  The basalt columns are pretty darn cool to see.  The landscape is beautiful around the beach.  It is definitely worth a stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Who doesn't love a black sand beach? Beautiful rock formations, crashing waves, and birds all around.  A great place to stop and site see if you are in the Vik area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We liked it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited at 23:00 in June.  Plenty of light and people.  Amazing geologic formations.  Did not hike to the top of the hill - did not realize until the next day the trail head is on the other side of the mountain, in Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MORE FOR THE COLOUR THAN ANYTHING ELSE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a bit miserable when we toured the area, not seeing it at its best. Apart from the black colour of the sand, the basalt formations behind the beach were as photographic. The chance to see the 'stacks' our in the waters was also good

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty place even spotted a puffin
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The rocks in the water are pretty cool. Don’t go in the morning it’s covered with your buses. We stayed at the black beach suites so we were able to go back in the evening. The rocks are nice as well. We even spotted a puffin. The only puffin we saw during our 5 days in Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definite "Must See" (watch for rogue waves)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very impressive with a "Game of Thrones" vibe. Gorgeous scenary with a resteraunt on site. WC=bathroom (200ISK). Excellent way to spend the day. Not safe for swimming. Limited access for wheelchair/strollers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Black Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning views. Black cliffs. Rough waves. I’m pretty sure that in an episode of the Vikings History Channel series, Floki landed on this very beach when he reached Iceland. We came here on a tour, so we had limited time, but I wish we could have spent more. The basalt columns, caves, and maybe - if you’re lucky - a puffin. This location is iconic to Iceland. How could one not visit?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the time to stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara beach is worth the time for a stop while on the Ring road near Vik. Wonderful black beach and basalt columns and caves. Beach is really black pebbles not sand which is kind of neat. Will be crowed with tourists in the summer. Walk away from the area closest the parking lot and you can somewhat get away from the crowd. Come late or early in the day for less of a crowd. Huge waves are fun to watch, but do not try to wade or swim here, as waves can knock you down. Enjoy the area

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blew me away
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is black sand beach. Stunning! Do this with Dyrhólaey Rocks, because it’s close by. Amazing place, and yes, the waves really can get big and eat one up 😱

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's Iceland, not Hawaii...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely worth a visit. Black volcanic sand beach, basalt columns and caves, and of course the sea. It's a windy place so be prepared. There's not much of a town but it's about the scenery. It's the southern route so it's a long drive, but scenic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A magical beach .....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an amazing beach with beautiful black sand,  basalt block on the caves where all the tourists stand and incredible rock formations spitting out of the sea. The key is to walk away from the tourists to enjoy some incredible photo shoots opportunity. We walked the beach and given that the tourists tend to be on a tight schedule, we had the beach to ourselves. The waves can be dangerous so follow the warning signs. There is also a restaurant with bathrooms if needed and there is a lot of parking. Try morning or late afternoon to avoid the load of buses full of tourists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Greta basalt columns at the beach & beautiful black sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Big free car park with a toilet, cafe & snack hut with the famous Icelandic Plysur (hot dog)The basalt columns down to the black sand are amazing but congested with people taking selfies! The sea crashes into the black sand & pebbles & you have a great view to the sea stacks.Visit early morning or late evening to avoid the crowds

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful and spectacular beach with black sand, basalt rocks and spectacular rock formations.The beach can be dangerous, because of the waves that can swollow you and take you to the sea. At least 5 warning signs tells you that on the way from the parking to the beach.As in many of the biggest attractions in Iceland, it is difficult to take pictures without having a lot of people in it. But it would be unfair to call it crowdy, because the beach is so big.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the "must sees" of Iceland.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning rock formations. It is worth to take your time and explore the area, especially in the direction to the Vik. Time it correctly and watch out the deadly sneaker waves!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must go! Great scenery and hexagonal rock formations!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach with black sands and great scenery and the hexagonal rock formations was amazing! Quite unforgettable scenes from there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful place on Earth!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I am in love with this place! I didn't expect it is so beautiful - the mysterious atmosphere, huge waves, black sand, specific caves and stones - everything sums up to a beautiful experience. Have a walk and look on the ground - the sand and little black rocks are amazing. Also, for the Game of Thrones fans - it was featured in some of the episodes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a detour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Impressive place to visit when in the Vik area. I like the black beach and the rock formations - it’s a very impressive place. Need to be wary of the waves ! We went on a grey misty day - very atmospheric !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Volcanic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with caves, rock formations, and really cool basaltic columns.  They say it is a black sand beach, but it is more like gravel.  It did make it a little challenging to walk along the beach.  Columns are totally fun to climb and play around on.  Lots of sea birds to view as well.  There was a cute little restaurant right next to the beach as well for hungry visitors.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: watch out for sneaker waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: it's a beautiful beach, but crowded and too cold to swim. it can also kill you, so maybe young kids should avoid the surf line.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were fortunate to visit this beach on a sunny, almost windless day. Our tour director told us that we probably wouldn't last more than a few minutes on a very windy day. It's difficult to even describe this place and difficult to capture its uniqueness in photographs. The basalt columns, the fine black sand, the ferocity of the ocean all add to the otherworldliness of this place. This beach was also seen in Season 7 of Game of Thrones!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views.  Saw puffins too.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The rock formations are amazing.  The sea is beautiful and the landscape, its volcanos reaching for the sea, make you realize that you have have found a truly remarkable place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No pictures justify the beauty of this place. Go early to avoid the swarming tourists and the best light. Wear comfortable shoes to be able to climb on to the rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular spot; do not miss!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a truely beautiful bit of scenery, what Iceland is all about.Unique is just one adjective to decribe this piece of geography.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool but black beaches are better
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On the bucket list. As cool as well like black beaches. But you should visit it as well. Restrooms available. 200ISk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold but beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth a visit if you're road tripping around Iceland, or are staying in the area.Even though the weather was not great during out 7 day vacation, the 2 days we got to leave the hotel were amazing!!We went in April and it was beyond cold, making being near the beach even worse. The weather was a mix of monsoon and blizzard for most of our trip but when the sky broke, we added Vik onto our Golden Circle Trip.Vik:I will say, although I loved seeing this, I wouldn't make a special trip just to see this with nothing else planned. Vik was 3 hours away from our hotel and made for a very long night. It is so beautiful to see the landscape unfold onto black sands with raging waves; however, there is not much to do in this exact spot. On the way to here though you can stop off and see the fallen aircraft. I forget what it's name is right now.Now, when we went it felt like 10 degrees out so after about 20/25min, we couldn't take the cold anymore. It was piercing and burning your skin. DRESS WARMLY! It's honestly the only advice I can give you. We dressed bundled up and were still frozen because of the time of year and the wind. Having said that, if you go in nicer weather or can withstand cold better than we could, you are not rushed out & can stay for as long as you want. You also do not need to pay to get in to see this which is nice. Because we really only spent 20min here, is it worth a whole special trip just for it? I don't really think so...BUT, if you are seeing other things, then hell yea, go. Its stunning!!Parking:There is parking in walking distance to the beachFood:There are towns nearby from that offer some restaurant choices that you can eat in. We went to one, I cant recall the name, and waited about 30min before being sat. It was a cool little place and the food was good and moderately priced. We were exhausted thought from a long day and left at around 9pm.Bottom Line: Worth the experience if you do other things in this area as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views with beach and basalt columns
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my favorite site visited that day. The beach was made of very fine black sand. We had fun climbing on the columnar basalt formations around Halsanefshellir Cave. The views from the beach to the ocean were great, and crashing waves added to the drama. We had to watch for sneaker waves which are dangerous and have claimed multiple lives at this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Landscape for movies
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have seen volcanic ash beaches elsewhere in the world, but this one combines different elements that make it seem like the ideal movie set landscape. And if you are not a director is still a prime location for photo shooting. You need to drive some 5km from the main road to reach it. Parking is free and there is a cafe on the end of the parking lot. The sand is black and is overshadowed by a cliff some 300m high with basaltic steep rocks, couple of caves and some large rocks on either side of the beach. do not get too close to the water since there are warnings about the sudden waves that might drag you in. 30min should be enough for your photo session.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but packed.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is truly stunning even on a rainy day. Parking is close to the beach access and there’s plenty of it, as well as two food establishments. The only downside was all of the people. It’s a very busy site making for hard to capture photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must-Do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This isn't a place for the kids to run wild. The incoming waves can be dangerous, but not a problem if you don't get too close. The cove and the rock formations are definitely worth the stop. Great photos to be had here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Basalt stacks are a must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came here on our Grayline South Iceland tour and were able to spend about 30-45 minutes here at this beach. I wish we had had more time to explore further down the cliffs and the sand because it was so gorgeous and there were lots of little caves that I wanted to peak my head into. The basalt stacks are the main draw of this beach, and you will feel like you're at Dragonstone if you watch Game of Thrones. The water here at this beach is dangerous with large waves and strong tides so if you're going to go close to the water make sure you're vigilant and careful. I went close and ended up getting soaking wet because I didn't expect the tide to come up as far as it did. Also a great beach to take some sand if you want that as a souvenir (I took a bunch). A very cool beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Smashing beach. Saw puffins here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went at 10am. Cliffs are worth a visit on their own to see the rock formations. Round the basalt rocks the puffins were flying.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An awesome beach with spectacular rock formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one awesome black sand beach with many strange rock formations including the Halsanefshellir Cave, the Basalt Sea Stacks and the Dyrholaey (door hole island) all in one stretch. The wave was powerful so beware and do not get too close to the water. Weather not so clear on my day of visit so everything looked greyish. It must feel much better on a bright clear day. It was quite windy so dress up for the walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Automatic five stars just because I’ve never seen a black beach before. I’m from New Jersey so the beach is nothing new to me but I’ve never seen sand like this. Not only did the sun glisten off the sharp black sand but the waves and rock formations added to the beauty. The sand was so soft and silky. The basalt columns made for a great photo opportunity. When people say be aware of the waves they aren’t kidding. They can be very powerful even when close to the shoreline.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Seriously amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just be prepared for the wind and unpredictable weather occasions. It is extremely dangerous to go near water, so follow the instructions. It looks stunning, you will enjoy every minute spent here! rock formations are unbelievable!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Nature
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning rock formations, an eerie lack of color, winds powerful enough to take your glasses and hat flying, and waves so powerful and humbling-- Reynisfjara Beach was a very unique experience. Do take noted precautions regarding the waves-- the sheer power of each wave is unlike anything I have ever seen. The rock formations are very intricate and it is exciting to be able to get so close as to touch the different textures of each formation. Our stop here felt about 15 degrees F colder than any of our other stops, so I would recommend an extra jacket or layer to stay warm here. Also, be aware there is a fee to use the restroom at this stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Interesting rock formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth a stop, interesting rock formations.  The power of the ocean can really be felt by the breaking waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unlike Anything I've Ever Seen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The rock formations here are spectacular.  While the beach was crowded and windy, it was still quite beautiful.  I was able to get a lot of photos even with all of the people visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great way to see the North Atlantic Ocean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a fun location to spend some time at. The cliffs and rocks were very unique and cool. It was also fun to actually touch the Atlantic ocean at the high latitude, seeing water the temperature was.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Powerful waves (of tourists)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even on a clouded day in May this beach was swarming with people disregarding all danger sign that warned against the waves that have claimed lives before. The power of the waves (even the normal ones) is stunning and the rock formations very special.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So Busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove the ring road clockwise and made this our last stop before Reykjavík. Because it is so close to where a majority of people stay, it was so incredibly crowded, taking away from the beauty. Dozens of photographers lined up along the beach, a music video being recorded and a professional photo shoot all took away from the natural landscape. Still loved the giant waves rolling in and the lava rock columns, but should have waited until after midnight when the crowds die down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Black Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the same as the Black Sand Beach. It is vast, powerful waves crashing into the black sand, stunning columns and an amazing cave. I am so glad to come here. It was one of my highlights on my visit to Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning but better photographed from the beach in Vik
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here on our way to Vik. Breathtakingly beautiful rock formations called Reynisdrangar, but can be better photographed from the beach in Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bucket list! You hav e to visit this Beach if you visit Iceland, 1h 45 m drive from Reykjarvik. Big Waves around 8-10 m hit the bich when we was there. A couples of People get hit of the Waves and get really wet. This Waves are very Dangerous so be careful. The Black Columns and "Troll rocks" is just fantastic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing & dramatic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of our top 3 sights in Iceland. Dramatic and beautiful. Sea cave with basalt stone pillars and a wide beach, but heed the warnings about rogue waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is one of the best beaches I saw while in Iceland. The sand, water, cave, and rock formations in the ocean were spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Basalt Columns and sneaker waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's about a 3 hour drive from Reykjavik, but definitely worth a visit. the columns are visually stunning and you get to check out a very cool cave or two. Be careful of the waves, they really do sneak up on you!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t miss this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has really cool black sand and pebbles as well as geometric basalt rock formations. Just a few minutes west of Vik, the views are great and there are fun rocks to climb and caves to check out. Be careful of the waves, there are warning signs at the entrance but some people still get too close and are surprised by sneaker waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very unique beach that you can't miss
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just down the road from Dyrhólaey, Reynisfjara is the unique black pebble beach with sheer cliffs and geometric basalt columns. Be careful of the powerful tides and waves - people have been dragged out to sea here from not being alert! Parking: Large lot at the base of cafe/gift shopTrail(s): >2-3km walk along beach to end. Smooth black pebble beach is easy to walk along.Traffic: Golden Circle stop - heavy traffic.The smooth pebble beach is comfortable to walk on

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My folks and I really enjoyed visiting this beach. The combination of rocky black sand and blue water is really quite stunning, as are the basalt columns of the cliff overlooking the beach. I definitely recommend stopping here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This black sand beach is beautiful. The water is extremely rough and the contrast of the black sand with the crashing white waves is amazing. You landscape is magnificent too. There’s a cave you can walk into and some cool rock formations when you get to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is another area that the Game of Thrones shot at if you're into that sort of thing. It was a rainy day so we didn't have an issue with it being too crowded. We took cover in the basalt rock cave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must go place when you visit Iceland. Southeast of Reykjavik you will find a stunning scenery of rock formations in the sea that almost look alien.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can walk along the rocks and enjoy the view, you can travel down closer to the beach and be fascinated by rock columns, etc. Highly recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The cliffs are beautiful, but let's be honest - the volume of people at this place was ridiculous, even in the middle of winter. I can't even imagine what it would be like in the middle of summer. I would definitely steer clear of this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iceland Coastline
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand beach with the rocks jutting out of the water. Quite a site and there are no shells, just round shiny  black and grey rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice scenery with a lot of other people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black beach offers a nice scenic view and the basalt columns are fascinating. It does get super crowded though and everybody tries to take their picture sitting on the columns.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Soaring basalt cliffs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful black sand beach, but definitely NOT of the sunbathing/swimming kind. Here you can appreciate the powerful waves of the ocean, admire the soaring sea cliffs with sea birds, look for perfectly polished pebbles and rocks, and examine the stunning geology of the basalt columns. Do be careful of small children and heed the warning of the signs...the waves are like nothing you've ever experienced regardless of when you visit and you WILL be swept if you're not paying attention. NEVER turn your back to the ocean!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing geology
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a lovely beach with lots of geology and rock formations to admire. The geological formations are formed by the volcanic activity on the island. It is a lovely walk along the beach and I would recommend doing it on a day when there isn't so much wind so that it is easier to see the scenery.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and caves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful cave, beach and rock formations along the black sand beach. Only 1m walk from the car park which meant if this is your last stop on a full days south coast adventuring you don't have far to walk!Free parking and cafe onsite by the car park. Toilets are available but you do have to pay (which you can do by card)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Striking and dramatic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This striking volcanic beach was well worth the drive from Reykjavik- dramatic black sand, crashing waves, soaring cliffs, large caves and the utterly unique basalt columns all make for a beach unlike any other. As others have noted, be sure to read the warning signs and exercise caution at the water's edge.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Drive road 215 all the way to the end, trough the small village, to the big parking area with a small restaurant. The black sand beach was crowded by tourists, but it's so huge that everyone could do their own thing. Nice to get out of the car and have a short walk and take some pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quickly stopped in here in between Skaftafell and Hella. The beach is beautiful and the columns are incredible. Just be careful of sneaker waves! Cafe at the beach also available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A scenic beach on black sand where Dilwale movie was shot- a nice cave and troll freezes in the sea - but the waves can be dangerous

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Reynesfjara, Black beach, South Iceland.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara is situated about 160 kms from Reykjavik and can also be covered in a day trip from the capital.It is all the more popular because of its association with the famous series ‘Game of Thrones’. The black sandy beach has an outer-worldly setting, with its white foamy waves crashing in all its might against the black shoreline, the foam and the spray rising up in the air.  Strong gusts of winds blows at you from the ocean and brings with it the moisture and the spray. The black monoliths which stand out from the sea about 500 meters into the water seems to preside over the whole show.  The black beach is majestic and surreal in its appeal. Nature around here is made up of shades of Black and white. No wonder, Reynesfjara is considered  one of the most beautiful beaches in Iceland.We stayed for close to an hour when suddenly  it started to drizzle and in a few minutes large drops of  rain pelted at us from the sky. It was time to rush for cover. Though   Hálsanefshellir  can provide some quick shelter, we decided to pack up and leave. Up near the car park, their is a well decked cafeteria with rest rooms and hot beverages for the weary traveler, which we made good use of. I was driving a Jeep Cherokee and mind you it is a wonderful car to have in such rugged and wild terrain . So my suggestion would be to pick up a sturdy car, preferable an SUV if you plan to do a similar road trip in Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go at low tide
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you can manage to get to the beach at low tide, go around the two caves and climb over the rocks. This will treat you to a climb through a small natural rock arch and then a view of the sea formations from the other side! Beware of the water (people die each year from the massive undertow of the sneaker waves), so if tide is coming in, don’t chance it. Instead you can drive around to the town of Vik and get a picture that way, just not as up close and impressive!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A black sand beach with sneaky waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not much to say about it.  It was a black sand beach and with warning signs about sneaky waves.  These waves could wash you away back into the ocean.  They showed the number of people who lost their lives last year.  It is part of the tour to and just one of many places in Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this was my favorite tour, always wanted to see black beaches, it was spectacular,the rock formations so unique. the sand so textured,amazing to touch. it was spectacular,true beauty

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A photographic wonderland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited in November, in the midst of a downpour. Even so, there were quite a few tourists here, so I'd recommend visiting in the off season (winter) if you want to avoid crowds. The beach is stunning with its polished black lava rocks and hypnotic, threatening, pounding surf.  (PLEASE be careful and don't turn your back on or wade into the water - it's a riptide that will suck you out to sea. During our 30 minutes here we saw several clueless tourists nearly get knocked off their feet, and my own boots got wet from an unexpectedly high rising tide.)The lava flow formations and basalt columns are fascinating.Worth the 2.5-hour drive from Reykjavik, especially if you allow yourself enough time to make it part of a south-coast tour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great looking beach but not for swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The late March day we visited the beach was windy, overcast and cold. Even then the place was quite busy and crowded. The sea was quite rough so we maintained a respectful distance to the crashing waves but even on such a day the place was quite photogenic. Avoiding the crowd was a challenge but we still managed a few decent photos but avoided climbing the famous basalt columns. A must see place if  you are in Vik.
