reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not such a magical experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would either visit early morning or late evening as during the day this beach gets run over with coaches. Parking is nearly impossible  near the restaurant. The restaurant is not worth it. However, the beach is wonderful if you walk a bit from the main entry point and the basal columns.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stop on the southern Iceland tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black sand beach and some impressive rock formations. Make sure you look up at the cliffs to see the variations in rock colours and their structure. Well worth visiting

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great and unique beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is well-known in Iceland and can be very crowded.I recommend you to come early in the morning if you want to take clear photos or use very long exposure to 'eliminate' the people there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really Interesting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really recommend coming here. The geology is absolutely stunning, and you can walk along the black beach past the popular basalt columns to see other formations and get a view of the formations off the coast. So much black, along with the wiping wind and crashing waves made this area a memorable experience for me.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach, photographer's dream
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As you get to the beach you see the rock formations and basalt columns formed as a result of vulcanology.  A bit irritating to find (as a keen photographer) a group of British schoolkids all sitting on the columnar forms while their teacher explained their formation - the kids, though, were absorbed in the phones and looking out to sea.  Shame they were polishing with their nether regions the things that they should have been polishing their intellects on - and they didn't half get in the way of those of us who like taking photographs.  Oh well; Iceland trip?  Box ticked.  Columnar basaltic forms?  Box ticked.The waves were wonderful; not seen anything like those on a beach since living in Orkney some years ago.  Good for the soul.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning black lava beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even in horrible weather this beach is stunning. Caves and rock formations on beach and offshore are amazing. Another "must see".

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the must-see stops on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No trip to Iceland can be complete without a stop on this famous beach. The place is just out of this world. The weather and waves can get scary in a heartbeat, but this just contributes to the magic of the place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Site
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For a very senior citizen, this was a hard hike, but the reward is there.  Nature created beautiful sculpture overlooking the black sand beach and out in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved this place. Having a love for geology this is a fascinating and intricately detailed place to visit. The sands are wonderfully black (when wet) and the sound of the surf breaking along with the hills overhead is a perfect accompaniment.  A word of warning, the beach is very busy with people and coaches are arriving and departing all the time. If you are looking to take more professional photos then you will have to be patient and lucky to get shots without throngs of people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wowee
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A mini giants causeway on a volcanic sand beach. Absolutely freezing in the month of March but nonetheless stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worlds most beautiful beach (for Goths)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is probably the best most memorable place I've visited in Iceland.Black sand with giant waves and giants causeway style rock formations as well as others all very stunning.And the breathtaking cave incredible!Beware of the sneaky waves turn you back on them for too long and they will try and snatch you! Do not get too close the undercurrents will drag you off before anyone can react!Definitely be coming back here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: .....and perfect vuews, it's just a shame it's so busy that you can't get a photo without someone else being in it!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very cool!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When I went it had been snowing and it was super windy. It was actually the worst weather of my trip. And it's half the reason I love it, it was so dramatic. There's a cafe and toilets nearby, just don't got too close to the beach or get stuck in any of the caves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: If Tim Burton directed your summer holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The little coastal town of Vik is sort of in the middle of nowhere, so sadly not many people get to see this incredible black sand beach. It's quite strange to see, as I'd never seen anything like it before. With the crashing waves and the jagged rocks out in the ocean, it's quite a dramatic scene. There's a cafe nearby so you can go in and get warm after you've built a gothic-looking sandcastle, perhaps.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A stunning black sand beach with fascinating rock formations all around but beware the sneaker waves (saw plenty of selfie-taking people get their feet wet!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's beautiful and dramatic--you should stop here for sure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are on the ring road, and why wouldn't you be, you are probably on your way here anyway.  Other than the number of other people also on the beach, this place is just fantastic.  Crashing waves, dramatic sunsets, basalt columns, black beach rocks, it's got it all.  There is a restaurant nearby, and it's a free attraction.  One of the must see spots in Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a black sand beach with an extraordinary cave (where a couple were having wedding photos taken whilst it was freezing and blowing a hooley) and some interesting off shore rock formations. Great location for photos. The waves are very dangerous and a couple of people were swept off their feet in spite of the warnings. Plenty of parking and a good café too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Photo Opportunities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here as part of a photography workshop for early morning sunrise.  Beautiful basalt rock cliffs and caves bordering the black sand beach with sea stacks out in the water.  Parking, small cafe and WC at location.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great ocean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The location is at the black sand beach. Is very windy as is beside the ocean.. the sand is black volcano sand.. with the special stone formations. Be careful of the waves though as is might goes very high most of times.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved visiting this popular Black Sand Beach near Vik, Iceland with beautiful rock formations just off shore.  Yes, there will be lots of people but the beach is large and you only have to walk a bit to find some privacy.  There is a cave and basalt pillars which are also photo opportunities.  If your lucky enough to catch a sunset on a clear day you won't be disappointed!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Extremely beautiful, Extremely busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A definite must see if visiting the south coast and every tour company in Iceland agrees.  It is truly something unique and beautiful.  The only problem is that when you go you are likely to be surrounded by tons of other people.  That’s the reason I can’t give it an excellent rating

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach....nature's wonder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Reynisfjara beach on 7th of March 2018. This is one of my favourite places in iceland. The fine black sand on the shore is amazing and a nature s wonder. We visited it during sunset and it was so serene and a visual treat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: black pearl beach is so amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the scene from Game of Thrones with black basalt columns and black lava beach... and strong waves crashing in ... was crazy beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but very busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was lovely, but was incredibly busy and also got there on very windy afternoon. With better weather would be more beautiful, however there are prettier places within iceland than this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are visiting the southern coast of Iceland, definitely make this a must-stop on your itinerary. It was beautiful! The basalt columns are incredible and make for some really amazing pictures. Walk around the corner to the cave too; it's really amazing. Great coastal views here too. Loved it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool black beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice visit to a black beach. Not a place to sunbathe but interesting texture and my kids even did sand angels. It is less windy in a cave which allows to sit and enjoy the view away from the wind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A stunning black beach with basalt columns and caves well worth visiting.Plenty of parking and a cafe next to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I CAN SEE FOR MILES AND MILES AND MILES!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The same day my son watched Bon Iver perform in London we walked the beach featured in the Bon Iver video 'Holocene'. It was a really windy day which added to the drama, The views are amazing. There are warning signs posted to alert you about sneaker waves, so you can spend an hour watching the idiots getting soaked trying to dodge the waves! Wrap up well, and wear Gore Tex if you're an idiot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Multi faceted wonder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited on a self-drive day trip to see the nearby waterfalls and Dyrholaey. There is a black sand beach in Vik but this one is before Vik and is signposted as Reynisfjara. The car park is free and there is a restaurant on site but be aware it ain't cheap (£5 for a coffee and £7.50 for a small portion of chips). The beach itself is stunning and though it will be busy most times it is large enough to not be intrusive in my view. The waves are spectacular and fun to dodge, just don't turn your back on them, as they bite. Take waterproof boots/shoes if you want to get near the shoreline. The rock formations are stunning and if you are lucky the weather conditions can compliment the views. Definitely worth a visit as part of any tour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful in a blizzard, has to be amazing in good weather!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was difficult to really enjoy this beach in the midst of horrible weather, but, even so, it was worth the trip. The sea was very rough and a little eerie in the half light, with the rock formations looming in the distance.  Add sunlight and birds and it has to be amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be aware of the sneaker waves ! take a waterproof shoes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand beach is a charming place where you can see the amazing basalt columns along with the sea sight and rock formations (Vik trolls)The sand is always wet due to sneaker waves that usually reach 50% of the bay's area so I would recommend a waterproof shoes to get a more comfortable experience

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Island is beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see place. Very tranquil, and just outstanding views from top to bottom. We saw The Gullfoss, Geysir and of course the Blu Lagoon

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The pictures really don't do this place justice.  You must go there and experience the beauty for yourself.  It was very crowded with tourists so perhaps find a time before of after all of the tour buses arrive, but definitely worth the stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most mystical and beautiful places on earth. Truly dangerous waters -- stay way back.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The basalt columns, fascinating caves, and black sand beach made this instantly one of my favorite places on earth. The ocean has never seemed more mighty and powerful than it was here on a windy winter day in February. Do not underestimate the undertow and sudden distance-crossing roaring "sneaker" waves. Several tourists have died here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the visit. Easy access, interesting scenery. It is totally worth the driving there. They have a coffee shop with food and bathroom near the parking lot which is very convenient.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A place of Gods
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This placed has got something special for me the moment I seen it in pictures. Being there at dawn, feeling the ocean, the wind and then seeing the sun rising behind the trolls rocks made me feel I am living in a kind of fantasy world. The beauty and power of nature is amazingly combined at Reynisfjara Beach. It was very windy when we've been there, and the force of the wind blowing from the shore to the ocean was getting really strong as we were stepping closer to the end of the beach. Be very precaution when you are there and don't try to climb the basalt rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One for the eyes...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a tourist trap without doubt, but don't let that put you off. The beach is easily accessed off Route 1 via the 215 road. Very weather and tide dependent. We parked the car close to the end of the 215 road. This left us with a 200m walk to the beach. The black sand is very striking. You are able to walk close to the cliffs and even climb the basalt stacks. From here you are then able to take in the scale of the place, with the waves coming in.This is an easy stop off to break up a drive. There is a shop / restaurant looking building in the car park but we did not venture inside.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this beach as part of the south shore tour. This is a very unique beach as it is black coloured. There are some really beautiful views here as well, I was fortunate enough to come here during sunrise where the view is spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous area! No fee for parking, but usually a fee to use the restroom. However credit machine was out of order, so we went inside where it’s free!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this on a dreary, rain-swept day; nonetheless, the brooding beauty of the beach and its spectacular landforms was undiminished. In fact, I'd venture to say that its mystery was very much enhanced by the weather, as well as rolling surf. The only downside to this place was the hordes of folks who had just arrived by busloads: I'd recommend giving the place a pass or waiting in your vehicle until the busloads depart, as they overcrowded the property and were exceptionally disrespectful to it by tossing Kleenexes, cigarette butts, and other garbage about.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is gorgeous. We loved it so much that we are going to visit it again for a second day! Highly recommend you check it out if you're in Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go Early to Avoid Tourists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a gorgeous beach, with really cool caves. Highly recommend going for sunrise, you avoid tourists and the sun rising over the columns is unreal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was impressive--the angry waves of the North Atlantic Ocean come crashing against the shore in unpredictable swells. This is not a beach for relaxing in your bikini!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Game of thrones fans
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved visiting this beach, one of the main highlights of our trip. It is a must see if you love game of thrones. The weather can be quite windy, so make sure to wrap up warm. There is a big carpark and a resturant with a bathroom. Highly recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful sand but it was extremely windy during winter and we stayes only 10mins because it started to hail so bad! But a must-visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chilly beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a pretty beach with great space and backdrops for photos, but it gets incredibly cold from the wind! Bring your coat and a hat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited here on the south coast tour. Very unusual place, black sand beach and interesting basalt rock formations. Unfortunately it was torrential rain all day so put a little downer on the day but still enjoyed it. Amazing waves on the beach, huge and great to watch. Be careful not to get too close as we were warned they’re so powerful and the current is so strong people have gotten too close before and not made it back. So enjoy from a distance. Toilets and cafe here for food and drinks, limited menu and pricey like everywhere so we brought a packed lunch which we ate on our tour bus

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Dramatic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very dramatic beach with angry waves crashing on the beach. Definite Must See! Be ware of the sneaker waves, they are legitimate and we saw many people unexpectedly drenched by them but luckily that's the worst that happened.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: black beach, perfect spot for lots of photos on the south coast. Rock formations,  must visit when exploring the south. car park and toilets on site

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unusual scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is beautiful. Very unusual and interesting. There is a little cafe here, too. Although it is quite far out, well worth a visit. You won't be disappointed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing spot in south of Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is incredible and very beautiful. We went there in winter so it was cold but the view amazing, with the black and white contrast between the snow and the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun Photo Stop with the Basalt Cliffs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really enjoyed a nice walk along the Reynisfjara beach. We sat on the cliffs and were mesmerized watching the waves come in. We were there on a relatively calm day, though we saw posted sign saying that the ocean has quite a powerful "sneaker" tide that can unexpectedly carry visitors out to sea. Our family spent about 45 minutes here looking at the beautiful rock formations and sea. There is a restaurant there, but it is situated in the parking lot with no views - very strange placement in such a beautiful area. We did not eat there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another Great Sight On The South Coast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came here on a very windy cold snowy rainy day, the waves were crashing on the black shore which that with the howling winds made it quite eery, the stunning Basalt columns peering majestically out of the sea and the caves made for some dramatic photos, i do believe it was once voted in the top 10 of best non tropical beach in the world which when there you can see why even in the adverse weather conditions.caution is needed when on this beach as the sea have what they call sneaker waves which come up further and can sweep you away with the force, your tour guide will keep informing you of this, lots of photo shoots here to be had and totally stunning along the south shore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place not to be missed on the South coast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place to see! Don't miss it on the South Coast! Caution is a must as people died after being caught bt a big wave. So don't go to close to the water. We could not see the cave as it was high tide when we got there, but worth the trip anyway. The parking lot at the end of the road is in a bad condition with a lot of potholes. Be cautious! If you go at the black beach restaurant, try the skyr cake. It is really good and typical.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful- even in cold, windy conditions!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here on our last morning in Vik before heading our of town. We went around 10:30 in the winter, which was right when the sun was coming up and it was beautiful! The wind was super strong but we still loved our visit here! Got some gorgeous picutres between the columns!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another great visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful scenery which is why we came back to this place on our trip to Iceland,The caves, the basalt columns, the beach are are fantastic and great for photographs. We have been told and there are signs saying that this is a dangerous beach because of the waves crashing in so beware.When we went on both occasions there were many tourists there but this really didn't bother us.We would go back when we visit Iceland again, hopefully soon!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: But tourists EVERYWHERE.  Difficult to get a photo without a person in it.  Sunrise and sunset are the best times.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the stops from the glacier hiking tour I took with Troll Expeditions. It’s unusual black sand, basalt stacks, and roaring waves is a must-see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning but DO NOT get close to the water!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This location is so well worth your visit and it was one of the highlights of our trip. In fact, we loved it so much that we ended up visiting it three times. The combination of black sand, huge waves and basalt columns lend itself to beautiful pictures and drone footage.There is a little rest stop right here with a restaurant/cafe and a bathroom. We didn't go into the restaurant/cafe area and wanted to use the bathroom but there is a charge so we just waited until we got back to our hotel which was only 10 minutes away. Try to get here when there are less people because it does get quite crowded and will make it difficult to get a shot without people in it.But major warning, DO NOT get anywhere near the water. You might think you're well away from where the waves normally come in, but there are "sneaker" waves that will take you right out. I made this mistake and fell in the water, but thankfully was not swept out. But I was completely wet from the waist down and dunked my phone in the water (but managed to recover it later) so the subsequent times I went, I didn't go anywhere near the water. So especially if you have children or avid photographers who get in the zone, make sure to warn them!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is before the town of Vik off the Ring Road.  It has a cute little church right before the beach. On the beach are basalt sea stacks and there are interesting caves.  It was ranked in 1991 as one of the 10 most beautiful non tropical beaches in the world. Water is treacherous so they advise not to go in although when we were there, one person ignored the warnings.  There is a cafe there as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stop here! Stop everywhere! It’s all amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came here and it was freezing, raining, and wind blowing 30mph+. It was amazing and beautiful in a raw and wild way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, black sand with hexagonal pillars made from volcanic eruptions. Cafe and bathrooms nearby, beautiful landscape.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do not miss it. A stunning black beach with beautiful views. Very exposed and windy. A real gem.....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a great location. Glad we did a day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was an a amazing location. Lots to see and photograph. Added bonus its free. We spent nearly 2 hours there with teenagers and they had a blast.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunrise engagement!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I will never forget out trip to this beautiful and magnificent beach. The basalt salt columns and rock formations are so magical it makes you feel like you’re in a movie. Visit this magnificent beach and be transported elsewhere.It is also the lucky spot as to where my bestfriend and partner forever proposed to me during sunrise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful during day, amazing during night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect spot for photographers, bird watchers and those who love the sound of the ocean. One of the top places in Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Landscape, Powerful Waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Drove here following road signs and google maps from my phone with my wife, found a spot in the spacious parking lot and walked to the beach taking note of a restaurant and restroom facilities at the front. The attraction was delightfully free of cost. So we skipped on over noting the strong winds and icy chill which made us reach for our face masks. Explored the cave like like structures, climbed unto the rock formations and admired the awesome power of the big waves the crashed ashore.After having enough we hurried back to the car to be comforted by heated seats and nice hot air along with a sip of hot tea and delicious snacks we packed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another must stop!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Continuing on with your South Coast tour of Iceland, be sure to stop by Reynisfjara Beach. It is not that noticeable at first that there is so much going on to see here.  You need to walk along the beach itself to see the parasailing, puffins, and basalt columns.No, this is not your typical beach so don't expect it to be warm. There is no one suntanning here! It is known to have riptides and many unexpected accidents have occurred as a result here.  As you enter, you will see many tall basalt columns that you can climb on for photos. They are all different heights.  There is also a basalt cave here.  Upon the cliffs above the basalt columns, there are plenty of birds flying and nesting seen-- many puffins build their burrows here-- you can see them better and clearer with a pair of binoculars. I used my zoom lens on my camera and got some great photos of the puffins nesting along the cliffside here.  They are so adorable as they assemble on the cliffs in groups or on their own-- you can get great photos of them in action. There is also a nice cafe located here at the beach which serves great sandwiches and fast food to go.  Plan to spend at least an hour or two to really enjoy the sights and sounds here at Reynisfjara Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Geologic Formation - Frigid in the Winter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The basalt columns and formations are incredible and surreal to see along with the black sand beach and general environment.  It's the type of thing you see so often in landscape photography, but it's an entirely different experience to see it up close and try to wrap your mind around it all.  The other thing that's challenging to wrap your mind around, is how cold a wind can possibly be when it comes ripping off the ocean - dress warm in the winter unless you want to experience a bone-chilling cold like no other.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach at Reynisfjara is stunning!  The lava rock statues that have been carved by pounding Atlantic waters are beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and dangerous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning! Loved it here but the wind was so strong, it knocked some peoples strollers over. Our was sturdy and we put the rain over over it which protected out little one. We followed advice and didn’t go right to the coast line. The sunset and views were amazing. Again, extremely icy but worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hold on to your kids, as the wind is very strong!! A must see place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you’re driving along the south coast , you got to stop here to enjoy amazing views and cool basalt columns / sea stacks , the black beach itself and giant waves..... our 7 year old hung on to us at all times as she couldn’t walk On her own because of the extremely strong winds .... It was sleet/snowy too so was hard for anyone to walk really . But that’s changed after 15-20 minutes. Weather changes constantly in Iceland. Do not go anywhere near the waves .... Some dumb tourists were climbing up on the basalt columns and going a bit too close to the deadly waves for that perfect selfie , use common sense is all I say ....It was lovely to watch the stunning views even in the horrendous weather.... Walk under the cave , it’s the only calm place without wind to enjoy looking at the black sands and the giant waves .....Highly recommend seeing this place . There was a small cafe and restrooms but we have not used the facilities. To get to the black beach ( when driving from Reykjavik) you need get off the ring road to turn right few kms (6 kms I think it was ) before reaching the town of Vik . Easy to get to , everything on ring road is .... we’ve left at 8.30 am in the dark and got to reynisfjara ( black beach ) just before lunch time . Only stopped once or twice along the way for photos... It didn’t get light until after 10.30 am ( December you only get 4 hours of daylight). We drove slowly as some parts of the road was icy ....You can definitely do it as a day trip from Reykjavik but we carried on driving towards the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon and stayed there for a night to break the long journey.....Happy holidays:)))

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great stop!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand is really great to see!Very different than our home in North America.The waves can be dangerous here so be cautious on the beach!There is a café and facilities.NOTE: you have to pay to use restrooms here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We blew in here during the late afternoon hours as the sun was setting. The basalt columns are cool and worth a stop for sure. We did not get around the corner of the beach to see more, as we did not have time. Worth a stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even in the cold, driving rain, there is no doubt this is a stunning location and a must-visit. The waves are dramatic and basalt columns are even more interesting in person.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful views of basalt stacks and columns
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Horrible weather conditions when we visited; A fiercely strong wind that whipped the sand into my eyes, nose and mouth. But there were gorgeous views of the basalt columns at the bottom of the mountain, the small cave-like notch in the mountain, and the basalt stacks in the water. It gave the place an other-worldly feel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow factor!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The coolest beach you’ll ever go to in a parka. It was an almost sunny day in December. Very windy! Take a walk around the corner to see both basalt caves. The black sand and smooth lava stones are unlike anything I’ve ever seen. Must do! Watch out for those “sneaker waves”....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A short detour from the ring road brought us to this black sand beach with unique sea stacks on the water and rock columns on the beach. Parking was a little tight when we visited due to the tour buses. Restautant just next to the carpark.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another ‘must do’ in Iceland!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although described as a black sand beach this is more than that. This is living history in Iceland.The pebbles on the beach are from 3 volcanic eruptions spanning 400 years, they’re of different colours, brick red for 1640ad, grey for the next one and jet black for the latest (apologies, dates not known).The basalt columns, visible from the side across the beach and from the underside from the sea cave are geology at its best along with the two stacks at the far end of the beach.Also look right to the island and see the ‘arch’ at the left end of the island, allegedly a journalist in a small plane flew it through the hole successfully!From the beach it’s possible to see the glacier to the north.Facilities are a cafe for hot drinks and snacks plus toilets which cost 150+ KronerPlease beware the ‘sneaky’ waves that happen in the surf frequently, a Japanese Man was caught out in 2017 and washed away! It’s impossible to rescue anyone as the drop off and undercurrents are lethal....Don’t turn your back to the sea, the next stop is Antarctica which is 9000 miles South.If this review has been useful to you I would appreciate your helpful vote, enjoy your trip in Iceland!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's the black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's the black sand beach. Beautiful, definitely visit this place.Interesting rock formation, similar to Giant Causeway in Ireland, in a smaller for packed scale with black sands, which Ireland's Giant Causeway doesn't have.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Memorable stop.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was one of the stops along our ring road drive in July.  I've read that this is a prettier and less crowded than the black beach in Vik.The place is very picturesque with sea stacks on one side and an arch on the other, with black sand in between. The basalt columns and a sea cave are impressive and are all within 3 minutes walk from each other. The sea cave floods during high tide, I read, and you can check the schedule online or just hope for the low tide.Restaurant and bathroom are available. The crowds were anything but small .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An other name for "black sand beach"
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is actualy the same place as "black sand beach", i gues it is the icelandic name for the same beach. Confusing for tourists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach! Great sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. We visited it in november 2017 around 10am, so we still had the sunrise. Great spot for pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The rock stacks at Reynisfjara really add a breathtaking view to the black sand beach. Worth some pics while you're in Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great monoliths on a wild beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a wild, wind swept black volcanic sand beach in South Iceland. It is known to have dangerous waves, so stay away from the waterline so you don't get swept out to sea! The weather in Iceland can change in five minutes! It was sunny, windy, cold, rainy and hailed in the 45 minutes we were there! The rock formations and basalt cave formations are additional attractions here.  There is a restaurant close to the beach for lunch, if needed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great picture opportunities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Backed rented SUV into parking spot facing the beach and had a tailgate lunch with cold pre-cooked chicken drumsticks and bread purchased at Kronan in Vik.  Then proceeded to take many memorable pictures in this very picturesque area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Interesting Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black sand beach was very cool to see and the rocks structures on the coast of the beach were really interesting. Definitely worth a stop. Very close to Vik.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing! A must do for sure!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Completely unique beach and experience. Geological formations, caves, black sand ... Mother Nature at her best. Be ready for wind and to get a bit wet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Other worldly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing natural basalt out cropping. Huge waves crashing on the black sand beach. Almost otherworldly An experience like nothing else in Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara is one of the most impressive and unusual place we visited during our two trips to Iceland.  It cannot be compared to any other beaches.  Weather permitting, the close you get to the ocean, the more you feel the power of nature being between basalt rocks and huge waves.  Reynisfjara is more accessible in summer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: otherworldly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was one of the highlights of my trip, it is like walking into another world. There were tons of tourists there, but even still it was so worth it. The sand goes from fine black sand to larger black pebbles, to medium sized stones. We took some of eac h as souvenirs. The water is super intense so make sure to stay back. It started hailing for a couple minutes while we were there and the contrast of the white hail on the black sand was beautiful. I would say it is a must-see attraction in Iceland. The restaurant there has delicious lamb soup and some decent fish and chips that we tried as well - prices were about typical for Iceland tourist restaurants. My 4 year old loved playing in the sand and going into the cave. We got some of our best photos here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara is a stunning beach.  There is s many beaches in the world but a black sand beach filled with formations, rocks, and tourist is a must!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must-Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The weather was rainy and misty.  But even then, the unique nature and views of this beach and the basalt columns couldn't dampen my family's spirit.  There are signs warning visitors not to go too near the water, as strong waves could come up the beach without warning and wash you away.  This happened as recently as a few years ago to a tourist, who drowned and died.  If you have small children, keep an eye on them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As well as black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great adventure. Perfect mountain, cliff, rock and sea. Great combination where created by nature. LoL

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well worth going
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there on a Saturday, so there were lots and lots of people.  Soooo windy! I thought I would be able to fly my drone, but no... it was waaaaay too windy for that. The waves were beautiful, the scenery incredible.  I took lots of pictures and videos and re-live the place when I see them. I thought it was one of the most impressive beaches I have ever been to.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Majestic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is at one end of the Black Sand Beach.  It is quite impressive and can be seen all along the south coast line.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had pelting rain and and winds so fierce, we had a hard time taking photos here. We enjoyed the beach. The elements made it difficult but we had never seen a black sand beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Trip to Iceland will not be complete if you do not make a stop here. I made a pitstop here to catch the exquisite view of the sunset and the waves. Definitely worth it! The beach was filled with people taking photos and couples doing their wedding photoshoots. Great experience nonetheless.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is like not other I've seen. The day we went it was very foggy which added to it's uniqueness. Highly recommend a road trip to Vik while in Iceland!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach with basalt columns
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy access to gorgeous views and the beach. Very interesting rock formations and basalt columns. Highly recommend stopping here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Windy and crowded, but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't forget your hat, if you are visiting this place in October. We stayed in Vik, and came before all the big tour buses - yet the beach was crowded. - Breathtaking views!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: black sand beach,crashing surf,bassalt columns  this place has it all
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is another destination our tour company Iceland Unlimited recommended.  The above title sums it up. Georgeous.  Great place to go for a walk but be careful of thewaves   They are especially strong and can pull you in.  I have never seen black sand before.  It is beautiful. Although there is a restaurant there we did not eat there so cannot report on it.  On concern however are the bathroom facilities.  There are not enough.  10:00 in the morning and there was a 15 person line up for the ladies.  Also they are pay toilets

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to find. Blacksand Beach is one of a kind. We have been visiting many beaches but This one is unique👏 words can’t tell enough, you must go and experience It yourself. There is little restaurant just next to beach, toilets too. Though, the Beach might be crowded, don’t worry... there is plenty of space for everyone to enjoy the view, take photos etc.5 stars👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Close to Vik is the unique black sand beach of Reynisfjara, with its caves, hexagonal, basalt rock formations, rock towers rising from the ocean and the beach, made up of small black pebbles.  It is unique and picturesque - and can be busy, naturally.There are so many photo opportunities and the signs say it, all reviews say it - beware of 'sneaker' waves that can creep up on you and potentially, wash you away.  It can be dangerous, but take care and respect the power of the ocean and its surprises, whilst enjoying the location.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach - Game of Thrones filming location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beautiful beach is a two hour drive from Reykjavik. There may be other beautiful beaches in Iceland but this one is easily reachable and it’s a lovely drive to get there. The cafe was a little grotty and the toilets weren’t great but they do have some use. 200isk to have a wee and then get locked in because of a faulty lock! That was my only negative. The beach has beautiful black sand and is super dangerous - creeper waves have been known to sweep people into the sea. Despite the warning signs I saw lots of people with selfie sticks close to the waters edge. Obviously think they don’t need to respect the ocean! Busy but not too busy on a Friday afternoon, a highlight of our trip to Iceland

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must Visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This black sand beach is one of the best places in Iceland we most enjoyed visiting.  The basalt columns are extremely unique and we took many nice photos there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and great geology
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely worth a visit to see the expansive beach (watch out for the sneakers/large waves!). Columnar jointed basalt rock was great to see in real life, and the view of the rock sea stacks was fantastic. Apparently one of the best non-tropical beaches in the world and we can understand why. Definitely worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach, hexagonal rocks, phalic rock formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just before arriving in Vik is the black sand beach of Reynisfjara. This is a popular attraction and a few hours from Rejkavik and Keflavik. I was able to make it here after an early morning stop at the Blue Lagoon and return to my hotel in Rejkavik that night. The large gravel parking lot was crowded when i arrived in the afternoon but I was able to find a spot. There where several buses here and the beach was full of people taking pictures. Tourists took turns posing on the hexagonal rocks and they were full of people the entire time I was there. Perched higher above were a few sheep lazily chewing on some grass. If you walk around the hexagonal rock pillars, there is Hálsanefshellir cave and the rock spires out in the ocean including the one that looks like a large phallus. I would call this a "must see" Iceland spot as you can take in and experience so much from here. It would be great to come early or stay late and perhaps enjoy it without the crowds. If time was tight, I may skip Dyrholaey in favor of this as the arches are visible from here. If you want to stay dry, be careful of the occasional rogue wave that sweeps extra high up the beach soaking tourists shoes and pants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing rock formations adjacent to a long black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The basalt columns are pretty amazing along with other interesting rock formations. The beach is quite long, but has a warning sign for "sneaker waves" which catch people ignoring the surf to take photos of the rock formations and occasionally result in tourist deaths. If you just pay attention to the surf, it is quite safe and lovely. There is a spur off N1 that leads down to the beach and columns that is on the west side of the mountain from the town of Vik. The black sand beach in the town of Vik is also quite lovely, but does not have a view of the basalt columns as they are around the curve of the beach, west of there. We visited the beach in Vik before realizing that we had to go further west to get to the park area with the famous columns.There is a parking lot which was not large enough to hold the cars on a late afternoon in October so I hate to think how crowded it would be in July or August.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place for a stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The longer the walk, the quieter it gets. Most people stay close to the parking lot.Nice beach with impressive rock formations.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible beautiful beach but be careful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is one of the famous black beaches in Iceland bear Vik. Black sand beach , basalt column and volcano stones formation. Be careful and  do not be very near to the beach there are warnings about the sneakers waves there as it is deadly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning, but deadly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most exciting part about this beach is the fact that you could be killed at any moment. The waves are 10 feet high and mighty with it, but every so often a mega wave throws all it's got much higher than normal up the black sand, catching photographers and tourists out and making them dash for safety. Thats if you're lucky. There have been 3 deaths here over several years, and many who have lived to tell the tale about how they lost their expensive cameras to the sea. There are warnings before you go onto the beach about this peculiarity. Heed them and enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great looking black sand beach and basalt columns.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a short drive off the ring road to the west of Vik but definitely worth it.  Unfortunately for us it was a windy and rainy day but we had to go.  The waves coming in looked like they were about 10 ft tall.  It was interesting to see the basalt columns, but because of the wind and rain we did not take the time to read any of the history of the area.  Because it was early in September most of the birds were gone.  We got soaked and didn't stay long with all the rain and wind.  Hope for a sunny day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the walk and the travel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It takes a while to drive here from the city but you definitely can do this on your own if you have a rental car. The drive is pretty and once you get to the beach there is parking along the road. However, you can not see the beach from the parking lot or the road. BE PREPARED TO WALK. It is about a 2.5 mike hike from the car park to the beach. Once you get to the beach it is definitely worth it but don't get too close to the ocean. The waves are usually very violent. This is worth a visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: lovely place to visit and taking landscapes photosBe aware of the waves, they can be very dangerous!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a gorgeous place.... just like everywhere else in Iceland! We enjoyed walking around, watching the sea, and getting some great pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very cool - especially the Iron Throne-looking basalt columns.  Worth a visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited here on a cold, blustery, rainy day.  The beach was still really cool with it's creepy cave and enormously tall basalt column wall that makes for a great photo op.  Be very careful of the waves - they were wicked strong, and the tide took photographers and tourists off-guard several times -- water washed up and overtook several unsuspecting people.  There is a small restaurant there (though we didn't eat there) and plenty of parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit but lots of tourists and buses
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see when visiting Iceland!  Such a beautiful spot!   Do not ignore the warning signs to keep a safe distance from shoreline.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely views but watch the waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place has a lot of great photography opportunities and lots of visitors around.   The waves are unpredictable and there are signs posted upon entry to the beach so just be aware of the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The only disadvantage has been that the parking lot was full and even had some loaded busses. I should have gone earlier and enjoy the scene myself.The basalt structures are truly impressive and the small cave structure with severe structures was amazing.What I enjoyed most however was walking the length of the black beach 2.5km.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A black sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was drizzling but it did not stop us from strolling along the black sand beach.Beautify scenery.We even climbed up to a few basalt columns for stunning photo snapping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Waves were pounding the day we were there and there were strong winds, but that did not detract from the beautiful view of islands.  It was definitely worth the long drive from Reykjavik!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy, but Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a gorgeous beach.Especially in the evening in summer.Unfortunately, it is packed with people, all wanting to climb up and down nature's interestingly created rocks.There are restaurants & shops close by which are great to rest, but overly busy and take off from the greatness of this part of Iceland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and Unique
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is just a short drive off the ring road. Even in the rain, it was amazing and worthwhile to see. The columns in the ocean, the cave, the black sand-all of it is captivating. Definitely a must-see!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: See Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the Black Sand Beach and all the things I've said about that would apply here.  it is very much worth the side trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to explore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty views of the black sand beach and large rock formations.  Missed it the first time, so need to be on the look-out for it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is easily accessible and there is a coffee shop and toilet close to the parking lot. The sand is more of a smallish pebble consistency and very black. TheBasalt columns are spectacular. People climbing the columns and a group of tourists blatantly disregarding the no drone were distracting. There were a few caves with distinct rock shape depressions. The puffins flocked to the cliffs above the beach in amazing numbers. The view of the sea stacks, or as legend has it 2 giants pulling a ship with 3 sails that were turned to stone, look different from each angle. Beware of the water. People regularly drown at this beach due to powerful ocean conditions.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A scenic location, ideal for that "beautiful beach photo" as part of a wedding photoshoot. As you guys have ample photos to see from the internet, I shall not describe the view. Instead, I will tell you what to expect.Good amenities available such as a lovely cafe with free wifi and plenty of parking space. The toilets are available for free if you are a customer at the cafe. Otherwise you need a pay a small fee for a separate toilet (pay like you would on a vending machine) located on the outside of the building. If you visit between 11am to 5pm, it will be very crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous end of the world beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Forgetting that Game of Thrones put this view on every fans to do list, it is still absolutely worth the trek if you're on the Southern Road.  Parking can be a challenge at peak times but it is free and there are bathrooms and a coffee shop if you want to enjoy a bevey on the sand while puffins cliff dive above your head.  Go at sunset and see the glistening light hit wet black sand and sea birds swarming to nest.  Beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and needs to be treated better
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's unique basalt formations, nesting puffins, and black sands make it a site to behold. The ocean is also quite active so the sounds of crashing waves adds to this scene. It is worth a visit. This is one of the more highly impacted beaches I visited. Tourist come here in bus and car loads, not all of them respectful to the surroundings. Be prepared to be around many people.A note for your consideration, cairns are rocks stacked on top of each other to mark trail heads or give direction on trails. When you make them anywhere else, not for marking trains, this is the equivalent of graffiti in nature. Please resist leaving your mark in nature. It takes away the beauty for the rest of us. There were so many cairns on this beach it did really take away from some of the beauty for me. Then there were others who decided they were targets to throw rocks at and sadly this was a group of adults doing this not children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite stop on our South Iceland trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We recently returned from our first (but definitely not last) trip to Iceland. We visited so many places in our 6 days along the Southern Coast, but this is definitely my favorite place. I won't say anything about the Basalt Salt Columns, Cave, or Reynisdrangar because everyone already knows about those and expects to see them, I was amazed at how much larger Reynisdrangar was than I had realized from photographs. It was simply incredible to experience during sunset. It is a very large beach so you can spend a lot of time here and get a variety of photos and video. We also enjoyed our dinner at Black Sand Beach Restaurant located right in the parking lot of this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not far from Ring Road and definitely worth the stop to see the amazing views.  We saw it at sunrise and it was breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: ohh the Black beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black beach or reynisfjara is amazing with wonderful rock formations around.Although it was pretty crowded the day we went considering august is the peak tourist season,I think if you want to get the real feel you should go really early and can have the complete beach to yourself

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy but worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful black sand (well pebble really) beach with spectacular crashing waves that make an amazing sound as the water runs back out through the pebbles. Great view of the arch at Dyrholaey, plus the puffins on the cliffs above. The basalt columns are fantastic too. The place is very busy - lots of tour buses and tourists there when we visited - but it really is worth a short diversion off route 1 if you are driving by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is also called the black sand beach  You can take great pictures here of the black sand, stacks in the water, basaltic columns are fun to climb on

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is quite striking with the basalt columns and black pebbles.  It is crowded, but worth seeing.  The Troll Rocks and the caves are the best features.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This black sand beach near Vik is a must if you have access to wheels. It is often overrun with seals and has a small restaurant as well as bathroom facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy, but still great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beware that there are A LOT of tourists here! Still, one can't deny that this is an amazing place and a really unique sight. The long beach with black sand, the caves, the basalt columns, everything looks kinda Game of Throne-ish. It's a great place for visiting and one you definitely shouldn't miss, but in the summer you can also stay here and relax sunbathing (if you don't mind a bit colder temperatures than normal summer weather), just don't go into the water - it's dangerous!If you are here, be sure to also visit Dyrholaey, the cliff you see to your right if you face the sea - the views there are way more beautiful than on the beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: If you drive through Vik, do NOT miss this beach!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here on our way back to Reykjavik from Vik.  Drove down the road from the ring road about 5 minutes to the parking area.  There is a restaurant and toilets.  The scenery here is amazing.  The sea is so rough, you have the besalt columns, black sand beach, cliffs, caves, amazing puffins flying around and the rock formations out in the ocean.  Truly an amazing place with lots of opportunities for great photos!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unique place. A must to visit. Very windy. Wear proper walking shoes because the black sand is fluffy and uneven, so not too easy to walk. Breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the Black Sand Beach of Vik. It is a must see with its black sands and interesting rocks. When you walk there, you may feel as if you are on another planet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rocks, surf, powerful waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One reaches this area of the beach after walking through the black sand beach near the basalt columns.  The crowds usually thin out by the time you get to this part of the beach.  You see tall, sculptural rocks coming out of the water, the waves crashing around them.  You can really feel the power of the waves, even if you just stand on the shore.  Do not attempt to swim--there are "sneaker waves" that have climbed many lives.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: South Coast Tour - Iceland Tours by Taxi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: SOUTH COAST TOUR - ICELAND TOURS BY TAXIWe are a party of 4 who arrived in Reykjavik on a cruise ship for 2 days in port.  We had booked Walter for 2 tours prior to leaving home.  Our ship was late to dock, but Walter checked our progress, and once we arrived was waiting for us in his beautiful clean and roomy van.  He switched our two tours around to suit our timetable, which worked out brilliantly.  Our first tour was the Golden Circle, and the following day we travelled to see the beautiful black sand Reynisfjara Beach on the South Coast - stunning scenery all day!  We cannot give enough accolades to Walter - our tours were absolutely amazing - his attention to detail in every aspect of the tour was great - he provided water and snacks, surprise location visits, local knowledge is valuable, free wifi in the van is great, he is a safe driver, and we felt confident we had seen everything there was to see in the time we had to tour.  His knowledge of the area, together with knowledge of coach activities, ensured we visited locations without the crowds of the coaches with also great.  His recommendation to have lamb soup was spot on - yum!  Rest stops were thoughtfully planned, and our photographers were very happy with the opportunities he provided for them.  We arrived back at the port in plenty of time before the ship departure.	We have no hesitation in recommending him for any purpose whilst in Iceland - he's a wealth of knowledge, a really nice guy, and knows how to show visitors to Iceland the best sights for a memorable visit.  We feel, as a party of 4, the tours were excellent value for money, and worked out more economical and were more personal than a ship tour.Thank you Walter, we loved our time with you - Aussies from down under!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice stroll after lunch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A rejuvenating walk - enjoy the cool wind from the ocean. Take your shoes off and feel the sand and the cold water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Black Sand Beaches and Rock Formations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Vik is a bit of a drive from Reykjavik, but well worth it. The area has beautiful black sand beaches, rock formations and several water falls in the area. It is a couple hour drive from Reykjavik, depending on traffic. Traffic is n ot really an issue, but the campers-motor homes can slow you down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sands and basalt caves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very popular destination in Iceland being the most southerly beach and geologically interesting (plus the chance of seeing puffins nesting up on the cliffs). We arrived in the rain and it was still very busy! A sign at the path down warns tourists of the 'sneaky waves' that undercut the beach and pull everything out to sea- our tour guide was sure to alert us to the fact that  two tourists had sadly already been caught out by this phenomena during the year. The basalt formations are the hexagonal ones which are pretty impressive combined with the dark volcanic sand of the beach. Out to sea, the sort of coastal erosion taught in school is plainly seen with arches and columns formed by the wave action. The beach has a busy car park and toilet facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mesmerizing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been there two times in different periods and the feeling was the same. It is a breathtaking place, for me one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. Staring at the waves crushing onto the black shore or walking towards the arch seems to take you to another dimension, out of time and far from any other place you know.Everyone should put this place in his bucket list!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short stop off
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth stopping off for half an hour. There's plenty of parking behind the N1 petrol station and a new supermarket and camping shop in under construction.Reminiscent of the Drongs in Shetland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So many puffins!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hoped to see one or two puffins here but saw dozens! Wonderful!Stunning geological scenery especially the basalt pillars and caves.The sea was gentle so enjoyed the walk along the beach and again entertained by the puffins flying from the cliffs into the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Free Puffin Spotting!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The black beach was beautiful! We got there midday so there were already a lot of people walking around. The waves were crashing in and the puffins were flying around everywhere. A lot of places will charge you for puffin tours, you can just drive here, if you have a rental, and see them for free. The basalt was an amazing backdrop. We were always amazing how the rock was form so many years ago.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved visiting this beach. It was beautiful with the sand, waves and rock formations. Amazing to just walk around and enjoy the scenery. One of my favorite stops during our trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Haystacks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful area with striking water views.  Not overrun with tourists like the golden circle area.  Thoroughly enjoyed our visit here.  Definitely worth a stop

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BE AWARE OF WAVES
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This location has been spotlighted in Iceland for years, but recently tourists are often being swept out to sea due to sneaker waves. Although signs are located at the beach warning people they are scarce and small. I saw multiple people sleeping right along the beach. Although these waves are generally worse in the winter months, you could still see in the sand where sudden waves had come much farther onto the beach than the others. Be aware that this can happen suddenly and watch a few youtube videos. I would hate to see this amazing location monitored or limited due to people being uneducated about its danger.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The sand was....not black.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After having gone around the ring road; I can tell you that the sand here is probably lighter than at most beaches. The sand is NOT the defining feature of this beach; but rather the rock formations and basalt columns, and puffins.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand and lovely views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was an amazing experience. This was quiet and you can walk around the amazing pitch black sand and enjoy the views of the endless North Atlantic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning area. Forget the golden circle and come here.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Scenic drive to this famous  and incredibly busy black sand beach.Nothing quite prepares you for the scale of the emerald cliffs behind which make it so special.Dangerous also - don't turn your back on the waves! There have been fatalities here.It would be perfect to visit when the crowds have gone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An impressive natural wonder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would agree to those that say this is a must-see destination in Iceland. An impressive black beach, the basalt columns, the "frozen" trolls. As the wind was strong and the waves were quite big that day, I just spent time sitting and looking at them as you could truly feel the strength of nature. If the conditions allow, make sure you walk left behind the first corner - there are more caves and less people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely crowded but gorgeous beach and breathtaking views.  Some crazy tourists scaling the rock walls.  You can see some puffins here too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see in Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are traveling in Iceland, visiting Reynisfjara beach is a must. The hexagonal basalt columns are beautiful and unique.  Though we saw other examples of this geologic formation, those at Reynisfjara beach were the most impressive and dramatic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favorite place in South Iceland
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This black sand beach was nothing like me and my family have ever seen.  Vik is about 186 km from Reykjavik.  Definitely drivable in a day.  The beaches are black because of the volcanic ash.   At Reynisfjara Beach there is a cave which is decorated with the columnar basalt which look like a church organ.  It's very unique. You can see the distinctive basalt rocks of Reynisdrangar rising from the sea.  According to folktale, these rocks are the remains of 2 trolls who tried to tow a ship to land, but were caught by daylight and turned to stone.  If you only have time for 1 beach we liked the Reynisfjara beach better than the beach at Vik.  The Halsanefshellir sea cave is only accessible at low tide and we were there at high tide and there are people making sure no one goes near the cave.  The waves are rough and people have died going into the cave at high tide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We saw tons of puffins!  And we found the beach relaxing.  Climbed over the rocks, checked out the cave and rock formations.  Had a bite in the cafe.  Surprisingly good food, especially the lamb soup.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were lucky enough to stay in a house very close to this beach, so were able to visit when it was quieter. During the day there are many cars, buses, and tourists there enjoying the sights.The black sandy beach is trecherous if you do not take normal precautions, and many have drowned there. It is well signposted to alert you.Caves formed by row upon row of tall basalt columns are a highlight, and everyone clambours up on them for photos.The little puffins are a huge drawcard. There are hundreds out to sea during May - August, and they continually fly in to their burrows on the grassy cliff fronts, wait for their photo to be taken, then fly off out to sea again.This is a great place to photograph the beautiful little birds, but across the bay at Dyrhólaey (lighthouse) they are much closer.There is a restaurant at the top of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Photographer's delight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its very windy there so be prepared before you visit. The beach is black which is a surprise as I had never seen a black beach. The basalt columns are very interesting with lovely views of the shoreline. The rock formation in the water is a treat to watch. However, the crowd visiting was a bit overwhelming. Hardly any place to park because of the rush. The place was very crowded. There was a restaurant next to it . Toilets in the restaurant was free to use.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Driving around Iceland you encounter many black sand beaches and this one is the bottom of the list for me. Too many tourists, you can't even admire the basalt columns because people are climbing all over them! Seems like this one is the "best" only because it is the most well known. Having already seen many other more beautiful beaches going clockwise around the Ring Road this one was a "could miss" for me. There are bathrooms available for $. Beware the sneaker waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great little detour and it's free
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Black sand, hexagonal basalt columns and lovely views. It was busy when we arrived but there was space for all of us. Children and adults enjoy climbing the basalt columns (good photo op) and the occasional puffin flies over head. There is a cafe and car park at the top of the beach. Access to the beach is free.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Highlight of the Ring Road
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The famous "Black Beach" is a must see for the ominous basalt columns and mighty North Atlantic shoreline.  The fantastic rock formations in the water give this an otherworldly vibe.  Beware the "Deadly Sneaker Waves" that have claimed the lives of foolish tourists daring Mother Nature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Black sand beach, basalt columns, and sea stacks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reynisfjara is the black sand beach, and Rejnisdrangur is the sea stacks off the beach. Both are lovely. We went down the road marked by the sign to Reynisfjara, off the Ring Road close to Vik. There's a road to Rejnisdrangur a bit up the road. We parked on the shoulder of the road and walked the rest of the way. This was a somewhat busy place. There's a small cafe and paid bathrooms. The walk along the beach was very nice. There are basalt columns in the cliffs. Very pretty. The beach is both black sand and small, very smooth, very round rocks. The sea stacks are at one end of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is special and a must see. However it is so crowded that it can be unbearable at some times. We stayed in a cottage not 100 yards from this beach and the owner told us to go after 10 pm because it would still be light(June) and there would hardly be anyone there. He was right. We had the best time exploring and taking pictures of those elusive puffins! It is a wondrous place and we made a point to go there two nights in a row!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice stop on the drive around Iceland. The black sand and volcanic rock formations are very unique. Great pictures.

reviews.title: Cool beach and scenery, though we preferred Diamond Beach further to the east; do yourself a favor and make that drive
reviews.text: It's cool to see and the rock walls and intense waves are impressive, but Diamond Beach 2.5 hours to the east is way more appealing. This is fine as a quick stop, with sufficient facilities and parking. It's just before Vik if coming from Reykjavik. Does the job if you have time to only visit one black-sand beach.

reviews.title: Worth a visit - beautiful beach
reviews.text: Lovely walk along the black sand beach, right next to town of Vik where we stayed on our first night of our Iceland road trip!You do have to pay for parking (£6).Definitely worth a visit especially if you’re a GOT fan.Be aware of the weather warnings and sneaker waves so don’t get too close to the water.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: This beach is absolutely beautiful. The black sand beach and rock formations makes for great pictures. This beach is also very dangerous because of the waves.

reviews.title: a beach to see
reviews.text: Beautiful beach l mysterious atmosphere, another planet, even if there are plenty of people, a beach to see.................................................

reviews.title: Nice but dangerous!
reviews.text: It is a very beautiful beach with black sand, but also one of the most dangerous in the world.If the light is green or yellow, and there is low tide, besides the basalt columns you can see the cave.Even if the sign is green or yellow, you should never neglect the waves or get too close, and if the light is red, never enter.

reviews.title: A fantastic black sand beach with a DEADLY risk.
reviews.text: A fantastic experience, one which should certainly not be overlooked.Reynisfjara is a beach with pure black sand, an impressive array of basalt columns near to the shoreline and basalt caves. Reynisfjara actually being one of the filming locations used within the Game of Thrones series.A great place to gather some seriously impressive photographs! But please be aware that Reynisfjara is NOT a place twhich should be underestimated; countless people have died at Reynisfjara  over the years after being swept out to the ocean; the authrorities have as such introduced a traffic light system to advise visitors to the beach. Be extremely careful on the beach, especially if visiting with young children; the ocean water is extremely powerful and sneaker waves are DEADLY. NEVER turn away from the ocean waves and always be aware especially if with young children.The first visit was during an Icelandic orange weather warning for high wind, wind gusts were recorded near to 40mph and this made it very difficult/dangerous to move around, especially with the beach traffic light system flashing red.The second visit was more successful, with the beach lights flashing amber. I attach some photographs.Happy travels but STAY SAFE.

reviews.title: Black beach
reviews.text: A spectacular and almost unreal place! Black sand, perfectly geometric basalt columns and Reynisdrangar rock formations emerging from the sea create a breathtaking panorama. The atmosphere is powerful and wild, especially with the Atlantic wind and rushing waves. Warning: waves can be very dangerous. Signs warn you to always stay away from the shore because the “sneaker waves” arrive suddenly. It's not a place to swim, but it's perfect for walking, taking spectacular photos and admiring the force of Icelandic nature.

reviews.title: Stunning black sand beach
reviews.text: ITs like you are in different planet, Iceland you stunning beautiful country and ruthless weather makes it so beautiful and amazing, never seen such varied landscapes. This beach is so beautiful and extremely dangerous waves., when we visited it was yellow warning due to rain, we stayed bit far from huge waves crashing to the shores, The black sand, basalt columns, and powerful waves make Reynisfjara one of the most stunning beaches I’ve ever seen. but request people to be extremely cautious about the waves. Heard many people died so ensure be cautious about your surroundings and kids. Take care of them:)

reviews.title: Magnificent!
reviews.text: This place was my favorite spot of what we saw in Iceland. The power of the ocean was just astounding. The red light signifying dangerous sneaker waves was on when we were there, so we didn’t go on the beach, although that didn’t stop a lot of people, I saw one woman fall when the waves came up quickly, luckily she managed to get up. But the scenery was just amazing. The black sand and the white ocean foam against the cliffs was truly memorable. Not to be missed.

reviews.title: Nice waves
reviews.text: Nice black sand beach and big gorgeous waves. We parked a bit far away because it was not clear which parking to use. The 1000 ISK parking cost is common.

reviews.title: The most crowded spot in Iceland?
reviews.text: This is just about the most crowded place we visited in Iceland. The car park is a decent size but was still overflowing, and there were bus loads and bus loads of people arriving every minute.Park, take the short walk and it’s there. Spectacular black sand, and some great rock formations on the beach, and just offshore.With a little patience and positioning decent photos are possible, despite all the idiots taking the warning signs as an instagram challenge.Plenty of toilets, and there’s a large cafe and souvenir shop.

reviews.title: Amazing place!
reviews.text: Amazing location and views! Basalt columns and caves are exceptional! We were glad that we went there during low tides as we were able to view the columns and caves well.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach with signature rocks
reviews.text: Visited the famed Black sand beach toward end of our long road trip on a windy and wet day, typical of September in this island. The beach has signature black rocks that are instantly recognizable in any picture of the beach. A red light was flashing at the entrance warning the visitors of the high waves and dangerous tides that are a serious threat to anyone. There is a cave there, which is also a danger zone when the light is flashing. I could not spend much time there due to high winds, but for some it was perfectly fine to take a stroll on the beach as I found. I have seen many award winning pictures of the beach, when beautiful puffins come to play during summer. On our way back from the nearby village Vik, we saw the beach and the rocks from the opposite direction, which was equally mesmerizing. The beach is about two and half to three hours drive straight from the capital. A must see when in Iceland.

reviews.title: Take your time to enjoy
reviews.text: The drive to the beach is beautiful. 2 parking areas with paid parking (of course…). It’s quite a long beach but everyone will concentrate on the cave and hexagonal columns. We had a hotdog and a drink and sat on the rocks to just enjoy a beautifully warm sunny day. After this, we walked to the cave to admire the structures and walked around the rest. Of course everyone ignores the warnings and areas you should not stand but hey…. Everyone survived to see another day. I am sure there are more beautiful beaches around but the surroundings are stunning and in general it is a nice beach. We spent about an hour here just sitting in the sun

reviews.title: REINSFJARA
reviews.text: Amazing View surrounded by the powerful Atlantic Ocean 🔥🔥🔥🔥I will visit it again on November see the winter also,the northern lights, the black sand beach!!
