reviews.title: Black sandy beaches of Iceland
reviews.text: This black sandy beach is quite popular. Located on the south coast of Iceland. Close to the small town of Vik. One of the interesting ones besides its black sand is the formations of granite tabs on a pretty instagrammable shore edge and several clusters of reefs associated with Troll fairy tales.When we were there the weather was muddy with a pretty strong wind. When the weather is very bad it may be forbidden to enter the coastal area.

reviews.title: Over rated beach
reviews.text: Spent a week touring Iceland 12 days ago. This beach was the most overrated spot we visited and it wasn’t close. Vikurfjara was nearby  and far superior without the crowds.

reviews.title: Lots of visitors
reviews.text: Lots of warnings about the dangers of this beach and sneaker waves !Still see plenty of peopleIgnoring advice but we didn’t !Never underestimate the power of the ocean !Lots of tourists but a pretty location

reviews.title: Crazy rude tourists
reviews.text: Enjoyable experience with fantastic scenery and atmosphere.  Well signposted as well as warnings about the obvious dangers of getting too close to the waves.  Sadly many tourists ignored this. One was lucky not to get caught by an unexpected wave.  Two other foreign tourists were arguing with a tour guide who was warning them about the risks.  Crazy. Just take care

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: After reaching the end of the road you arrive...in the car park...paying (toilets available)!From the parking you are 50 m and you are on a beautiful black sandy beach!Along the cliff you will arrive in a lava cave but be careful not to be surprised by the waves!!!You will also see many puffins flying overhead.The cliff and its basalt columns are impressive.In short superb place, very touristy

reviews.title: Dramatic and Unforgettable
reviews.text: The black sand, basalt columns, and powerful waves make Reynisfjara one of the most stunning beaches I’ve ever seen. Truly unique and a must-visit in Iceland!

reviews.title: Extraordinary experience
reviews.text: A unique and fascinating experience that cannot be missed by those who want to experience the incredible geology of this fantastic country. It is advisable to follow the warning signs.

reviews.title: Reynisfjara Beach - Black sand beach Iceland
reviews.text: Reynisfjara Beach found in South Iceland, is a very popular Black Sand Beach. Nearby one can also see a cave made from Basalt.. the black sediments have been formed by the hot lava.It is advised not to swim or go close to the waters due to strong currents and heavy unpredictable waves.

reviews.title: Busy location but a unique site
reviews.text: Great beach with a cave and unique balsalt pillars. The beach is a mix of pebbles and black sand and has a restaurant, hot dog stand and washroom facilities.

reviews.title: Must See Black Stone Beach
reviews.text: Beautiful scenery - from the basalt columns to the volcanic beach. This beach has thousands of perfectly smooth black stones - the kind that spas who offer hot stone treatments use. Heed the warnings and steer well clear of the water. As recently as August 2nd, a 9-year-old was swept out to sea and drowned. As with many Iceland tourist spots, they charge for parking, but the bathrooms are free. If you have time, drive about 12 minutes east of the beach to the small town of Vik. Drive up to the church for a nice view.

reviews.title: Dangerous beach. Recommend reading news articles about beach safety before you go. Read warning signs at beach
reviews.text: Beach is scenic but not always safe. There are warning signs and warningLights but they are not prominent across the beach - people can access the beach without seeing them. Suggest you research before going on beach especially with young family (read news articles about the danger) -Many locals are calling for more protection and warnings.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Lots of signs to the area that help with navigation. A couple different parking lots near there for parking which you need to pay for using the parka app. There’s a cafe and bathroom on site. The sand is absolutely beautiful and so cool to see. Definitely a crowded touristy spot but for good reason. The cave area and mountains are stunning and watching the waves crash on the black sand beach are great! It’s important to be safe and not stand too close to the water in case of sneaker waves

reviews.title: The force of the sea
reviews.text: Black gravel beach, with cliff of basaltic columns, in which nest puffins. It is not advisable to approach the shore, the waves can be very dangerous.

reviews.title: A unique landscape to look out for
reviews.text: The beach offers a unique landscape, with black sand of volcanic origin joining the square basalt cliffs that give a unique whole. You can also take a short walk, among caves and pebbles, while always remaining attentive to the sea, whose level changes quickly and can be dangerous if not monitored.

reviews.title: Iconic tour of Iceland
reviews.text: After arriving in the car park -for a fee-, about fifty meters separate you from the black sand beach (Black Sand Beach), a strip of black sand with magnificent rolls of raging sea borders a cliff where puffins (shearwaters) nest, basalt structures carve this cliff Game Of Throne way (fans will recognize the place) with a cave type depression (no depth but an important vault. The place was really spectacular despite the wind blowing that day. Visit to do for the unusual side of the place

reviews.title: A beautiful beach with exciting cliffs
reviews.text: It was probably the black stones on the beach that gave the beach its name, but it was the exciting rocks I was fascinated by.It is 2 parking spaces and P2 is a bit cheaper than P1. Then you get a little longer walk walk from P2.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: I went with high expectations but it is one of the places that least impressed me in Iceland. When I visited there was a green flag so there was no danger.It is very crowded and it is better to visit very early in the morning to find the beach alone. Parking costs 7 euros.

reviews.title: Fun place to visit near Vik
reviews.text: This is the world famous black sand beach located at the end of Rt 215 south of the Ring Road near Vik. There are a couple of different carparks to manage the crowds that visit here each day. The closest P1 carpark fees start at 1000kr per vehicle while the P2 lot which is further back on the road starts at 750kr per vehicle. Reynisfjara is where you see the deep black sand and pebbles formed from cooled volcanic lava broken down by Atlantic Ocean waves over the centuries. It is a beautiful place to visit but also known for dangerous sneaker waves. There are warning signs to not turn your back to the sea at Reynisfjara and to always be cautious of rogue waves that show up out of nowhere. In addition to the black sand beach, you can also enjoy gorgeous basalt column cliffs along the beach, the fun Hálsanefshellir Cave and iconic Reynisdrangar basalt sea stacks out at sea off extending beyond Reynisfjall (mountain). Also make sure to look up at the seabirds making use of the cliffs here, many of them are puffins which you can view quite nicely with a pair of decent binoculars.

reviews.title: Beautiful, wild, pristine, great view of the Reynisdrangar columns
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with fine black sand. At the western end high cliffs with many breeding birds (even puffins). Wonderful view of the Reynisdrangar cliffs

reviews.title: Beautiful black beach
reviews.text: This stunning black sand beach is known for its dramatic caves and striking rock formations. Be cautious, as the high tide brings in powerful, unpredictable waves—it’s strongly advised not to get too close to the water. The beach is about a two-and-a-half-hour bus ride from the city. While it’s a long journey, the scenic drive and the beauty of the beach make it well worth the trip.

reviews.title: Sneaker wave almost took someone away! Beautiful columns and black sand.
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with towering basalt columns you can climb on. This place is definitely worth a visit. There is a cave back away from the sand that is easy to access, and a cave around the corner with basalt columns inside that can be iffy depending on tides. The sneaker waves really should be watched out for. When we first arrived, we saw a little girl almost get swept away. She was barely saved by her father, who caught her hand as she fell. Be cautious and don’t get too close to the water. There is a sandbar that stretches out to the right that you can walk on sometimes. Overall a beautiful spot for pictures, but keep an eye on the water and don’t try to swim.

reviews.title: A beach with geological formations.
reviews.text: It’s a black sand beach near Dirholey arch. There is typical basalt rock formation. It’s a a peculiar looking specially for common people. There are two caves. One of them is easy accessible. The ceiling is high but the cave is small. But the other cave is little away from this but accessible only on low tide as the beach at that position is under water and the path for its access is rocky. This cave is of low ceiling but deep in. In the cave the basalt rock is in other direction. In the distance several rock formations are seen in the Atlantic Ocean. This place is a tourist hotspot. Several picturesque sites are here. We loved this place. Also so many tourists gather here.

reviews.title: Black beach
reviews.text: A few minutes away from Vik, you park and you are on an immense black beach often with strong wind and sea waves that go even far ahead with the risk that some inattentive tourist can be dragged away given the strong undertow; beautiful basalt columns that form a sort of natural sculpture.If you want to take pictures a little more solo it is better to walk to the opposite end of the beach in order to be more alone and appreciate the beach at its best.

reviews.title: One of my favorite places
reviews.text: This is truly one of my favorite places in Iceland. There is something almost otherworldly about it - the black sand, the crashing waves, the basalt columns and the strange, eerie spires jutting out of the sea.  When we got there, it was windy and grey, which just added to some of the mystique, but then suddenly the sun came out! Weather can really change on a dime here.This was also one of my kids' favorite places; they loved exploring the cave, scrambling up the columns and watching the waves and seeing how far the surf would get (the waves can be quite dangerous and are best observed from a distance!) - we had an amber day so there were a few times it even got close to their shoes despite that!We could even see plenty of puffins nesting in the square rocks above us.  It's a great place to visit in all types of weather. It's clear why this has been used in so many fantasy or sci-fi movies (Game of Thrones, Rogue One, etc) but it just goes to show what our own world can offer.

reviews.title: Beautiful.
reviews.text: You arrive in a large parking lot, for a fee like everyone else in Iceland. Which I find right, there are available bathrooms and the signage is very neat. On the beach you have to pay close attention to the sea and the warning signs because the waves can be very strong and dangerous. If the sea is calm and shallow you can take a walk on the left between black sand, basalt rocks and sheer cliffs. The sea is very suggestive and the cliffs, full of birds, are also beautiful. There were a lot of people but not everyone continues to the left and you can have some peace. I recommend it

reviews.title: Must do, go early or late in the day
reviews.text: Go early morning, or late at day/evening, as it is crowded. But indeed the rock formations are very nice. When entering the beach, also go left (keep walking), and eventually go over the big boulders / rocks, no crowd and great view to the formations  in the sea.

reviews.title: Incredible sight columns, black sand and haystack rocks
reviews.text: We absolutely enjoyed this experience. There  is plenty of parking. The sand is volcanic black. The waves are rough and make a crashing sound. There are basalt columns and caves. Game of throne vibes. We enjoyed walking around taking pics. Its goes on for miles.

reviews.title: Encounter with a seal
reviews.text: We head to take some pictures, I remember that the beach is potentially dangerous for unexpected waves, while we are distracted and attracted by the wonder that surrounds us at some point from the shore emerges the head of a seal almost to greet us, a surreal meeting that I will always carry in my travel memory, I wish visitors the same luck and promptness that I did not have in taking the photo of this cute subject!

reviews.title: Top location - definitely worth seeing!
reviews.text: Wonderful beach with black sand, great views of the southernmost point of Iceland, beautiful basalt columns, a surf cave and views of rock needles in the sea. Very good infrastructure with parking, toilets and restaurant.

reviews.title: A Dangerous Black Sand Beach with a Magical Atmosphere.
reviews.text: We visited Reynisfjara black sand beach in Vik as part of South Coast, Diamond beach & Jokulsarlon tour by Gray Line Iceland - booked at a discounted rate through Get Your Guide.  This beach has been voted by National Geographic as one of the top -10 non-tropical beaches to visit on the planet and has been featured in Game of Thrones Season 7The lava that flowed into the ocean during volcanic eruptions were cooled by ocean water and broken down over time by powerful waves resulting in the black sand we see on the beach today.Although beautiful to look at , this is an extremely dangerous location due to sneaker waves - strictly adhere to the safety precautions posted. The visitor center has rest rooms, a Kronan grocery store where you can get a good variety of packed food (they have even provided a microwave outside the store to heat up the purchased food) an overpriced  restaurant and a cafe

reviews.title: Black sand, crashing waves.
reviews.text: Spectacular day trip. About 2.5 hours from Reykjavik, so leave early in the day. The crashing waves are quite dangerous, so pay attention so as not to get sucked away. Nature is awesome.

reviews.title: A beautiful beach
reviews.text: A beautiful pebble beach and black sand. It is cold and windy but the scenery is worth a visit. We spent 2 hours with our daughters admiring the sea and climbing the rocks.

reviews.title: towering basalt columns
reviews.text: Located near the village of Vík on Iceland’s South Coast, Reynisfjara Beach is not your typical sun-and-sand destination — it’s bold, mysterious, and fiercely beautiful. With its jet-black volcanic sands, towering basalt columns, and roaring Atlantic waves, this beach feels like a scene from a fantasy film (and actually has been, featuring in Game of Thrones and Star Wars).

reviews.title: Best beach in Iceland
reviews.text: Iceland’s famous Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach does not disappoint. This beach is one of the most famous attractions in Iceland and I can see why. Its rock formations with the basalt columns are brilliant and its small cave is not really a cave but still really great. The beach stretches to another great attraction called Dyrholaey which you can see in the distance. The beach also has a large lake separating fresh water from salt water. Reynisfjara is also the most dangerous beach in Iceland with its famous sneaker waves. The water slaps against the cliff face of Reynisfjall and pushes the water creating a deadlier and faster wave which catches out many people so my advice its best to view the waves from the distance. Currently it was an amber warning while I was here and I did witness 1 or 2 sneaker waves of which tourists got caught out on. Still none-the-less its one of the most scenic spots in Iceland and it cannot be missed. The cafe here also does some great cakes.

Breathtakingly beautiful! Reynisfjara Beach in Vik, Iceland is a must-visit. The unique black sand, stunning rock formations, and powerful Atlantic waves create an unforgettable experience. A true natural wonder!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Very picturesque with a range of beautiful rock formations. Be sure to pay after book to the warnings to avoid being caught out by dangerous waves!

reviews.title: Amazing Rock Formations
reviews.text: There is so much drama here ie. the beach, the rocks, the cave and the sea. The beach is as black as it gets and rising from the sea are the Reynisdrangar basalt sea stacks situated under the Reynisfjall mountain. These are natural hexagonal basalt columns and the Halsanefshellir cave is also located on the beach.  There are warning lights indicating the danger of the powerful, and sometimes unexpected, waves which form in this area and the warnings should be strictly observed. An area not to be missed on the South Coast.

reviews.title: Dramatic waves on black sand beach.  Take note of warning lights
reviews.text: Unfortunately we were not allowed too far onto the beach as the red warning light was showing.  It was very windy and the waves were high,  We could only see the one rock column and were unable to access the basalt rock formation but we still found it strangely beautiful and an experience.   Parking is chargeable.

reviews.title: Pay attention to the warnings!
reviews.text: This place is incredibly beautiful and incredibly windy! Be very careful when you’re going around the cliffs to see the other side of the cliffs. We could barely stand up because the breeze was so severe. It’s a very beautiful place though!

reviews.title: Beautiful Yet Dangerous
reviews.text: Reynisfjara situated 10km toward west from small town of Vik, with entrance fee of ISK1000/ car/ day. It also features basalt columns, the hexagonal rock formations which are formed by cooling lava and create an impressive backdrop for the beach. The other prominent element there is Reynisdrangar sea stacks that rise dramatically from the ocean, which can also be seen from Vik. As stunning place, it also one of most dangerous sites due to the unpredictable sneaker waves, that can appear suddenly, reaching much farther up than expected. Some incidents there led to accidents, fatalities and lost. Warning signs & indicators erected throughout the area, explaining risks of sneaker waves and urge people to keep a safe distance from the shoreline.

reviews.title: A challenge in winter
reviews.text: Great rock formations, but so strong wind that you could hardly walk. And despite warning signs, some go too close to the water The waves are so fast and the pull so strong that it has blown some away. No fun emerging from the sea in sub-zero temperatures.

reviews.title: Beautiful show and awesome wind
reviews.text: Unique spectacle for the color of the sand and the big waves of the ocean. The wind was extremely impressive, you could hardly stand still. Shoot the sand that hits you during.

reviews.title: Beach with views
reviews.text: Black sand beach with interior lagoon and view of strange rock formations.There's a parking lot.They say the waters on this beach are dangerous, especially for those who get too close to shore.

reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.text: We went during end of December 2024, it was windy , very less crowds and great scenery overall .Quite amazed by the view and got some amazing drone footage !

reviews.title: Amazing view, interesting rock forms.
reviews.text: Amazing geology.Don’t forget to pay to park.There are toilets and a cafe with a small shop. Walk to beach around 100m where there is a cave with stalactites, a rock face with prisms, two outreach large rocks and a bay… I’m no geologist so can’t describe!!!The beach is long with black sand, shingle and then snow on the day we visited. Wind was low but waves were still high!!Beware lots of coach trips despite winter conditions.

reviews.title: Nice stop
reviews.text: Views are amazing. Staff is on the beach reminding people no to get too close. The waves were rough when we went later in the day.

reviews.title: Black Beach Beauty
reviews.text: Witnessing this stunning black sand beach along Iceland’s South Coast was absolutely mesmerizing, the beach is known for its natural hexagonal basalt columns, the Halsanefshellir Sea Cave, and the large rock formations that rise from the sea. I’ve never seen anything quite like this breathtaking natural landscape.However, be cautious when visiting! The area is known for sneaker waves that can crash ashore unexpectedly as shown in the signs. I experienced one myself it didn’t knock me over, or drag me, but it did soak my wellies! So, my advice is to keep a safe distance from the shoreline to stay dry and safe. I would highly recommend visiting here while in Iceland. PS: If accessing by car you will have to pay for parking there, there wasn't many signs indicating that so something to bare in mind.

reviews.title: Stunning, But Watch Out For The Waves
reviews.text: Yet another stunning site along the South Coast road. The beach is made up of small smooth black pebbles. There are nice basalt rock formations too, but as many have warned watch out for the sneaker waves they really can catch you out, seen a couple of people get their feet & legs wet.Access to the site is free, but parking was the usual 1000 ISK for a car. There is a small café/restaurant and the toilets at the side of that are free.

reviews.title: Nice beach, EVERYONE at the cave and cliffs!
reviews.text: Walking the beach was nice and calm, although look closely, as I passed a mound of sand, but on the way back, realized it was a beached whale 😳. This was winter, so no one was at the beach, although tons of people were at the cave and cliffs. Loved the view.

reviews.title: Interesting formations
reviews.text: Stopped in here as part of a 2-day South Coast tour.  The sand and basalt columns were interesting, but WAY TOO MANY tourists which completely detracted from the visit.  Many trying to climb the rock cliffs for their photos and getting in the way of everyone else, and most ignoring all the warning signs regarding the sneaker waves - saw a few get wet shoes and pants.

reviews.title: Can be Deadly
reviews.text: This beach has sneaker waves which basically means it a strong undertow that will drag you into the ocean and hold you underwater.  I grew up with waves and currents like this and was taught to never turn my back to the ocean.  I also grew up with black sand beaches.  I was taught to watch the waves and beach before entering especially with a beach that is unfamiliar.The tide looked low this the day.  We  were able to walk to the edge of the beach without the water reaching us.  This beach was beautiful and magnificent.  The ocean here is powerful.  Does it ever calm down?In November, wear your winter jacket, wind breaker and glasses.  The wind makes it feel colder.  When the wind picks up, the black sand will hit you in the face and eyes.  It hurts.It would be the one beach I recommend going to in Iceland.

reviews.title: Romantic
reviews.text: A beautiful lava beach where you can admire the sunset. It is very wide and you can find spots without other people around. At the eastern end are the famous stacks.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This is a black sand beach at Vik famous for the rock formations in the water. The beach itself and the view out to the water are very impressive. You also get a great view from the Dyrholaey lighthouse.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: This beach with its basalt columns is absolutely breathtaking! It does seem to get quite busy from sunrise, but it’s well worth it- just be super careful of Sneaker waves and pay attention to the warning lights at the entrance.

reviews.title: Magical Moments at Reynisfjara Beach, Vik
reviews.text: I visited Reynisfjara Beach in Vik this year, and it was one of the most stunning places I've ever experienced! The contrast of the black sand against the ocean, along with the towering basalt columns, created a truly magical atmosphere. The Reynisdrangar sea stacks were breathtaking, and I loved learning about the local legends surrounding them.While the beach can get crowded at times, it’s easy to find a spot to soak in the beauty and take photos. Just a friendly reminder to be cautious of the waves—they can be surprisingly strong, so it’s best to keep a safe distance.Overall, Reynisfjara is a must-see in Iceland. It left me in awe, and I can’t recommend it enough!

reviews.title: incredible beach
reviews.text: very spectacular beach with impressive rocks and columns like giant causaway in northern ireland. but the huge waves could be very dangerous.

reviews.title: Traitory and dangerous beach!
reviews.text: Reynisfjara is a beautiful black sand beach of volcanic origin. It is located near Vik. In addition to the black sand, there are basalt columns and two rocks in the ocean. The landscape is splendid, but all care is little, as this beach is best known for being dangerous and treacherous. The strong, unexpected waves and the cold water can be fatal.

reviews.title: Increible
reviews.text: The black beach is a truly stunning place, where you can admire majestic basalt columns, volcanic rocks and a dark colored sand that gives a special touch to the landscape. This natural environment is a wonderful one as you can see ducks, seals and seagulls that live in the area. The panoramic views it offers are amazing.

reviews.title: Cool, but can be VERY BUSY
reviews.text: Cool spot, but VERY touristy and crowded. Caution signs up, but 95% of people seemed to ignore them. Coffee shop & WC, but line too long. Paid parking, but not clear on how to pay. Beach was awesome with varied sized black pebbles and cool rock features & basalt columns. Would like to return early am or pm when less crowded & no buses/tours.

reviews.title: Interesting, but skip the cave/recess for safety and read the signs/warning lights
reviews.text: This was my second visit.  I strongly recommend going with a guide or organized tour because 1.  you learn so much more about the geology, folklore associated with the site and 2. guides know how to assess and guide you safely at this very high risk site.  I enjoyed this visit more (our first was on our own) because our guide taught us so much, and safely guided us in AND rapidly out of the basalt recessive area.  Tourists/visitors really have no clue how dangerous the waters are.  Despite our tour guide giving detailed safety information about this site (in no fewer than 5 different languages) I saw multiple people from our group disregard the information and walk down to the water line.  It is very deceptive - smooth flat beach, 20 minutes of calm waves - then BAM!  One hits out of the blue and knocks someone over.  What happens next is random - you may be able to scramble to your feet and escape or a second one can drag you out, where hypothermia and frozen limbs and wave surges stop you from being able to emerge again.   It is not worth that selfie.  Tread carefully at this site - and most of all, don't do something because everyone else is.  Most visitors are clueless about outcomes here.  There were many people at risk I saw.    Keep your distance.

reviews.title: A beach of a different kind
reviews.text: Black beach, not sand, white foamy waves, amazing sculptures made of stone. Just beautiful. However, one must be very cautious about the sneaker waves warning system before entering the beach. Those waves are really dangerous!

reviews.title: Stunning, a absolute must see!
reviews.text: Beautiful jet black, soft sand and the foaming ocean waves create a dramatic scene. We went early in the morning so not many people on the beach. The sunrise was incredible. The basalt columns that backed the beach were stunning. Be careful of the waves. They can catch you off guard. A quick drive from Vik.

reviews.title: Dramatic Landscape - worth the trip
reviews.text: The contrast between the jet black, soft sand and the foaming ocean waves is very dramatic. When we went the ocean waves were raging which added to the experience. It was very crowded but most people hang out near the rock face and don't venture too close to the water so if you step out, get near the incoming waves, you have more space to yourself. Easy drive from Vik.

reviews.title: Mother nature power
reviews.text: Awesome black beach in South Island coast.This beach is sadly famous for its dangers, since often sneaker (or killer) waves swallow visitors into the cold ocean, leaving no hope when the beach becomes far.The sights make you speechless, with the amazing troll rocks and the basalt formations creating a cavern.Do follow the traffic light indications before entering the beach and never turn your shoulders to the sea for a selfie.... it could be you last one!

reviews.title: Black sand and rock formations
reviews.text: It was fun to explore the beach and different rock formations. We went during a “yellow light” period, meaning that the sneaker waves were there, but not large enough to close the beach.  Occasionally a wave did surprise people by coming up higher than usual on shore, but I never saw anyone get more than ankle deep.  (Still very unpleasant in the cold.)  There were very unusual rock formations that we were able to climb and a couple of shallow caves to explore.  The stop was definitely worth it to get your picture on a volcanic sand beach.

reviews.title: Beware of parking monitors
reviews.text: Amazing views of the beach! Beware of two things. Multiple people got hit by sbeaker waves. Also beware they watch you when you park and if you don't pay they see it eight away and toss you a parking ticket. Best to pay the parking for this site as they are sus here.

reviews.title: Stunning as usual!
reviews.text: This was our 2nd trip to Iceland and 2nd time in Vik area... not to stop here would be a crime :) it is busy, it is touristy, but it is also big and there is room for everyone (and even for all that paid parking too haha)We had seen this place and the basalt columns first in 2022, in 2023 we got to see similar ones in the Norther Ireland, but I like them here more - it's that cave next to them that looks like a giant prehistoric basalt mammoth is about to come out of it any moment that makes the difference :) People are sometimes people... and yes they ignore each other and get in the way... the newest silly thing I saw was people dragging bottles of the Icelandic orange soda just to have it with them on the picture.... I found that silly considering it can break easily and the glass would cut everybody around but... again people/aka tourists will be tourists... let's be mindful of each other :)

reviews.title: Black sand beach
reviews.text: Interesting and beautiful black sand beach surrounded by a landscape of mountains and stacks, not far from the waterfalls.

reviews.title: Nice views and puffins!
reviews.text: The black sand beach in Vík is something I would not rush back to do again however that being said it was nice to visit and experience. Aside from the black sand the best part of the beach is seeing a large amount of puffins on the cliffs! This was the highlight for me and the only reason that I would consider going back. I’d like to clarify that I’m not saying that the black sand beach is bad however I am saying that it is the sort of thing once you’ve been there for 10 minutes it begins to get boring. There are nice views from the beach of the cliffs and of course the puffins! I really want to stress this: BE CAREFUL OF THE SNEAKER WAVES!!!!! I saw so many people facing away from the sea taking pictures and then having to run away from the sneaker waves but you might not be so lucky… The beach is completely safe as long as you follow the rules and stay away from the waters edge so please please be careful because you don’t want to be swept out to sea! In conclusion if you are heading through Vík and want to stop somewhere come here for a bit they have a food truck and facilities for you to use whilst also providing nice views and a bit of sea air! In general not one of the key things to do in Iceland but if you have the time to drop by I would!

reviews.title: Magic beautiful
reviews.text: Incredibly photo friendly. Black beach with lots of opportunity for stone picking. High waves that fascinate. We soendered an hour hear and it was enough for us, long line to the toilets and chaotic parking

reviews.title: Nice but disappointing
reviews.text: Nice place, but crowded. There are two paid parkings, parking 2, 100m further away which costs 750isk (3 hours, if you want to add hours you must pay 750isk more every hour) or parking 1, more carca and it is the same but with cost of 1000isk. By 8:20 am it was already full of tourists taking pictures without being able to see it pretty. Yesterday afternoon, at 18h anyway, many people climbed the rocks. If you want loneliness, 8am at the latest.

reviews.title: Unique Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: Unique Black Sand Beach with incredibly powerful waves crashing on the shore. The cave also makes for an impressive photo shoot.

reviews.title: Unique and beautiful beach
reviews.text: Absolutely unique and stunningly beautiful. The black sand, cave, unique rock structures and puffins flying above.Please be aware it can be very dangerous so be aware of the ocean and warning signs to alert you to conditions.

reviews.title: Worth a Stop, but Not Your Typical Beach
reviews.text: Very impressive rock formations and stone wall which are definitely worth seeing, and the ocean is quite powerful, so keep your eye on it and stay away from it! But, this is hardly a beach, since you can’t swim here or even go near the water nor even sit since the shoreline is extremely rocky. It’s nothing like the black sand beaches in Hawaii where the sand is granular and powdery and you can actually sit or lay on it, just like any other beach, and enjoy your day. Nevertheless, it’s definitely worth seeing, but don’t think that you’re going to “spend a day or a few hours at the beach” because you’ll snap a few pictures, use the restrooms and be on your way.

reviews.title: Amazing.
reviews.text: It is totally worth the visit. In August it is crowded but to see those rocky walls so different and the completely black sand is amazing. You have to pay parking, 1000cr, there is toilet.

reviews.title: Unique experience
reviews.text: This is such a unique experience! The basalt columns and cave are very cool to see up close. Climbing up a couple of columns makes for a great photo op!  There is some interesting folklore about the basalt rock formations located in the water near the shore. Keep an eye out for puffins, they like to gather on the rocks above the cave. There is a cafe,  and restrooms are available.

reviews.title: Black beach with rain
reviews.text: Ring Road stage: one of my favourite stages. Immense basalt columns. Very black beach. We were there during a bad rainy day unfortunately, but it made everything more suggestive. Parking is charged with the Parka app. Check the traffic lights before going down to the beach! Look up too, despite the rain was full of Puffins!

reviews.title: Great rock formations and black beach, can get crowded
reviews.text: This is a popular beach with black sand and a neat cave with rock formations over to the side. Quick tips: there is a cost to park here, so be sure to factor that in. There is food nearby but it is not cheap. This place can get very busy relative to other spots. Be aware of the dangerous waves when on the beach and exercise caution unlike others who go onto the rocks waiting to be swept in. We barely spent 15 min here which wasn't worth it for us with the paid parking and there are much better things to see, so the second time around we can skip it. Please kindly indicate if you found this review to be helpful!

reviews.title: Great beach with puffins
reviews.text: Very very nice beach. In our case he was very calm, but the weather also played along. We have seen a lot of puffins but also the beach itself is very nice. You just have to follow the rules and not get too close to the water.

reviews.title: You just have to get there early enough...
reviews.text: ... because there is no other solution to the tourist crowd. Oneself - myself included - is part of the phenomenon when one shows up there. If you get there before 10 a.m. during the week, it goes and you can also find one or the other 10-second window to take a photo of the basalt formations without tourists on it. With a bit of shouting and the request to wait a moment longer with the climbing it is also possible. Parking costs (of course) another thousand. If you walk about 200 meters east or west you are alone. Interesting phenomenon, because everyone apparently just wants to take a crawl photo in the basalt and then disappear again. Good restaurant & cafe and you can sit wonderfully outside on the terrace. When I was there it was windless and no sign of waves, let alone anything with killer waves. But the danger seems real and the problem is the low water temperature of the North Atlantic. Even in summer, in 5 degrees cold in the water, your strength leaves after 15-20 minutes.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and rock formations
reviews.text: You need to pay for parking through the app. It's a short walk to the beach and cave where you can see the rock formations. We took a lot of photos there.

reviews.title: impressive
reviews.text: Impressivea show for the senses, unique. no bathrooms allowed, logical.There is an access control or traffic light that tells you the risk at the time of the visit

reviews.title: Witness the force of nature here
reviews.text: You can witness the power of nature here. The sneaker waves are real and, of course, you see people getting way too close to the water. I enjoyed the black sand and rock formations but wonder why you have to pay for parking when there are other black sand beaches that you can visit for free.

reviews.title: Short stop. Expensive parking
reviews.text: We wanted to stop here because of Game of Thrones “cave”. The beach parking was expensive since we only spent a few minutes here. Waves can be dangerous so beware. They are called “sneaker waves”.

reviews.title: Give yourself time.
reviews.text: Very interesting, black sand, hexagonal colums, further down are two caves to the left, the trolls rock stacks and arch stone at the far end of the beach.We went with the south Iceland tour, well worth the money.  We would return and take our time, but for the first visit great and very helpful to have safety information from the tour guide.The waves are so strong and long, they sweep far in and have killed many people, be careful!!.

reviews.title: Beautiful but too busy
reviews.text: Impressive black beach with a beautiful view. Too bad about the overload of tourists. It was not high season and yet it was far too busy. People also venture far too far and do not adhere to the regulations. The beach on the other side of the rock “Vikurfjara Blach Sand Beach” is equally beautiful and we were almost alone there!

reviews.title: Geologically awesome
reviews.text: Still surprised how many people get far too close to the shore line despite it being known for its dangerous sneaker waves.   Keep your distance and enjoy the amazing geology on show.  As an aside the toilet/cafe block is a fabulous black architectual delight, so in keepign with the surroundings.

reviews.title: Dangerous but beautiful
reviews.text: Yes, there are warnings. Yes, there are dangerous sneaker waves. Yes, there are even traffic lights showing the intensity of danger.And what do a lot of tourists? They ignore it and get wer or - die in the current. So the warnings not to turn your back to the ocean is true. For the time we were there (which was about an hour so) three people got very wet, one was fully covered by the wave.Nevertheless the beach is simply beautiful: black pebbles and a stunning stone cave. Maybe you try to avoid the tourist buses which is not easy. But even with them you can find a spot for yourself.You need to pay a parking fee of 1000 ISK, which is about 8 Euros. There are toilets and a restaurant.Maybe Bring some clothes in case you get wet.

reviews.title: Black Beach / Basalt cliff
reviews.text: Strong Sneaker waves also known as killer waves , capable of draging you into the deep cool sea to your death if you are too close, the sand looks beautiful n safe but deadly. The peebles are beautiful and soft & shiny with different sizes. The cliff are basalt column. There is a bar/ restaurant , check the prices before you order, a bit expensive.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: A very beautiful beach. 🖤 But It was very crowded when me and my best friend were there... but is worth a visit definitely.

reviews.title: Beach with basaltic columns
reviews.text: This famous beach with black sand and notable basaltic formations attracts tourists a lot. We must not forget that the sea here is dangerous, with waves that have given more than a few upsets to reckless tourists.

reviews.title: Tourist trap
reviews.text: Take care. It´s just a beach like many other beaches in Iceland. You have to pay for the car park but they don´t show that on the road to the parking.  So you drive on a public road and without notice you end up on a payed parking. Payment only by internet and without invoice. Tourist trap I never will visit again. Iceland is a nice country but too many tourists and greedy icelandic companies are destroying it as a tourist destination.

reviews.title: Incredible!
reviews.text: The most incredible beach! The black sand, the powerful surf and the dramatic basalt columns are truly a sight to behold. Just be sure to keep a safe distance from the water as the currents are very dangerous.

reviews.title: Great service.
reviews.text: The staff are very nice and extremely supportive during the stay. Everything! The staff, the room, the food at the bar, the location.

reviews.title: Stunningly beautiful
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful, the sea stacks and crashing waves were amazing, highly recommend, one of the best beaches I have visited.

reviews.title: A Mighty Beach…..Reynisfjara Beach
reviews.text: When one thinks of the beach our thinking normally is synonymous with beach chairs, swimwear, and beach towels.  However, a visit to Reynisfjara Beach will be an experience quite different from a normal beach day but one that is extremely memorable.  Reynisfjara Beach is located on the South Coast of Iceland in the town of Vik approximately two and a half hours from downtown Reykjavik.  The first rule for visiting Reynisfjara Beach is to remember that there are rules that must be followed due to the sneaker waves which have such magnitude that an individual can be easily swept out into the ocean.  It is often said to never turn your back on Reynisfjara Beach and to keep a safe distance of 100 feet.  There is also a warning system that is the color of a traffic light to remind tourists to exercise caution at all times.  Reynisfjara Beach is a site to behold and I can understand why it was featured in a Season of Game of Thrones.  The basalt columns are amazing to behold.  Iceland is the land of fire and ice and these columns allow one to see firsthand volcanic rock that is formed from the solidification of molten lava.It is said that basalt is resistant to erosion and weathering.  Many people come to this beach to take photographs of the amazing basalt columns and to observe in awe the work of Mother Nature.  Visiting Reynisfjara Beach was one amazing moment; however, one must remember that safety is paramount so be careful because the waters along Reynisfjara Beach have the potential to be unpredictable, dangerous, and powerful.  Proceed with caution!

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Huge magnificent placeHuge black sand beachGreat sunriseObviously quite touristyToll parking

reviews.title: Must See
reviews.text: My visit to Reynisfjara Beach in June was magical, thanks to the near 24-hour daylight of Icelandic summer. The dramatic black sands and towering Reynisdrangar sea stacks added to the beach's otherworldly charm. The extended daylight allowed for more time to enjoy the beautiful scenery and watch the native seabirds, including the adorable puffins. While the beach was busy, it still offered moments of tranquility. Respecting the beach's powerful nature and adhering to safety guidelines was crucial, but it didn't diminish the awe-inspiring experience. Overall, Reynisfjara in June was a breathtaking and unforgettable experience

reviews.title: A beach of black pebbles and rocks
reviews.text: Cold & windy day but beautiful!  LOTS of tourists and most of them stayed back from the big waves.  A few times people had to run for it.  A few tips-parking is tight and not free.  Find the sign to pay for it.  Dress warm!  It is cold & windy!To future tourists-please don’t sit each of your children on the basalt columns and take 15 min photo shoots of each kid when people are waiting for pictures as well.  Be polite!

reviews.title: very nice
reviews.text: You will feel like you are in another world on this beautiful beach. In winter there is a nice contrast between the white snow and the black sand. beautiful

reviews.title: One of real musts
reviews.text: I rarely use "must see" in my reviews, but Reynisfjara is that for sure.It's located in the middle of the southern Iceland coast, almost at the most southern tip. You can easily reach it by paved road at which end is a paying big parking lot.Have in mind it's one of the most tourist places on entire island so expect huge crowds.The beach is just amazing, no wonder it's voted one of the worldwide top ten.And, I say that after visiting it on the worst day we had in Iceland.It was raining all day, clouds to ground with very strong winds putting black sand into our faces and clothes and roaring crushing big waves. But, that also left a deep impression of mother nature power. So, no matter how's the weather do come here and visit. Just follow the rules many others pointed out in terms of approaching the sea and dangerous sneaker waves.I can only imagine (and see from pics of other travelers how it's on a sunny day).Reynisfjara is one of reasons we'll be back in Iceland, hopefully in better weather.

reviews.title: An amazing sight
reviews.text: No trip to Iceland is complete without visiting Reynisfjara beach. The Black Sand Beach. At least for first-timers.It's a very long stretch of sand. Black in colour because of the volcanic stone/soil. There are also amazing cliffs and stacks/rock formations in the sea.On the east end you'll find the carpark, the visitor center and all the facilities. Parking comes with a fee, the beach is free to enter. Many folks just rush to the stacks, cliffs and cave. But take your time if possible. Take in the breathtaking scenery. Take a walk towards the west. As far as you like. You could actually walk all the way to the Dyrhólaey útsýnisstaður (the arch). We walked about 45min to the west. Just met two more visitors. It's peaceful and quiet. Most visitors won't walk away further than 3min. It's really too bad, since this is a major attraction and takes time to appreciate.It really is amazing as people say. Something you need to see. Even though busy and popular it's a must-do. And people come and go quickly, so you will get some nice pics if you're patient. If you don't need a sunny, pic-perfect day, choose a cloudy/rainy one to meet even less visitors.

reviews.title: Windy spot
reviews.text: This beach is so windy!  The black sand was blowing everywhere.  The waves were too rough to walk around to see cave on other side.  We thought we would get blown away!

reviews.title: Characteristic, photogenic Icelandic black sand beach
reviews.text: A black sand beach, alas not at all suitable for bathing (the sea is too perilous).  The black sand is created by the grinding of the glaciers on basalt over millennia.  Apparently black is the normal colour for sand here; gold is the unusual one for an Icelander! The beach is a photogenic location, because of the impressive basalt columns that look as though medieval builders have created the entrance to a cathedral.  Just out to sea are some basalt stacks – the Troll Rocks, said to be petrified trolls (a folk legend is attached to this).  In summer, apparently, puffins are plentiful here, but had disappeared for the winter by the time of our visit.

reviews.title: Black sand beach
reviews.text: All angles could be nice pictures. Be careful while climbing those Basalt columns, they are slippery.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: We went in very bad weather, very windy, even so it was beautiful. It seemed like we were in Game of Thrones🤣

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Magnificent black sand beach with carved stones on the beach edge. A marvel of divine creation. Parking is now paid.

reviews.title: A must see when in Iceland
reviews.text: This was definitely one of our highlights on our recent trip to Iceland. The black sand, the amazing black shallow cave, the basalt columns and jagged rocks standing in the sea…really beautiful and very dramatic. We visited around 4.30pm and there were still a lot of other visitors even in October. Free parking right next to it. Beware of the sneaker waves, they might look fun but can catch you out…you don’t want to be pulled in to the sea. Look fir the warning light system as you enter the beach. It was amber the day we visited so we didn’t walk too far down the beach. It can get very windy and cold…wear appropriate clothing.

reviews.title: Do it at sunset!!
reviews.text: This black sand with its protruding rocks from the water and the basalt boulders on the beach are impressive to see!Can be combined with Dyrholaey.Not far apart.

reviews.title: Wrong statement
reviews.text: Vik is not a fishing village. There are no harbor at Vik. Please correct. I’m often with my family in Vik, so I know. I have lived in Iceland for 67 years.

reviews.title: Too crowded
reviews.text: There are many black sand beaches in Iceland and they are less crowded than this one!   I was on a tour and it was super crowded when we were here.   The yellow warning light were flashing but people were still down close to the shore.   We were asked not to climb the basalt columns but people were all over them.   It was a bit of a turn off.   I am sure this would be so much more enjoyable at a quieter time, but I was glad to leave.

reviews.title: Absolutely surreal…
reviews.text: After stopping at lovely Vik, our wonderful Nice Travel small group tour had arrived to the highlight of our trip: Reynisfjara - The Black Beach. It is a miracle of a sight: a symphony of black volcanic ash on the beach, mighty black and golden cliffs, deep caves with whimsical mosaic of the walls inside… Looks surreal… like from another planet.

reviews.title: Reynisfjara Beach
reviews.text: A beach that does live up to the hype, though you may want to forget about sunbathing here. Stunning back sand, basalt columns, caves, rock formations, cliffs with Puffins dependent on the time of year and magnificent waves which you need to be very respectful of, though on the day I visited the amber light was on but plenty of people were in the amber restricted zone. So I joined them, making sure I was amongst those people who were furthest away from the waves. Any closer and you are asking for trouble.

reviews.title: Immense beach and basalt cliff
reviews.text: If the weather conditions are unfavorable it is considered the most dangerous beach in Iceland (upon arrival you will find a traffic light that lists the risk at that moment). In favorable conditions it welcomes you with a wide shoreline made of very fine black sand and often with cutting winds. On the left, the enormous hexagonal basaltic cliff complete with a cave contrasts with the stacks (legend says that they are Trolls petrified by the sunlight). Above, the rocky spurs welcome birds of various seabirds. To the right the beach extends to the Dyrholaer peninsula.To get there, from the SS1, turn onto the 215 and follow it to the car park( free). Always crowded, but that's normal given its popularity.

reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.text: The black beach of Reynifsjara is perhaps inappropriately considered one of the main attractions of southern Iceland. Crowded by droves of tourists, it is actually a relatively ordinary black beach with rocks overlooking the sea. In Iceland you can find much better (and perhaps with less crowds)

reviews.title: Stunning nature
reviews.text: Such a magical place. Reynisfjara has been on my bucket list for years and it was so magical to finally see it in person. The beach features stunning jet black sands, moss covered cliffs, balsaalt cliffs and puffins.They have a small parking lot which was full to the max when we came. We saw puffins on the cliffs. We spent a good couple hours here just taking in the breath taking beauty. I have seen lots of nature in my life but nothing comes close to this place. Enjoy on of Earths most stunning locations and just take in the beauty of Reynisfjara beach. It will certainly take your breath away

reviews.title: Black sands!
reviews.text: Amazing black sand beach! Easy to walk to and the parking is free. Beautiful scenery and you can see the basalt stacks. The town of Vik is worth the visit.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: A magnificent black beach, beautiful cliffs, rocks emerging from a sumptuous blue sea, the play of lights: truly magnificentPlus a few seals and puffins to add a little life to this mineral spectacle!

reviews.title: Good Photo Op
reviews.text: The black sand, basalt columns, and scenic views made this beach a good stop for a photo op.  The Black Beach Restaurant is located next to the beach parking lot and has free wi-fi.

reviews.title: The Iconic Black Sand Beach…and Puffins!
reviews.text: We visited Reynisfjara in the second week of august on a gloriously sunny morning. The tide was out and the vibes were high. We were able to see into the cave just around the corner and see the incredible rock formations alongside the basalt columns. Being able to lay on the sand and look up at the rocks almost falling at you is quite an impressive sight.It was when looking up as well that we realised the wild Atlantic puffins were nesting above us! We spent a good twenty to thirty minutes watching them coming and going from the cliffs to the sea to fish.Whilst we were present there was an amber warning light to indicate where people should avoid but sadly tourists were not paying any attention to it - it is not surprising there are so many incidents here.A great place to experience nature but respect it and also the advise of the safety information!

reviews.title: Impressive stone formations!
reviews.text: Gorgeous! Our favorite spot in Vik. Black sand beaches and beautiful stone formations. Crowds, but doesn’t feel that way in the immense space. Walk away from the parking area to truly enjoy the natural beauty.

reviews.title: An interesting and dangerous place at the same time, but there are nicer beaches on this island :)
reviews.text: An interesting and dangerous place at the same time, but there are nicer beaches on this island :)Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach (planet Eadu) is a spectacular black sand beach located on the south coast of Iceland, near the town of Vik. It is famous all over the world for its unique black sand, which was formed as a result of volcanic activity on the island.

reviews.title: A must in Iceland
reviews.text: Wonder of nature; during the day it was besieged by hordes of tourists: fortunately we stayed overnight in Vik and returned in the evening after dinner to enjoy it almost alone.

reviews.title: 15 minutes
reviews.text: 15 minute stop - car park payment via Parka App. Very busy. Expansive black sand beach and basalt columns. Done but not sure I’d go again.

reviews.title: Wild and beautiful
reviews.text: Wild and beautiful, with a strong wind blowing over the black sand, an indelible memory of our trip.

reviews.title: Pretty neat
reviews.text: We didn’t spend a lot of time here, but was pretty cool. There are great views but not a ton to do other than walk on the beach.

reviews.title: Basalt Columns
reviews.text: There are cool basalt columns here.  The waves were crashing on some rocks.  And a  few “caves”.  Two little kids were playing where the waves crashed on the rocks and they ran from it just giggling away.   It was a pleasant walk on the beach.  Lots of people though.

reviews.title: Nice beach, but impossible to pay the parking
reviews.text: The beach is nice but overrated. It's a nice black beach but there are so many people... And not much to do. You have to pay for the parking, but only possible via an App, no vending maschine. Impossible to install the App. In the end most people gave up to pay for the parking.

reviews.title: Goth beach 2023
reviews.text: A dramatic, gothically romantic seascape that can call up interest for anyone interested in geology, volcanism, puffins, or just pretty views that surprise the senses. It’s important to be careful of the times of course, though I would have preferred to stay longer, maybe walk further along the beach and climb. Maybe that’s the real measure: this was a place so interesting that I just can’t imagine not going back for more!

reviews.title: Interesting Beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with interesting basalt column formations.  Can be very windy so be prepared.  The only downside is it's extremely popular and nearly always crowded.  There even was a wedding going on during our visit.

reviews.title: Part of ring road tour
reviews.text: The black sand beach together with the halsanefshellir cave are a good geological formation to visit. You can also see the Reynisdrangar outcrops further out into the sea. Although the Reynisdrangar can be seen at the black sand beach at the shoreline of Vik, the caves and more black sand beach need to be reached by taking route 215 slightly to the west on ring road route 1. How far you can go on the beach depends on the tide.

reviews.title: Clearly the top attraction in Vik
reviews.text: This is why everyone comes here and it does not disappoint- amazing cliffs along the black Sandy shore and the rock formations in the water. Simply amazing.

reviews.title: Amazing rock formations! Came back and worth the second chance to see it!
reviews.text: Amazing rock formations! Came back and worth the second chance to see it! The weather was terrible the first night that we tried to go so we came back. It was definitely worth it. The rock formations on the cliffs are super unique.

reviews.title: Awesome but respect the warning signs
reviews.text: We went in the middle of the evening after seeing a forecast for severe gales the day that we had planned to go. I imagine that you'd get good photos at most times but the evening sun definitely helped in our case. We'd seen the warnings about sneaker waves in advance and the coloured picture warning boards looked clear enough to us. It didn't stop one large family group taking pictures with their backs to the waves and letting their toddler paddle. Luckily they only got wet shoes.

reviews.title: Amazing Visit to The Black Beach
reviews.text: The beach was stunning, very windy but a highlight of our trip.  We were careful not to get too close to the water as there were multiple warnings about sneaker waves.  My husband, adult son and my two sisters all enjoyed this one of a kind beach experience.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and great photo ops here.  Easy to get to and a nice place to walk around and check out and explore.

reviews.title: Cold and Windy
reviews.text: A bit crowded the day we went. Weather was considered mild, but as a Floridian I found it cold. Worth visiting, though.

reviews.title: Well worth seeing
reviews.text: This is a very scenic black sand beach with unique rock formations in the cliff. It’s a short drive off the main highway about 2 miles west of Vik. There’s a nice cafe next to the parking lot with good food, drinks, and seating. There are signs warning about “sneaker waves” so be careful and don’t get too close to the water.

reviews.title: Reckless Tourists
reviews.text: This is one of the most visited areas of Iceland's south coast. It is beautiful and dangerous and there have been several fatalities and injuries to tourists over the years, entirely due to recklessness by the tourists in ignoring safety warnings from signage and tour operators. There are reports every year of aggressive and threatening behaviour from tourists ignoring the advice of guides..It is the presence of a beach bar that concerns me most. It does nothing to reinforce the safety message, instead encouraging people to drink alcohol in a  much publicised danger zone. Surely this has potential to make matters worse,  dulling human perception of danger, affecting behaviour and judgement.

reviews.title: Magnificent Balt columns!
reviews.text: Part of our organized tour, we saw this stunning black sand beach in the the south coast of Iceland. The small fishing village of Vik is beside it. Unfortunately the fishing industry is not active as it once was. The dramatic landscape, the hexagonal basalt columns were magnificent to see. There is a cave called Halsanefshellir but we did not visit .

reviews.title: Nice if on your way
reviews.text: Beautiful place with stunning rock formations.However, I would not be in my absolute must in Iceland. Stop here if it's on your way to some other place.Be careful. We where there mid May, around6pm, the sneaker waves did arrive to the bottom of the rock formations.

reviews.title: Go in good weather.  Not worth it if it’s foggy.
reviews.text: We went twice, and we’re so glad we did.  We arrived first on a rainy afternoon and could see some of the beauty but could not even make out the beautiful stone buttes.  After checking into our hotel in Vik, we saw the sun peeking out and hopped back in the car to return. We were pleased we did.   Not only was the weather better but as it was later there were fewer people around. We loved dodging the sneaker waves (danger rating yellow on the day we visited) but just reveled in the beauty of the place.

reviews.title: Beautiful and unique place.
reviews.text: Be careful of sneaker waves.  Some were standing on rocks taking pictures and got knocked over and nearly pulled out.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Couple with a young child.  We went on an organised tour, as we researched the area.  Which is unsafe and should not be visited unless.with an experienced company.  The sand is black and warm,  our child stayed toward to.top away from the shoreline and.played with the sand.  Very picturesque.

reviews.title: Stunning and imposing black sand beach
reviews.text: It is a stunning black sand beach with imposing views of black rocks in the ocean, unusually shaped rocks all around and amazing views. One huge downside is the weather - the day we went there was very sunny, but the wind was so strong, you could barely stand still or keep a camera up.

reviews.title: Nice place.
reviews.text: We was there 3 weeks ago. The beautiful place for me and the best moment of all was we had a very good luck to see Orca near the beach.

reviews.title: Most wild and inspiring views on earth
reviews.text: Visiting this beach was an amazing experience. The surf is wild! If you start facing the ocean and turn counterclockwise you'll see: - Huge ocean waves- Rock formations of Reynisdrangar- Basalt columns looming over the beach- Halsanefshellier Cave- Snow-capped mountains- Black sand beach stretching out- Dyrholaey promonadeIt's one of the wildest, awe-inspiring locations I've ever seen.

reviews.title: Awe inspiring!
reviews.text: We love the sea and the coast but weren’t prepared for this! Black volcanic sand and huge waves make it a unique experience. It was worth the 3 hour drive from Reykjavík as part of the South Island tour.Don’t bring your trunks as it is unsafe to swim in.

reviews.title: Don't miss
reviews.text: From the beach to the little church it was perfect.  We went on a day after 95 mile an hour winds the waves were so powerful

reviews.title: STUNNING!
reviews.text: Stunning beach. Breathtaking views. If the weather is bad and cloudy, the beach is even more beautiful. Don’t miss this unique beach!

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: Even though it was very windy the day we went, it was so beautiful! Great views. Great cafe as well on the beach.

reviews.title: Captivating
reviews.text: Captivating view and rock formations…Just like any beautiful spots, there are lots of tourists  — very difficult to take shots without having to pixelize them. The waves can be rough, and some tourists who went too close did get quite wet. Be wary please.

reviews.title: Very Interesting Beach
reviews.text: Like most of the beaches in Iceland, the sand is black.  The views from this one are great.  You MUST be careful.  About one in every 15 waves is much larger than the rest and if you happen to be close to the water when they hit, not only will you get wet, but you risk getting pulled out to sea as the undertow is very strong.  There are signs warning people, but we saw several people getting very wet.

reviews.title: Don’t miss this
reviews.text: This is a stop that won’t take long but not to be missed. It is so dramatic and beautiful. We were there after a tremendous snowfall so the contrasts were out of this world. White snow. Black sand. Grey basalt columns. Blue sky. Roaring waves. There were lots of people so it wasn’t as peaceful as I would have liked while seaside but amazing nonetheless. The crowds helped to usher us along to our next stop. Sooo beautiful.

reviews.title: Crazy Iceland Wind made this beach even better!
reviews.text: We woke up to pouring rain and hurricane like winds.  Our ice climbing excursion was cancelled and we were left scrambling.  When the rain (but not wind) let up, we decided to drive to Reynisfjara.  While it was hardly empty, I'm guessing the weather kept most away this day.  There's so many caves and rock formations to explore and climb (and escape the wind!).  My favorite spot was just past the large cave.  There's a tricky scramble to get to what can best be described as a natural throne (view in pic).  Sitting here on my own (completely blocked from wind with no one else in sight) was one of the highlights of the whole Iceland trip.

reviews.title: Will not disappoint
reviews.text: Stunning landscape that warranted two stops (late afternoon and early morning) and neither time was a disappointment

reviews.title: Wonderful
reviews.text: Wonderful, really fantastic and beautiful. Quite some tourists but still magical views all around, really worthwile a visit.

reviews.title: Sprawling black sand beach with hexagonal basalt columns
reviews.text: The hexagonal columns were a sight to behold, as was the dark sand (it is finer and blacker in other places, e.g. on the beach in Vik!) and the hexagon-patterned cave. Beware of waves that can rush almost all the way to the columns and develop a very strong pull.

reviews.title: Mordor in Real Life
reviews.text: So ominous and foreboding, such a strange landscape, so beautiful. If you are a photographer this will be especially delightful.

reviews.title: Beach and basalt columns
reviews.text: Great beach with unique basalt columns that is a great photo op if you are able to climb up them.  Great local restaurant just up the path with tremendous fish and chips

reviews.title: Holy Cow
reviews.text: Words are not enough to describe this astonishingly beautiful water and landscape! Walking along the beach, you will see beautiful Reynisherfi basalt columns and the striking Hálsanefshellir sea cave. Off the shore you will see the Reynisdrangar pillars, dramatic rock formations that rise from the sea near the beach. I’m not going to tell you to be careful and do not get too close to the water, sneaker waves crash ashore without warning and the current is very strong, but two tourist died there this summer.

reviews.title: Unique Basalt columns
reviews.text: You should definitely visit if you're in the area and marvel at the black basalt columns next to the beach.This is a very busy spot with Tour buses stopping frequently, but there is enough space available for all to get a private photo and time to explore

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Recently came to visit this beach. Very beautiful beach that has a lot to do. There is a local restaurant with clean restrooms. There is a big parking lot to accommodate lots of vehicles. The waves at the beach are very big. Be very careful as you walk around as they are very dangerous!

reviews.title: Amazing Landscape!
reviews.text: A really impressive beach! Black sand, surrounded by enormous basalt stacks! Stunning View! Atlantic Waves are amazing but particularly dangerous, often pushing further up the beach than many would expect. You are advised to never turn their back on them, and keep a safe distance of at least 30 meters. These are called sneaker waves, and they can appear when least expected, even on incredibly still days!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach... but SO MANY people
reviews.text: Honestly, this beach is beautiful.  The basalt columns, the black sand, and the crashing waves make for some epic scenery.  And I would have loved to have taken some better photos here... if it weren't for the absolute hoards of people there.  Granted, I was one of them so I probably shouldn't complain.  But just be aware that it's nearly impossible to take any pictures without hundreds of other people in them, even in late-September.

reviews.title: A beautiful beach
reviews.text: This beach is worth the trip even in the rain. Take the Icelandic advice and DO NOT get close to the surf. The waves here are ferocious and they do not behave in a predictable manner.

reviews.title: Beautiful, but dangerous
reviews.text: Definitely one of the most spectacular places in Iceland, with soaring basalt rocks, caves, black pebble beach, seastacks ... but also treacherous and dangerous "sneaker waves" that have been the cause of death of several visitor in recent years.

reviews.title: Stunning!
reviews.text: This beach is absolutely beautiful! Plenty of photo opportunities! It can get crowded though I would love to come back closer to sunset next time!

reviews.title: black sand
reviews.text: Incredible rock formations and black sand. A nice walk to take in the coastline and the variety of eroded rock.

reviews.title: It’s crowded and nice
reviews.text: It’s ok for the fun stones and a view back towards the dyrholaey. But it looks way too crowded for this view which is good but not outstanding like the rest of the places in the area.

reviews.title: Uniquely Beautiful
reviews.text: Despite a nasty wet breeze blowing off the ocean, I made the trek down to the beach to view as much as I could.  It is a gorgeous location with cliffs of interesting shaped rocks, the "trolls" offshore, a cave area and puffins and sea birds flying all about.  I was fascinated by it all and was so disappointed we didn't have better weather in which to enjoy the beauty.

reviews.title: A Must See in Iceland
reviews.text: Said to be the world's most beautiful non-tropical beaches.  I’ve seen black sand beaches in Hawaii, but Reynisfjara takes the cake.  Unparalleled.  Caves to wander among.  Of course, you can see the iconic basalt stacks of Reynisdrangar.  Depending on the season, you can see puffins roosting in the cliffs.

reviews.title: Definitely worth a stop for this unique view.. the most dangerous beach in iceland
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and rock formations…interesting is the most dangerous beach in iceland because of sneaker waves?!  We stopped here in the rain and mist but still managed good photos.  Decent coffee shop with free toilet for customers, 200isk toilet for non customers (hot chocolate is 500isk)

reviews.title: Man of the mountain
reviews.text: 1000's of pictures i have reviewed, but none of them are of "the man of the mountain".my wife captured him in this picture just a smiling away

reviews.title: Stunning beach, great basalt pillar cliffs
reviews.text: Make sure you abide by the warning signs, this beach is dangerous but fantastic to visit. Especially in the evening with the Puffins flying from the cliffs.

reviews.title: A real pearl worth visiting
reviews.text: Unbelievable rock formations, an impressive beach ans sea views - and a huge puffin colony to discover. This site is worth even a bigger detour, and it is only a 15 min drive from Vik, so if driving along the coast anyway, be sure not to miss this. There’s also a decent lunch place/cafe near the beach.

reviews.title: NOT OVERRATED! Amazing Cave!!!
reviews.text: Had mixing feelings coming to Vik... thinking that many places may be overhyped and overcrowded at the same time - but as I learned about many stops along the way in the first couple days before arriving to Reynisfjara Beach, not only all those places are as amazing as people say but also they aren't that terribly overcrowded - and we visited in the middle of summer! The black beach, the basalt columns, the cave, the size and scale of this place... it's just a serene experience and almost hard to believe it's made by nature - it looks almost as if some some alien mammoth type of creature lived in that cave - stunning view!There are indeed many people here, but they are in many areas of easy access attractions of Iceland, but everyone takes turns at their "picture moment" and people were generally respectful of one another - plus this place is huge - look how small we all are against the cave :) TIP: there is a cute Black Beach Restaurant right by the parking lot upon arrival - not sure why people review it so poorly here on TripAdvisor but we stopped there for a coffee to warm up after crazy winds at Dyrholaey and we enjoyed it a lot - outside tables are available, "free restrooms" (looks like normally you need to pay but they were broken/unlocked) and there is also a hot dog stand - otherwise right around the mountain going east there is a cute town of Vik with more choices for food

reviews.title: Puffin paradise!,
reviews.text: 2 magic things not to miss here….  First the Puffins living on the side of the cliffs. Magical how there launch into to see with wings flapping wildly😀We lucky because of guide told they should have migrated by now (late August). I guess the amazing warm weather persuaded them to stay while.Secondly the rock columns formations are fascinating. Great place to visit with a decent restaurant on site.

reviews.title: Spectacular!
reviews.text: Spectacular!  Beautiful basalt formations, and puffins!  Don't miss this.  The black sand beach is incredible to see, and the offshore columns are spectacular.

reviews.title: A unique place to see
reviews.text: After watching several sneaker waves at this beach via YouTube, it was neat to be there. The beach is certainly unique. I was so happy to see the puffins were still there. That made my entire Icelandic travels!

reviews.title: Not to be missed.
reviews.text: Tough to walk on the beach, but certainly a highlight to see.  The rock formation along and in the water are really amazing.  Just don't get too close to the water or turn your back on the sea as it has claimed many lives.

reviews.title: One of the highlights of our trip
reviews.text: Black beach, huge waves, basaltic columns, caves, plenty of opportunities to take the most memorable photos of your life

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: The black sand is amazing and the basalt columns make for a nice backdrop.  We went in the evening and their were many puffins coming in with fish for their nests.  There are signs regarding the dangers of the ocean here that must be heeded.

reviews.title: Beautiful black sand beach with basalt columns
reviews.text: Beautiful black sand beach with basalt columns and striking rock formations.  A must-see.  A bit overcrowded during the day, but worth a stop when driving the south road in and around Vik.

reviews.title: Incredible beach to visit
reviews.text: This is an incredible place.The rock formations are something I will remember forever. The scale! They are massive and look otherworldly. It is busy here, but it is worth the drive.

reviews.title: Completely worth the drive and the crowd!
reviews.text: Along with Dyrholeay on 218 off route 1, this is the other “come on, you really have to see this” in South Iceland.  We drove past 218 to start here, where in the distance you can indeed find a gorgeous view of the Dyrholeay arch and islands.  But Lord.  Do mind the signs—the waves even on an incredibly calm and windless day we’re very strong—but the basalt formations here are simply mind blowing, from 200 yards or 2 inches.  We even saw some puffins swimming a hundred yards off shore.  Yes yes there are people milling around here, but it is worth the crowd.  The little restaurant there supplies a WC if you need one, and the sandwiches were really very good.

reviews.title: Commercialized tourist trap
reviews.text: This plane was once a beautiful, serene spot in nature but over the years it’s been heavily commercialized, a restaurant put in, and is now teeming with hundreds of people. Sad to see what it’s become. Be prepared for masses of tourists coming here.

reviews.title: Best black sand beach
reviews.text: If you are comparing black sand beaches in Iceland, this one is better than the one in Vik.  It has everything: black sand, sneaker waves, basalt columns, plenty of parking.  There is a restaurant there (we didn't go in) with a pay toilet attached that appeared to take only coins.  Was a little crowded in mid-June, so I'm sure it gets worse as the summer progresses.

reviews.title: Spectacular Scenery
reviews.text: This is one of the most spectacular natural areas we have ever seen!  The area hiking was fantastic as well. In addition to the amazing scenery, we saw a seal hunting and then resting on the beach.

reviews.title: Great beach for photos
reviews.text: We went to this beach very early in the morning (around 5am) just to feel the atmosphere and to look at the famous Halsanefshellir Cave there. The morning light makes the sea and surroundings very atmospheric, and the black sand really does have silvery streaks in it. I think this beach is a must-see if one is around Vik. We enjoyed taking photographs there.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach,
reviews.text: It is a short drive to the beach from the ring road. Its very pretty. and worth a stop , we did not walk far but took lots of photos.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: What a beautiful beach. The sand is so black. Make sure to stroll the left end of the beach and you will be able to get away from some of the tourists. The basalt columns are cool. The only downside is the Instagrammers all clamoring for their epic shot. It is really obnoxious. Some will get upset if you sit to long. The views in both directions is quite stunning. Take your pictures and put your camera away and take time to just enjoy the beach for what it is

reviews.title: Must see
