This attraction has it all.Short drive on paved roads from the ring road this is easy to get to so it can be busy.Cafe was a bit chaotic, bad coffee which was overpriced. Toilets are only free to customers. A beautiful location and interesting for teenage fans of Game of Thrones.

reviews.title: Amazing photo opps!
reviews.text: You must stop at this black sand beach and check out the basalt columns- makes the perfect photos!!!

reviews.title: Awesome beach
reviews.text: The black sand beach is quite different than the beaches in North Carolina.  If you are a beach person, you will want to see this beach.

reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.text: We visited Reynisfjara Beach around 7pm one June evening and thought it was stunning. The black sand beach has great views in both directions. There are some quite amazing basalt columns. If you walk around the headland there is a big cave with the most geologically interesting roof I have ever seen - really stunning and worth the visit. Do be careful with the tide though and make sure you can get back. Don't turn your back on the sea as this part of coastline has 'sneaker waves' which are massive ones that appear without warning and have caused drownings.To the right you can see the stunning Dyrhólaey Peninsula with an arch and rocks jutting into the sea. This beach is well worth a visit and can be accessed via the 215 road just off the Ring Road to the west of Vik. There is plenty of free parking by the beach.

reviews.title: Great stop!
reviews.text: It was windy, but this stop has a lot to offer....views, caves, black sand beach, cool rock formations. Definitely worth a stop. Plan to stay for 30-60 minutes.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: A nice black sand beach with views of sea stacks and a sweeping view of the bay.  There are also climbable basalt columns which provide a nice backdrop for photos.

reviews.title: Amazing nature site
reviews.text: Easy to get to if you are on the southern main road. Several beautiful nature views which are great for pictures.

reviews.title: Potentially incredible
reviews.text: The day we visited it was extremely windy so our visibility was limited. We were pelted by the sand. But, being among all the sounds and sights of the beach were incredible. It just so happened we didn't have a great weather day, that's the way it goes, especially being we traveled in March. I would still recommend this beautiful natural wonder.

reviews.title: Gotta Stop Here
reviews.text: This beach is indescribable, but I'll try.  Black sand, black pebbles, perfect basalt columns, phallic symbol, far away views, beautiful blue sky with clouds(when we were there), beautiful water and powerful (potentially dangerous) waves crashing.  This is another GOT filming site. There are lots of people and it's hard to get a picture without stangers in the background. If you are not aware of sneaker waves, google it and know these waves are not uncommon on this beach and people die from them.  There is free parking and a very crowded restaurant on site.  Highly recommend.

reviews.title: beautiful but full of arrogant tourists
reviews.text: the beach is beautiful but Iceland please put a ranger on the beach, there are too many people climbing on the columns and sitting on them, not only ruining photos for others but also will end up ruining the columns over time.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: We visited here in June. It is much more than black sand.  In June you may be rewarded with sightings puffins all over the cliff above. Watch out for killer waves. Don't turn your back towards ocean. The formation of rocks are awesome.

reviews.title: More than just black sand
reviews.text: If you can go to this beach in the evening you may be rewarded with viewing puffins as we were. I researched ahead of time the best viewing times and evenings were mentioned as the time the puffins come back in to roost for the night. We could pick them out from the other flying birds as they were the only ones not soaring but flapping like crazy. While the beach does not afford a close up view of the puffins, if you have binoculars or a telephoto lens on your camera you should be able to see them. And then there's basalt columns, and sea stacks, and a cave. I believe going in the evening, it was about 9PM  (during shoulder season) when we went, also meant fewer people on the beach. Our time there was cut a little short as the  evening fog was coming in off the ocean, but even that was beautiful to see.

reviews.title: Trolls turned into basalt columns?
reviews.text: Be sure to read the warning signs about sneaker waves before you charge out to see the beautiful rock formations and cavernous openings along the beach. This is a beautiful spot, not to be missed.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Beautiful, but truly head the warnings - get stay farther away from the water than you think is necessary.  Sneaker waves really do come in quite far and are, of course, dangerous.

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: The Drive to this Beach is Very beautiful specially Early morning ....As its bit foggy and the Green mountains look very pretty. Beach has some volcanic formations ...If you have time then only would recommend ...Otherwise spending much time here I wouldn't recommend. It's very windy and waves are rough

reviews.title: A beach like no other
reviews.text: You must stop and walk along this beach.  The black sand is spectacular in itself, but the basalt columns are absolutely breathtaking.  A must see.

reviews.title: Majestic
reviews.text: I’m not sure the “black sands” are the feature here. The jagged rock formations, which were the inspiration for Hallgrimskirkja Church in Reykjavík, are incredible. The layered rock formations, the caves with diamond-like ceilings, and folds in the earth are as fascinating as they are beautiful. Take your time here. Listen to the waves, listen to the birds, and enjoy the laughter and talk as children play on the beach. There’s no swimming here because the waves are quite dangerous.

reviews.title: u just cant get over it
reviews.text: mesmerizing place...u just cant get over it !!the beauty here is soo soo much that you will forget everything else..

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Definitely worth a stop.  Nice cafe nearby.  If I had to do it again I would try to visit early or late to avoid the crowds.

reviews.title: Dramatic
reviews.text: The black beach is a dramatic scene, certainly unusual. There were quite a lot of people hanging out by the basalt stacks and it was a bit sad to see all the tour groups unload the bus, go onto the beach for ten minutes and head off again.Fortunately we walked down the beach in the opposite direction and found it near-deserted so we could properly appreciate the location.

reviews.title: You’ve seen the pictures-don’t miss out!
reviews.text: This was my favorite spot for beach photos. The black sand is truly black, and the angular symmetry of the basalt columns was somehow mesmerizing. We took our holiday card family photo here; the light is best in the afternoon as the setting sun shines directly on the pillars.

reviews.title: must see
reviews.text: amazing beach - a must see on your tour of Iceland . I would go back again & recommend friends to go.  Nice walking trail up the hill.

reviews.title: Magnificent
reviews.text: I have never seen a black sand beach and I'm glad that this was my first.  This place is stunning and if you're into photography or nature it is a wonderful place to visit.  You cannot go swimming here because of the sneaker waves and you must watch that children and adults alike do not get close to the water.  The natural rock formations are weird and cool all at the same time.  The sights here brought me back to highschool science class as I saw things that I have only seen before in books or talked about in class.  It was neat to see these things in person and get an up close glimpse into how the world was formed.

reviews.title: Beautiful black sand beach with sea stacks
reviews.text: This was a treat.  The beach has large basalt columns (kind of like giant's causeway in Ireland on steriods) that you can get close to. To add icing to the cake there are some caves (not super deep but cool) and then the Sea Stacks.  You can get some great photos.  You might want to watch the tide, you are close to the sea I am not sure what it would look like at high tide (not sure what tide we were there at).Worth the stop

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: The black sand beach is lovely but the volcanic rock formations are the star of the show.  The day we went, there were no sneaker waves. Well worth a visit.

reviews.title: Stunning black sand beach with basalt columns and puffins
reviews.text: This place comes with 360 degree views!! If you stand on the black sand and just slowly turn you will see Dryholeay off in the distance, a long stretch of black sand beach, basalt columns and more. Make sure you walk past the basalt columns, because just around the corner is another cave like area, rock structures and a better view of the rock islands.This attraction is free, has a large free car park. There are toilets, a restaurant and gift shop also available.

reviews.title: Beautiful black sand beach, but crowded
reviews.text: Reynisfjara beach is strikingly beautiful like much of Iceland. There are interesting geographic formations such as basalt columns, a cave like structure, and sea stack just offshore that make this a worthwhile stop while traveling across the southern coast of Iceland. The beauty of the beach also makes this a popular destination so it gets quite crowded. We were there at 3PM and parking was limited. Our kids enjoyed running around the beach but there are many warnings for “sneaker waves” so there was no splashing around in the water. The water is a little cold for that anyway.

reviews.title: Quite Spectacular
reviews.text: Not to be missed, what is considered a world-famous black sand beach just outside of Vik on the southern coast, just off the main Ring Road. We were there on a windy day, so the small, black sand pebbles pelted us as we walked along the shore. It did not take away from the amazing view of rock formations just off shore, basalt columns in hexagonal shapes on shore and the caves throughout an upright undulating rock formation. We understand that puffins like to nest and are found here from May to August, but we were too early to see any. We were told of the dangers of "sneaker waves" that randomly come ashore farther than expected, pulling the unwary out to sea. A tourist apparently had to be rescued when she went around the corner beyond the caves, (easy to do) and the wind suddenly whipped stronger waves ashore, and she was afraid to venture back around on her own. Even though we were told not to climb the rocky stones - so temptingly laid out in steps, but some were loose - many did so to get the perfect selfie.This place is the source of great folklore involving trolls, and how they have become the basalt columns for all their evil deeds. If you have been to the Giant's Causeway in northern Ireland, the rock formations are very similar. So interesting!

reviews.title: Impressive Rock Formation
reviews.text: Our 8th day (5th June, 2019) of family free and easy tour of Iceland first spot is the black sandy beach of Reynisfjara. The black beach is of fine sand to pebble beach. With the blue seas and the unique rock formation and caves the spot is picturesque and scenic. Very impressive rock formation and caves with the North Atlantic ocean made the visit a special one.

reviews.title: Black sand beach
reviews.text: One of the most famous places in Iceland - the black sand beach of Reynisfjara. It's stunning with the basalt cliff formations and a small cave. In the background you get the view of Reynisdrangar -  the sharp rocks on the sea. At times, you can feel like in black&white reality :-)

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Amazing black sand beach. Waves are huge and you have the historic church behins you. The green the black and the blue all blend in together

reviews.title: Interesting Beach
reviews.text: In Iceland there are a lot of black sand beaches, but this one is definitely interesting to check out. The rock formations and cave were very cool. There are signs warning of the dangers of “sneaker waves” that worried me a little but but the tide was out pretty far and it really didn’t seem to be dangerous. We probably stayed for about 30min walking around and taking pictures. This is probably not typical but we encountered a completely nude woman engaged in a photo shoot while we were there which made us uncomfortable and reluctant to walk all the way down the beach.

reviews.title: certainly different
reviews.text: It was raining heavily the day we visited this beach but it was still  worth looking at.It's not a soft sand, more like fine gravel. I wouldn't say it's worth going out of your way to see but if you are in the area stop in.

reviews.title: A Very Interesting Beach
reviews.text: We actually visited Reynisfjara twice. The first day it was pouring rain, very windy, and the surf was very high and dangerous and you could not get to the cave. Later in the week we stopped back and the surf was much lower and we were able to see all of the unique basalt formations.

reviews.title: Stunning Beach and Rock Formations
reviews.text: Loved this place for the black sand, huge beach area and unique rock formations.Could not stop taking pictures and just watching so many people revel in this place.

reviews.title: Impressive and huge beach
reviews.text: That beach is amazing. When we went there it was very sunny but windy. We have seen the power of ocean waves, huge cliffs and basalt columns! Beautiful place

reviews.title: Stunning natural beauty
reviews.text: The drive down into the valley and towards the beach is probably one of the most stunning parts, with a long view over the beach, water and rocks. We came in evening (well, 6pm, which was like afternoon for their sun) - the light was silver off the water and around the promontory to the west. There's a beautiful little church in the traditional style that you pass on the way down. The grass was a brilliant green and the beach itself was wonderful black sand. The basalt columns and rocks off shore were beautiful. the only downside - lots of people... I was surprised that even in May it would be so packed. Glad we didn't come in June!Even with all the people, definitely worth the visit - incredible natural beauty!

reviews.title: Fascinating Beach Area
reviews.text: The black sand is so cool but, the surrounding rock formations felt otherworldly.  Our son told us about the lore surrounding 'Three Trolls' rock formation that was intriguing.  So fun to see the formation behind the story.

reviews.title: If you like sand, this place will float your boat!
reviews.text: Quite sandy. I like sand. Got married here. I also like that. Ran in the hills here. That too was alright.

reviews.title: What a place
reviews.text: This is truly wondrous and the black sand is so much better than the golden sands of the rest of the world.I don't think it matters what time you turn up to the beach as within 5 minutes the light would have changed. We arrived early evening and it was sunny, then cloudy, then it snowed and was sunny again.This is a great place to visit and there is ample parking too. There are toilets which you ahem to pay 200ISK for but luckily when we were there, they were unlocked.A word of warning which is DON'T go near the sea as it is unforgiving and there are freak waves around and you will NOT win.Go visit as it is worth it.

reviews.title: Interesting, iconic spot in Iceland
reviews.text: This is one of the iconic places in Iceland everyone should probably visit.  The black sand is strange to see when you're used to yellow sandy beaches!The basalt formations in and around the cave cut-outs at the back of the beach are fascinating.  Another place where no-one appears to heed the warnings on the signs about dangerous unexpected waves... but I guess it'll kill them, not me - so I shouldn't complain!There is a nice restaurant that does good quality food at a not-too-horrific price, by the name of Black Beach Restaurant (catchy, eh?) - it's located between the car park and the beach itself.

reviews.title: Very impressing
reviews.text: This was probably the one visit we did in Iceland where there were alot of people (we visited in may). But the basaltcolumns were so fascinating! There's also a big cave behind the columns, and the sand is black from the volcanos.

reviews.title: GORGEOUS
reviews.text: Worth the trip. The views are incredible. The sand is like no other sand.  Just be careful because it is an incredibly dangerous beach, do not disregard the signs posted.

reviews.title: Perfect basaltic beach !
reviews.text: Reynisfjara is the famous black sand beach located in south Iceland, close to the fishing village of Vik. The beach is particularly easy to locate on the gps. The parking lot is spacious, with a coffee place and washrooms. And the beach is hardly 100 metres from the parking space. The sand at this beach like most beaches in Iceland has been painted pitch black by the lava eruptions. The lava eruptions have also created enormous basaltic rock formations at this sea, that look like a pyramidal staircase touching the sky. The rock formations are called Gardar. At the bottom of the Gardar is the halsanefshellir cave. This is one of the locations for the sitcom GOT, incase you happen to be a GOT fan. Do take precautions as the beach is known for its notorious sneaker waves that can suck you in , in a matter of seconds.

reviews.title: Great to visit
reviews.text: This is a great place to visit for half an hour or so as part of a south coast tour.  The black sand and the basalt stacks are really interesting and there are a couple of caves.  It wasn’t too busy when we visited in may, but I can imagine it could get very busy in high season.

reviews.title: Awesome beach
reviews.text: Awesome beach. The black sand is really cool and the basalt columns and massive cliffs above are stunning. It is cool to watch the seabirds nesting and flying around. Just avoid getting hit with poop. Be careful going to close to the water as there have been multiple deaths due to the large waves and rough seas.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach with amazing basalt columns
reviews.text: Reynisfjara Beach is also known as Black Sand Beach. You must drive down to the south coast to get here, however if you have the time you won’t regret it. The black sand is beautiful and even more stunning are the basalt columns

reviews.title: Surreal
reviews.text: A must visit when in Iceland. Something very out worldly, surreal, like everything in Iceland. We spent there around 15 minutes, because of crazy wind, but still managed to see enough to be impressed.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Very interesting beach on Southern tour. The cave is where weddings are held and is quite magnificent.

reviews.title: Beautiful southern coast!  Rock formations are impressive!
reviews.text: Beautiful black sand beach with gorgeous rock formations netting out of the water! The rocky cliffs is unique and worth a small climb! We were there in early April- it was about 35F and super cold & wind yet absolutely awesome!

reviews.title: Beautiful, black sand beach
reviews.text: This beach is simply beautiful; however I must admit I was a little scared because of the threat of "sneaker waves".  My recommendation: just pay attention to your surroundings.  Stay off your phone except for the occasional pictures and just soak in the beauty of this beach.There are paid toilets and a small cafe on site.

reviews.title: Lovely photos
reviews.text: Big car park for free, visitor centre next to the car park. Be warned the blacks and will end up in your shoes. Lots of lovely sites to take photos of. Just outside vik x

reviews.title: Majestic rock formations out to sea
reviews.text: The combination of the blue water and sky, black sand quite contrasting. Also the rock formations out in the sea are very majestic. Well worth a visit when in southern Iceland.

reviews.title: Classic coastal landforms
reviews.text: This beach is one of the great beaches of the world. It is a black sand beach, which is exposed to the full force of the Atlantic Ocean. There are many signs indicating how dangerous the waves can be. The coastal landforms here are superb. There are views to a natural arch at Dyrholaey, stacks sit on the beach, there is a sea cave in the cliff behind the beach. The cliffs have excellent columnar jointing in Basalt. A geomorphologist / Geologists dream location.

reviews.title: Rugged and strange
reviews.text: Backdrop not inspiring but the church silhouetted against the hills is interesting and the waves crashing against jagged lava stacks a sight. Then of course fine black sand; all the feel of a golden beach and the grains fall away from your fingers without any trace of colour

reviews.title: Windy & Sandy, be sure to have shades on
reviews.text: Headed over early December and it was so windy i brought home some black sand in my pockets. Overall lovely beach, wish it wasn't as windy when we got there to have a longer stroll after lunch at the cozy cafe upstairs.

reviews.title: Stunning beach with great rock formations
reviews.text: There isn't a long walk to get onto the beach from the parking lot, and the rock formations are really stunning. Would definitely recommend that people stop here if in South Iceland!

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Gorgeous beach with crashing waves, worth a stroll. Try to avoid times when a huge tourist bus lets off (unless you’re one of those). It’s best appreciated with a stroll early in the morning when you have it all to yourself.

reviews.title: Amazing with a splash!
reviews.text: It was raining and the waves were roaring!People were taking photos on the columns. Suddenly big wave poured in and "drown" some of the photographers. Leaving the models stranded. :))All in all, worth the visit even on a bad weather! Careful though.

reviews.title: Uniquely Beautiful
reviews.text: The black sand beach with the columns you’ve seen in countless pictures is just as beautiful in person. Great photo opportunities. Please heed the safety warnings about turning your back to the tide.

reviews.title: Enjoyed
reviews.text: Must see if planning a tour of this portion of Iceland. Such a unique environment. Stay in Vik and be able to enjoy it before all the tours from Reykjavik arrive.

reviews.title: Stunning Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: This beach is just beautiful with the most amazing basalt column cave. Highly recommend a visit to see this beach.

reviews.title: Such a cool beach!
reviews.text: We braved the crazy strong winds and stopped here and it was totally worth it! The rocks were so cool and loved the ominous black sand - wish we could’ve spent more time here wandering the beach!

reviews.title: Picture perfect church
reviews.text: Stand by the beach and look up and snap a picture of this church. It is the best sight of a small settlement and the simple life people lead there.

reviews.title: Sneaker Waves are real!
reviews.text: Never turn your back on the water as you take in the beautiful rocky landscape and black sand beaches. The waves look fierce and deadly and the basalt columns are the perfect backdrop.  A must see experience.

reviews.title: Beware of the waves!
reviews.text: The black sand beach and basalt columns is something to see. In the distance, the stone formations of Reynisdrangar and Dyrholaey can be seen.  Out of this world! The waves come in very quickly so be careful you don’t get caught while taking those marvellous photos and videos. When we were there, people had to make a run for safety as a big wave suddenly came. Almost caught one of the tourists!

reviews.title: As beautiful as everyone says it is
reviews.text: Well worth the stop here. We saw it near sunrise, which made it all the more stunning. Ideal tomgo early and avoid the crowds.

reviews.title: One of the top 10 non-tropical beaches by national geographic
reviews.text: Wish we could have give this a 8 out of 5 Not surprisingly this beach was voted one of the top 10 non-tropical beaches on Earth.  It’s also quite dangerous it was closed the first time we tried to get to it.   ‘Sneaker waves’ can appear when you least expect it, even on calm days.   There are no significant landmasses in between Antarctica and the shores of this beach, so the waves have thousands of kilometers to build.  We were told never turn your back on the waves, and keep a safe distance of at least 30 meters.  There is also some crazy wicked riptide.Interesting side note: see the largest arch in the sea on the right side of the first pic?  Some crazy dude actually flew a plane thru that once 🛩

reviews.title: Pretty, but crowded
reviews.text: The black sand is very pretty, the basalt columns nice, and the view to Dyrholaey awesome. It took quite a while to get a decent picture of the basalt columns and the formations offshore due to the steady stream of people climbing up the columns. Definitely worth a stop.

reviews.title: Must see but...
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful places I have ever seen however it is wildly popular with loads of tour buses. Makes it hard to get photos of the majestic beauty. The weather changes in minutes so come prepared. Really crowded but you gotta see it!

reviews.title: Be super careful!
reviews.text: Not sure how to rate because despite its beauty, its incredibly dangerous. Take heed of signs and stay away from the ocean! Out of nowhere freak waves can sweep you out to sea. We nearly witnessed this happen, a young couple were knocked down and submerged, but were very lucky and were able to cling onto each other but could have been a different story. They were very shaken, as were we, but 5 minutes later more tourists arrived and were playing around in the exact same spot! Keep children well away from the surf especially by the columns, and do not turn your back on the ocean. People have died on this beach so by all means enjoy its beauty but respect those waves..!

reviews.title: Beautiful black beach in Iceland
reviews.text: Popular place to visit in Iceland on the south coast. Reynisfjara black beach west of village Vik. Restaurant near the attraction is called Black beach.

reviews.title: A Few Tips About this Black Beach
reviews.text: A “must see” area with outstanding beauty. The black beach was once ranked in the top ten non-tropical beaches in the world. Obviously, all beaches in Iceland are black. There are several features about Reynisfjara that makes it stand out. With that said, you need not go close to the water’s edge as the waves are extremely powerful. This area is about a two and a half hour drive from Reykjavik.This black beach is famous for the basalt sea stacks that you see on post cards, films and books.  On a nice day the area does provide dramatic photos.  Make sure you go around the corner and see the shallow cave.  Also, when the sea is turbulent, you just can’t help but takes pictures of the ocean. Not far is an area known as Dyrholaey. You can see this area from Vik and from the famous black beach.  A small peninsula juts out with a historic light-house, a huge sea-arch and pillars sticking straight up from the sea.  Unfortunately, our tour did not take us there.  My daughter a year before did this area on her own.  She thought Dyrholaey is well worth exploring.   We visited this area while on a ten hour “Reykjavik Excursion” tour of the South Coast. We went as far as Vik. On this tour we also went to Seljalandsfoss (a waterfall you can actually go behind in the summer); Skogafoss (a waterfall with rainbows and you can climb 500 steps to the top and see it above); and Solheimajokull (a trail that leads up to a glacier.) The South Tour we thought was excellent, better than the Golden Circle tour. If you have a car, your self-guided tour will have great flexibility.  We highly recommend at least a one night stay in Vik.  If you continue on the Ring Road for an hour, you can come to the famous “Glacier Lagoon” and the very interesting “Diamond Beach.” Certain times of the year, icebergs as large as a cars float upon the black beaches making it look like “diamonds.” At the head of Glacier Lagoon is where jeeps will take you up for Ice Caves and glacier tours.      If you found my review “helpful” in any way, please press “LIKE” to let me know.

reviews.title: a must see on an iceland trip
reviews.text: the white foam on the black beach, the sea stacks and the crowds of sea birds all make this a great experience. in can get crowded when the day trippers start to arrive from the capital so get there as early as you can.

reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.text: It is an amazing site. The ocean is pretty treacherous on this beach so caution is mandatory. They call the waves Sneaker waves. You Certainly will understand that term when you are there. We watched some dare devil kids try & climb the rock while there. Without any warning a massive sneaker wave crashed into the roach soaking all those sitting up to near 20ft. Above the beach. One woman was thrown into the water but thankfully she survived. The black “sand” appears to look like sand but it is a different composite. It’s an amazing site!

reviews.title: Unique rock formation and black sand
reviews.text: It was raining pretty hard when we first got there and that's why I'm assuming that's why there was barely anyone there besides us. It was really beautiful even with the gloomy foggy weather. The waves are really strong so be careful and DO NOT go near the water. We got some pretty awesome photos since there was not one there. By the time we left there were multiple tour buses came and the area got packed real fast and even in the cafe that is located by the beach. I don't believe it is necessary to do tours to go to this beach or even the waterfalls. It's all places you can drive to and enjoy yourself on your own time. Do take time to appreciate the really cool rock formations!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and rock formation
reviews.text: Only ~11Km from Vik, the rock formation and the view at Black Sand Beach are a must-see.  This place can get extremely windy.  Also stay clear of the dangerous waves.

reviews.title: Unusual Beach
reviews.text: This beach was a stop on our tour group, but I would definitely recommend this on your own. Fun stop to just soak in nature!

reviews.title: Sunrise for great pics
reviews.text: Great pic spot. Take care with the sea and respect it. Very powerful waves but great at sunrise. If you’re passing by definitely stop for a photo. Parking is free and next to the beach.

reviews.title: But stay away from the water and the waves!!!
reviews.text: Beautiful location and beautiful black sand beaches.  Beware... rogue waves take visitors out to sea every year so you must be careful.

reviews.title: Very interesting rock formations on a pretty beach
reviews.text: If you are staying or travelling through Vik, then a visit to this beach is a must. There are some amazing views of basalt columns and an intriguing cave.Beware of the waves as other people say but it can be fun to watch the idiots that ignore the signs getting wet.

reviews.title: Cool beach
reviews.text: It's a cool beach. There are some basalt columns you can climb/pose on (I'm actually not sure if you're supposed to, but everybody was doing it), and the whole cave is just super awesome looking. Be careful of the sneaker waves, though! They will literally kill you. There is a restroom in the little cafe, but you have to buy something, because they're for customers only

reviews.title: Day trip
reviews.text: My gf and I did a day trip from Reykjavík to Vik (essentially Golden Circle tour without the canyon).  This was something my gf wanted to see and I was indifferent.  Boy was I wrong.  This was absolutely spectacular!A MUST see.TIP: It is worth seeing this from the beach as well as from above.  To see from above, you take an exit left before you get to Vik or the beach level entrance.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Stunning views, incredible scenery. Super windy when we went, make sure nothing of yours flies away! Worth the drive for sure.

reviews.title: Otherworldly
reviews.text: One of the most unique places I have ever had the fortune to visit.  Reynisfjara is a beautiful black sand beach where you can also see a cave, rock formations, and puffins (if the season is right!).  Enjoy the scenery but heed the warning signs about not getting too close to the waves which are powerful and have been known to suck unsuspecting tourists out to sea.  The beach is an absolute must-see on your trip to the Southern Coast!

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: When looking at booking Iceland this was one of the places I really wanted to visit. It’s about 2 1/2 hour drive from Reykjavík.. but you can see two waterfalls and one glacier on the way..!!Definitely typing this in place to see the black beach. If you type in Vik you will just end up in the town..which is ok ...They tell you not to go near the water as the waves are really powerful. And they really are..Stunning beach lots of parking a very short walk to the black sands...This is the place to see the Northern Lights but we didn’t stay so I think we missed a good light to show that evening. But luckily we still saw some in Reykjavík the day before...!!Pictures speak for themselves

reviews.title: Unusual, great experience
reviews.text: This is really amazing, the black sand and the basalt columns make up for a dramatically beautiful landscape sight. The sweeping views over the beach are amazing. There are a lot of tourists though. The beach in Vik itself has much smaller sand, while this one has more gravel.

reviews.title: Beautiful But Dangerous !!
reviews.text: Fabulous beach but please, please, please take care, and be aware of the sneaker waves. The lack sand is stunning, as are the rock formations but every year people get swept out to sea, and we saw at least two close shaves !! Yes take your photos, have a fabulous walk, but just don't get to close to the water.

reviews.title: Beautiful black sand beach
reviews.text: This beautiful black sand beach is good place to take pictures. You will be able to enjoy the beautiful scenery.  There is also nice cliff and there are some birds.

reviews.title: Don't Venture to Close to Waves
reviews.text: Amazing spot but you need to understand the tides and not get too close as waves have carried several people out to sea.  A good rule of thumb, only walk where you see footprints.  really nice location for sunrise but bring pleanty of warm layers.

reviews.title: Must See!
reviews.text: Beautiful Beach with wonderful basalt columns and formations in the water.  Terrific photo shoot.  One of our favorites in Iceland.  Don't miss it!

reviews.title: You have to go
reviews.text: Reynisfjara is a famous black-sand beach on the South Coast. It looked incredibly dramatic and beautiful when we were there with the powerful waves crashing onto the black sand.The Reynisdrangar are basalt (volcanic rock) sea stacks under the mountain Reynisfjall. Lots of people were climbing up them which I would not advise but you can certainly pose for photos on the lower ledges!The Reynisdrangar are basalt (volcanic rock) sea stacks under the mountain Reynisfjall. Lots of people were climbing up them which I would not advise but you can certainly pose for photos on the lower ledges!

reviews.title: Don't go at night!
reviews.text: This beach is amazing.  A handful of sand just rolls off the hand like marbles.  This is an area for sneaker waves and they are not to be taken lightly.   Every few waves can be a rouge wave and sweep you off your feet.   The wind is very strong there but there is nowhere else on earth like it.

reviews.title: Incredible Rock Formations, Incredibly Windy
reviews.text: Once you leave the parking lot and round the corner to get on the beach, prepare for to hold onto your hats. The wind was more powerful than anything I have ever felt before. We actually tried running against and with the wind, it was really funny! There is a large cave you can go inside to escape the wind and admire the jagged walls. The basalt columns are the star of the show.We actually had the opportunity to also view the beach from above (our zipline tour guide drove us up to the private overlook) and we stood on the edge of the cliff feeling the wind on the top of the world. So memorable and exclusive to see a perspective not frequently seen by the masses!

reviews.title: Lovely - but watch out for Sneaker waves
reviews.text: This place is stunning and so unique with the columns, the cliffs and the black sand however there is no natural barrier that stops the waves before they hit the beach which means there is nothing dulling their power. This place is so beautiful with endless photo oppourtunities but you cannot let your guard down. However there are a few dangers that people need to be aware of:1- The sneaker waves - if there are no foot prints or only one or two paths it means a wave has just been there so stay back. By back I mean a good foot or so. 2- The icicles in the cave melt and fall down out of no where so make sure you don't go all the way in.

reviews.title: Fascinating but can be very dangerous
reviews.text: Reynisfjara beach and it's black sands and rock formations are a unique sight and very pictureesque with plenty of photo oppertunities, beautiful to see the sun rise. If you are going over to vik, head to see the Icelandic lava show booking on their website with promo code 'ONLINE' not only will you learn about why the sand is black and how the rocks are formed, but you'll also get to see and feel the heat of real lava flowing and cooling down Infront of your eyes I cannot stress enough though the dangers of the sea here, whilst you may think youre safe, this coastline has a think called 'sneaker waves' which have claimed many unsuspecting lives and also those who ignored the warnings all around, this sea is no joke, stay alert

reviews.title: Incredible view on a very windy winter day
reviews.text: Reynisfjara beach has multiple viewpoints one better than the other. They are perfect for pictures. If you are lucky and come here on a very windy winter day (just after a code orange for winds) you are in for a treat... you get to witness the unbelievable power of 10m waves smashing into the rocks. What an incredible show of nature! Keep in mind to take wind-proof clothes or you will be very very cold. One last thing... the only fees are for the toilet :)

reviews.title: Beautiful scenery!
reviews.text: As with all beaches in Iceland, don't turn your back on the water and stay clear of it so you don't get swept out. Really pretty, very windy!

reviews.title: Sneak Wave Can Sneak Up On you
reviews.text: Famed for it's pitch black sand from weathered basalt, and the basaltic columns a must for photos ops.Sadly, this beach with it's huge wave lurks an even greater danger. Sneaker wave had claimed many unsuspecting tourists, the latest a Chinese man in February 2016.

reviews.title: Beautiful in winter
reviews.text: We visited Reynisfjara Beach in winter, at the end of Januar, and it was an amazing experience. The landscape is very beautiful and it wasn’t very busy only with isolated groups of tourists having a walk around and taking pictures. Definitely a must see in the south of Iceland. Stunning views...The parking is free and the car park is big enough and well organised. The Black Beach Restaurant is more like a cafe but it is really pretty and perfect for a stop after a long walk on the beach. ❄️❤️🌊

reviews.title: Natural Wonder
reviews.text: From the formations in the shallow cave to the hexagonal formations along the cliff, to the black rock beach. this place is truly amazing when considering how it was all formed.  Just off the main ring road, it's easy to get to and there's plenty of parking.  There's even a restaurant. Be warned, it can get windy and the surf can be quite rough.

reviews.title: Excellent Black Sand Beach with an Amazing Geology
reviews.text: An excellent Black Sand beach near Vik with an Amazing Geology. The rock structures are truly stunning and a beautiful place for Sunrise or Sunset. The volcanic Sand is very different and a must see. In summers they say you have a chance of seeing puffins around this region.

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: You can see the remains from the eruption, amazing structures and the stones on the beach were amazing.

reviews.title: Great geology
reviews.text: This beach is just beautiful and impressive with all of its different geological features in this tiny spot.This is a must to visit. However, lots of tourists around can be annoying.

reviews.title: Wonderful location
reviews.text: If you're visiting in the summer drive your own car and stay at the beach for the day. Plenty of other sites to see along the way and on the return to Reykjavik.

reviews.title: Game of thrones
reviews.text: So unusual the black beach not black sand like the canaries but amazing to see with the caves and columns you could almost expect to see jon snow. Stunning scenery excellent photo opportunities  take care of sneaker waves as the pull is very strong. Care also required as car park was like a skating rink. Nice little cafe and shop

reviews.title: Black Sandy Beauty
reviews.text: This is a beautiful beach. I stood for hours steering at the waves and the sand and rock combination. It is most unique. Visited recently in winter and still encountered a few tourists. Nothing to complain about honestly. There is a restaurant with bathrooms inside and outside. If you are not dining at the restaurant then You are required to pay in order to use the (WC)/ bathrooms/restrooms. They are very clean inside. Outside, not so much. Beware of the waves. They can quickly seeep you away especially if you are not paying attention. Enjoy the view and walk all the way to the stretch if you can. Amazing view and pictures

reviews.title: Wild and Wonderful!
reviews.text: This was one of those places where you are both in awe and wonder of its beauty, but aware and respectful of the sheer power of Mother Nature.  We visited here in early-January and while it was party sunny, the wind and seas were fierce! The basalt columns are magnificent and truly unique to view with the backdrop of the waves, black sand and the jagged sea stacks. During our visit, the waves were crashing into the cliffs and coming far up the beach which prevented us from venturing around the corner towards the cave. But the beauty and power of this place should not be missed during a trip to southern Iceland.

reviews.title: Beautiful but watch out for the waves!
reviews.text: The beach is beautiful, the basalt columns made it worth the trek. I was there on a day with a huge storm so the wind was very strong and the waves were quite dangerous.

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: Wow! What a stunningly beautiful beach to visit on our travels! The waves were massive and barrel rolled on to the black sand, was a site to see. The noise of the large waves were relaxing and the views from the beach stunning. I would definitely recommend a visit here when your travelling around Iceland. There’s a supermarket 2 mins walk from the beach also a lovely outdoor shops that’s sells everything to keep you warm

reviews.title: Blistery & windy..
reviews.text: This place is amazing to watch the rock formations. Its covered in black sand and is windy and blistery throughout.

reviews.title: Black sand beach!
reviews.text: Was just incredible! Never seen anywhere like it. The waves were silent. Couldn’t understand where the sound of the waves crashing goes! The only thing to watch is the double waves and then the water coming onto the beach when you just don’t expect it! We got absolutely soaked. Worth the soaking however. Will be back in the summer. Seeing it in the snow was lovely but I’m sure in a different season it would be totally different.

reviews.title: Sneaker waves are serious!
reviews.text: We visited Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach with a tour last month and i wanted to tell everyone to please take the signs seriously! The day we went the waves were absolutely huge and coming in fast. Our tour guide warned us about  sneaker waves, he said “don’t walk anywhere there aren’t foot prints in the sand”. My husband and I were trying to selfie with the basalt stacks, I didn’t like the first photo he took so I asked for another one, as he turned to take another photo, we were hit by a fairly large sneaker wave…. Luckily my husband stayed standing but I was completely knocked over, II am so extremely lucky that my husband is tall and well built because he quickly grabbed me and pulled me back before the wave could take me. Since returning back to Australia, i have read so many articles about how many people have died at this beach because they didnt read or simply ignored the signs and get taken by waves and drown. Please dont be silly, these waves are the gentle waves most people are used to, they will come up fast and take you just as quick. Dont get me wrong this is a really stunning beach and you have to visit it if you are in the area, but just be cautious and use your brain, dont get too close to the ocean and keep an eye on the waves.

reviews.title: Cold!
reviews.text: December found this beach very cold and windy. We still enjoyed our visit to see the black sand and different rock formations. Beware of the very dangerous surf (at least when we were there)!

reviews.title: It was breathtaking
reviews.text: It was a cold, blustery day when we went.  It was gray, low clouds.  But beautiful.  The rock formation, the sand was just beautiful.  But, please, be smart.  It was very windy making for beautiful, wild waves and people were acting like it was athe calm water from your bathtub.  Many people fell and got drenched trying to get away from the waves.  This is nature at her her best—please respect it.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Watch the waves! They are dangerous. Definitely worth a visit to this strange beach. Great at sunrise!

reviews.title: Well worth any amount of traveling to get here...
reviews.text: Words cannot express how amazing I feel this place is. There are not many places in the world as beautiful as this from the different grains of black sand to the basalt columns to the endless black sand shoreline,  This place is about 2.5hrs from Reykjavik and is about 20 minutes from the lookout point which is equally stunning.

reviews.title: Catch it during the sunrise
reviews.text: We visited the beach during the sunrise and it was truly stunning. But be careful of the strong waves!

reviews.title: A Nice Beach To Visit - Beware Of "Sneaker" Waves
reviews.text: We stopped here while on a tour of Iceland. It is definitely something to see if you are in the area. As the photo of the warning sign shows, you should be aware of the waves at all times, as apparently people have drowned here when hit by waves larger than the average sized waves and then being swept out to sea.The rock formations are impressive. We were glad our tour stopped here.

reviews.title: worth the detour, go early
reviews.text: this is lovely place but very crowdedgo early so that you enjoy the view on your owntake nice pictures

reviews.title: Absolutely loved it
reviews.text: When we got here, we were surprised by the number of people.  This place is magical.  I loved the cave that you could walk into as well as the straight columns of rock formations next to it.  The beach had black glistening sand.  The ocean rushed the beach and some rock formations stood guard.

reviews.title: Wonderful rock formations
reviews.text: The beach was gorgeous with truly black sand. We'd been at a couple other blank sand beaches and I don't recall them being as truly black as this one. The rock formations along the cliff edges and Hálsanefshellir  cave were really neat to see as well; it's very interesting how they can form in the way they do. Be sure to heed the warnings and be aware of sneaker waves. While the name may sound silly they definitely are not a laughing matter as plenty of folks have been killed by them. Yes, there were plenty of tourists around when we visited, but not enough to detract from the experience in any way.  Definitely worth a visit!

reviews.title: Probably the busiest spot on the ring road
reviews.text: Although this was probably the busiest spot on the whole ring road (in November), it was still pretty amazing. Just walk round the corner and along the beach and suddenly you’re all alone - don’t be a sheep! The basalt columns are really interesting but the high cliffs and sea stacks are just as aesthetic. I walked right along to the left side of the beach until I got to the end and just sat and watched the raw power of the sea.

reviews.title: So pretty but cold
reviews.text: So pretty and basalt columns are so fun to climb. Do not get in the water! there are many caution signs as people have died there. Wear warm clothes because it is very cold and super windy.

reviews.title: Iceland's black sand beach us Otherworldly
reviews.text: Iceland's Reynisfjara Beach is an amazing alien terrain with volcanic black sand, large basalt columns, and powerful Atlantic waves. According to Icelandic lore, the basalt columns used to be trolls that pulled ships from the ocean onto the shore. When the trolls stayed out to late, sunrise came and turned the trolls into solid stone. A must visit on your tour of Iceland.

reviews.title: Insanely Beautiful.  Terrifying with the wind.
reviews.text: So many pictures on TripAdvisor portray Reynisfjara Beach as a calm, beautiful place.  If you’re looking for both beauty and a thrill go there when the waves are crashing and the wind is roaring.  It’s amazing.  It’s also on the dangerous side as it only takes one “sneaker wave” to come up behind you unexpectedly and snatch you.  Bring your camera and cloth to wipe the lenses from the sea spray as there are about a billion different angles to get a great shot.  Be aware that this is a heavy tourist location

reviews.title: Windy, rugged and amazingly beautiful
reviews.text: We traveled all over Iceland and this was one of my favorite places. Incredible beauty here. Extremely windy with dangerous waves. Stay clear! I recommend rain gear while here. There seemed to be a heavy mist coming off of the ocean, even during sunshine (heavy fog with mist constantly blowing in).

reviews.title: Otherworldly!
reviews.text: Th cave, rocks, and waves are the most dramatic I have ever seen.  It's no wonder movies film in Iceland. This place, and this beach in particular, are out of this world.

reviews.title: Black Sand
reviews.text: The “black sand beach” is beautiful. I have been other places that claim black sand beaches, but this is the darkest sand I’ve seen by far. The basalt columns are very interesting to see. Yes, lots of tourists everywhere (myself included), and it can get very crowded. The waves were so powerful, and the wind was absolutely howling!! We stayed in Vik for 2 nights and so we stopped here twice. On the second day the wind was so furious that we pretty much turned around right when we walked out onto the sand and got back into our car. I am unsure why people do not heed the signs about the sneaker waves. It is NOT to be taken lightly. The day that we were there, the winds were at least 50-60mph, and it was freezing cold. We saw two tourists get completely knocked down by a wave, and start frantically crawling to get out of the water. They were fine, but clearly soaked. I can’t imagine them having to get back in their bus for the rest of the day and see the sights in those wet clothes, if they didn’t have anything else with them. Not only the inconvenience of being cold and wet, but the water had a fury I have never seen, and I can imagine if they had been a few feet closer to the water, the situation could’ve been very unfortunate. It is not the place to go in and rescue anyone. Would love to go back in the summer to see the puffins. This place is definitely worth a stop!

reviews.title: November 2018 visit
reviews.text: This is a nice black sand beach.  There are so many sections to this beach, with great photo opportunities.  There are some caves that look really nice inside.  There is a car park, a souvenir shop/cafe, and toilets.  Watch out for the waves.

reviews.title: Black Sand and basalt columns
reviews.text: What an experience. Never saw black sand before and the basalt columns were really different. Once again very foggy so the effect wasn't as great. However, this is something you need to see.The black sand is really different and those who are used to seeing white or light brown will really be surprised. The overall beauty and the formations make this place really special.

reviews.title: great place
reviews.text: so great to watch the sunrise from here!  if you can get around the tides and see the east side, this place is amazing!

reviews.title: Beware of the 'Sneaky Waves'
reviews.text: Such a cool place. Very windy on the sea front but you just have to go down and have a look.There are 2 caves in which you can go in- not very big but makes for a great photo. We saw a couple of people get hit by a 'Sneaky Wave' catching them of guard which was amusing... VERY AMUSING!! Although out of season, we were told this is where you can see the puffins during the summer.

reviews.title: Great featues all in one place
reviews.text: What a dangerous beach and there were ,may chancing their lives with the vicious waves  As you walk from the car park they warn you - why do they ignore it

reviews.title: Reynisfjara Beach
reviews.text: My first experience of a fulk black sand beach. It's a hidden gem in a sense you will not realize a sea is around until you reach the Reynisfjara town. Located in lovely town of Vik in South Iceland, this place is an absolute beauty. You will be quite lucky if you get less crowd as the views are spectacular then. The beach offers a beautiful sunrise view. One of the locations for Gerua song from Bollywood movie Dilwale featuring Shahrukh Khan.

reviews.title: Beautiful Place
reviews.text: Be careful with the waves, they are dangerous. We went there early morning so we got the beach less packed with people, it was wonderful.

reviews.title: Black sandy beaches...
reviews.text: It was pretty gusty when we arrived here.  The Atlantic doesn’t take prisoners when it’s windy.  Watch out for the sneaker waves which can creep up behind you pretty quickly if you’re not careful.  The contrast in the black sand and white foamy waves was stunning.  You can also see the waves crashing against the basalt columns.    Parking is free and there is a cafe next to the beach.

reviews.title: Cold, Windy, Fierce
reviews.text: The fierce waves come onto the beach lashing the mountain sides, which show signs of wear.  Winds are blustery with gusts robust enough to knock a small or frail person to the ground.  We lean forward and hold onto our caps.  The fury of the attack from nature lasted for seconds which seemed like minutes.  The cold coupled with the high speed of the winds pepper your body with icy water.  Do not turn your back to the waves, you may succumb to the aggressiveness and potentially lose your life. Give respect to the grandeur of nature.

reviews.title: Surreal Geology
reviews.text: This is a must see if you travel to Iceland! Not only do we enjoy the relaxing drive to the area because of the open roads but the geology of this beach is spectacular! The black sand is only the start because the rock formations and rock outcroppings combined with splashing waves are just phenomenal to see with your own eyes. It really only took around 2-2.5 hours to drive to from Reykjavik and there are multiple sights to see on the way! The area is a tad bustling but we did arrive around sunset which could have added to the business.

reviews.title: I absolutely loved this place...
reviews.text: I was lucky to be here twice. Once on a moody very windy day, with massive waves. And second time few days later we come here to watch sunrise when sea was calm. On both occasions I found this place fascinating.Black sand, interesting rock formations, bit different beach landscape to that we get used to.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: An incredible place and a must if you're in southern Iceland. The cafe was really nice and there plenty of parking. Watch out for the "sneaker" waves, plenty of people got soaked when we were there!

reviews.title: A beautiful place, watch those waves.
reviews.text: Found on the right shortly before Vik on the 1 road from Reykjavik. A large car park in front of a cafe greets you at the end of a twisting access road about two miles long. Past this building to the right is beach access. The beach itself is of black, volcanic pebbles and sand. The cliff face is a fantastic sculptured wall of basalt columns with shallow caves. To your right is a vicious sea which hits a (fairly steep at high tide) beach of pebbles with a wide variety of waves, mostly very short and then a long, unexpected one, surprising the unwary. It has been called "The most dangerous beach" on the island. Do not swim....Dress very warm in the winter. Boots are best. Very busy with busloads of tourists so go early or late for peace.PSCafe is great for hot lamb soup in winter

reviews.title: Beautiful place
reviews.text: Black sand, sea stacks, caves make you feel like you are in an movie! The drive is pretty along the way but the beach really is to be seen to be believed. Watch the puffins fly around & all the tourists doing their best poses but try just take a minute to appreciate the view. Beware of very strong waves

reviews.title: Don’t be a statistic!
reviews.text: Reynisfjara Beach is a dramatic beach landscape if you check out YouTube videos. Watching drone footages of this black beach is simply jaw-dropping. On the ground, unfortunately, is a less dramatic affair with people milling around. Still the black sand, the black pebbles, basalt column, caves, the 2 columns sticking out in the ocean and the windy wet weather more than make it up. The real star of the site without doubt, are the crashing waves. Watch the waves transform from normal to crashing waves in matter of seconds and you will understand why Icelandic people call them ‘Sneaker Waves’. So far this year 2018, there has been no fatality so please heed the warning sign and don’t be a statistic. The cafe near the entrance to the beach serves drinks, soups and food. The WiFi and toilet are complimentary for customers otherwise there is a small fee levied.

reviews.title: Windy day
reviews.text: Windy and misty day, but it is worth it. Kinda hard to describe the situation that you end up in, but you have to go to experience it yourself.

reviews.title: Well worth a visit!
reviews.text: Just a few minutes drive from our accommodations...we got here late in the afternoon close to sunset. It was raining on and off, but there were still plenty of people visiting. This is a beautiful site with two caves right near each other..both of which we ran to for cover when it started to rain. The basalt columns were filled with folks climbing to all levels to get a picture and the black beach with rock formations coming out of the water was a treat! Despite the gloomy weather, we got a little bit of sunset peeking out through the clouds over by Dyrholaey (which you can see from the beach..including the functioning Dyrholaey Lighthouse). Although we didn't go, there's a place to eat right by the beach as well.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Beautiful and clean.  Tons of tourist close to the parking lot but you can walk away from them and get amazing pictures and find meditation nooks.Be careful of the strong waves.

reviews.title: Sneaker waves
reviews.text: We thought we were far enough away from the beach area.  We were not.  It was so beautiful that my wife and I started to look all around us.  Out of nowhere we got hit by a sneaker wave, we were about 50 from the beach.  My wife got pushed in closer to shore but I had to be pulled out by a GOOD person.  Wet winter clothes are very heavy and I am very grateful she dragged me out.  Look around it is great but stay far away from the water.

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.text: I think the most amazing place I have ever been to on earth. Make the drive here when you visit Iceland. It will take you

reviews.title: Uniquely Iceland!
reviews.text: Must do when you are in Vik! Amazing black beach made of lava! Weather was great and the views of the beach with rainbow over the hills made it spectacular!

reviews.title: Stunningly Beautiful, a must see!
reviews.text: Reynisfjara beach - black Beach is the southern most tip of Iceland and is beautiful. With caves, columns, black sand and sea stacks, absolutely beautiful, highly recommend.

reviews.title: Black sand and basalt
reviews.text: Look for the rock frozen giants in the ocean and enjoy climbing the basalt columns. The sand is silky soft pure black.

reviews.title: Beach, waves, and caves! A must-see Icelandic landmark.
reviews.text: This beach near Vik and an absolute must-see destination!First of all, the basalt columns are amazing. They will make you feel like you're on another planet, they really blew me away.I was beyond fascinated by the sand itself, it's so black, the texture is soft and stone-like, and honestly, I scooped some up and took it home with me. Lastly, there are no bad views on this beach. Every direction has something amazing to look at. The horizon seems never-ending and the dramatic colours make for some of the best photos of our trip.This site can get busy, which makes taking good photos difficult. But if you wait your turn, most of the other tourists are more than willing to move out of the way so you can get your shot, just be sure to return the favour :)

reviews.title: Simply amazing
reviews.text: This is definitely worth visiting. Pick the right time of day though it can get very busy which makes photography difficult. Check out the puffins flying from the cliffs out to sea and back.

reviews.title: Beautiful Reynisfjara Beach
reviews.text: Reynisfjara is the most famous black sand beach in Iceland with its wild and dramatic beauty of roaring waves from the Atlantic Ocean. It is also the ideal place to meet the Icelandic trolls (rock formations in the ocean with a mythological-like story). Note: the black sand is actually formed from heavily eroded volcanic rocks that are black to begin with i.e. cooled lava turns black as it cools and hardens.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, waves, and caves!
reviews.text: This beach in Vik is definitely worth the stop! The black sand on the beach is beautiful, and the horizon is amazing at sunset. Be careful of the "deadly sneaker waves"! The signs warn of these dangerous waves, and they are no joke!

reviews.title: Beautiful, awe inspiring and dangerous!
reviews.text: When you see the sign saying it's dangerous, please, please believe it! You can have 20 waves coming in and they all finish about the same place then you get a HUGE wave - and people are caught out (especially the ones more interested in their selfie stick).  On the day I went, someone was swept out to sea later that day.  Enough of the health and safety warning - this beach is amazing.  Black sand, perfectly flat black pebbles, a little cave with amazing rocks/geology and the dramatic sea stacks. The mist drew in really quickly which added to the atmospheric nature of this beach but, again, just be mindful of this when you set out.

reviews.title: Surreal Beach
reviews.text: A must see spot when going to Iceland. It is not too far from Reykjavík, located in Vik. The place does get busy but not as much in off season. There is also a cafe and washrooms, though you have to pay for the washrooms if I remember. You can fly your drone here but be weary about the sand and having it get into your drone

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: One of the main reasons I wanted to come to Iceland and it didn’t disappoint. Amazing views. Just a fascinating place with the basalt formations. Well worth the trip. Waves are winds are strong, but a great walk along the beach. Stay safe!

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: We drove here from Reykjavik on our first day and it was beautiful and worth the drive. The beach has the most amazing black pebbles and is backed by these massive cliffs. There are rocks you can climb over and get to a more secluded part of the beach. The square stones are unlike anything we have ever seen. We also saw a massive seal in the water! There is a cafe on site, though the line was really long when we were there, so we didn't get anything. There are also bathrooms available.

reviews.title: Beautiful even with the crowds
reviews.text: If you plan on going to Vík you must stop here. Easily the largest black sand beach I’ve seen...miles and miles and miles. You can see Dyrholaey about 5 miles up the beach.

reviews.title: Stay Safe
reviews.text: My husband and I were here on an extremely windy day. The beach and the waves are absolutely stunning, although the area is relatively small, but the feel of grandeur was just like scenes from the Game of Throne. The only thing was, as it was so windy, we walked with our heads down and didnt see the warning sign regarding how dangerous the waves can be, afterwards I saw videos online of waves swallowing tourists... I'm glad we did not have to experience it. Many tourists have died here.... so my advice is... this is a MUST GO, but please stay safe!!

reviews.title: Amazing beach
reviews.text: Really special beach which can be a bit spoilt by all the tourists. Walk down to the very end and you can have it to yourself

reviews.title: Dramatic beach
reviews.text: The South of Iceland surprised us with its different terrain, I have been on Black beaches before but this was truly spectacular. It has a strange eery quality to it , and the stacks are super for photos. I would have liked to look properly in the caves but they were overrun with tourists so we walked to the far end of the beach and enjoyed a bit more solitude. The crashing waves and seabirds on the cliff gave it all a great atmosphere. I will remember this beach for a long time, just slightly spoiled by silly girls with selfie sticks .

reviews.title: Try to avoid the crowds
reviews.text: This place has a mysterious feel but the large crowds you‘ll meet here can easily spoil it. I suggest coming very early or late, strolling along the beach and taking your time for an atmospheric picture to catch the special mood.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: The cliff formations are outstanding.  I was on a tour and the parking lot was jammed. There are lots of warnings about the current. The cliffs look like sheered off lava and are amazing. I loved it.

reviews.title: Went to see cliff formations
reviews.text: I went to look at the cliffs and wasn’t disappointed. The black sand is unusual but not surprising and the deadly waves didn’t look so bad. Definitely swam in worse at home. Surprisingly busy even at the early part of the day but pretty good if you wait for the idiots climbing on the cliffs to shift. Sea birds a bit limited in the autumn but not a shock either. Hexagonal shapes in the cliffs very interesting. That’s what I went to see.

reviews.title: Black sand beach with lots of scenery
reviews.text: This was the first blach sand beach I saw. It is beautiful especially when was used to looking at white sand beaches. The beach is covered with sand and instead of sea shells on the beach there are black smooth rocks all over it. You can see cool rock formations in the water and the Dyrholaey in the distance. There is a cave that you can walk in and take pictures.

reviews.title: Stunning.  Breathtaking.  Majestic.
reviews.text: As we walked along the black-sand beach towards the spires, the huge waves were crashing, and the opportunities for photographs with several of my lenses were endless!

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: We saw Reynisfjara Beach on two different days......coming into Vik October 3rd on a blustery rainy afternoon and headed back to Reykjavik two days later on a bright sunny warmish day.  First visit was dramatic with the wind swept surf and second visit felt peaceful and calm. The basalt columns on the cliff face are something to be seen and a great photo op .   However, heed the warnings to keep far back from the water due to sneaker waves.  It is a spectacular spot, not to be missed.  There is a cafe there, but we didn't go in. It's a hop, skip and a jump  outside Vik.

reviews.title: black sands
reviews.text: This is basically a sightseeing venture since you can see a lot just in buzzing around this area. Black sands are truly spectacular.

reviews.title: Majestic Experience
reviews.text: One of the most striking views I witnessed in Iceland.  As you gaze at the basalt columns while the icy wind is whipping around you, and hear the deafening crash of the waves beating against the black sand beaches, you will behold a truly majestic experience. Be careful, the waves are treacherous and it is very cold. Was also happy to learn that this was Eastwatch by the Sea in a few episodes in season 7 of Game of Thrones.  There are various views of this beach around the Vik area and each one is simply stunning.

reviews.title: Other worldly place
reviews.text: This beach truly makes you feel like you’re on another planet and it’s no wonder so many films use this location for inspiration. Being able to watch the brilliantly ice blue waves crashing on the shores of the black sand is an experience I will never forget. This was a pretty easy drive along the coast to get to since the weather was working in our favor that day. Convenient parking lot and cafe located right along the beach. If you don’t feel like making the drive yourself, there are tours from Reykjavík that will take you there.

reviews.title: Beautiful, but crowded.
reviews.text: Hard to get the picturesque views of the rocks in the back due to the many other people here.  But totally worth the stop.

reviews.title: Group tour.
reviews.text: Unbelievable beach. A must see if your in Iceland. Bring warm wind proof jackets and warm coats. North Atlantic blows cold and strong here.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Well worth the trip. Beautiful beach with black sand, ocean view and interesting rock formations. During our trip in october it was very windy. But it made it feel even more magnificent.

reviews.title: Just as incredible as expected but be aware of the waves
reviews.text: It's quite something, to see your first black beach, with a looming cave and basalt columns. My tour guide stressed that it was very, very important to never have the water behind you, and I got to see first hand why. The freezing wind was howling the day I visited the beach and the waves were high and mighty, crashing upon the black sand. What was particularly astounding about the waves were how fast they lapped at the beach, and how far the waves would rise up the shore. There are warning signs as you descend the beach to be careful of the waves and not to get too close to the water, and it's important that the signs are taken seriously. The black sand is very very soft; as water runs through the sand, your footing is very precarious at best. A few tourists have lost their lives here as a result of being dragged into the sea; moral of the story is- enjoy the view of this spectacular beach don't flirt with the water!!

reviews.title: Different and intriguing
reviews.text: This is an unworldly place.  The surf is up with pounding, dangerous waves, the beach is all black with shiny diamond-like sparkles, and the pencil-like black columns of lava rock have to be seen to be believed.  Then add the driving wind and numbing chill, which can be only lessened by standing next to a blocking column, you have a place to remember forever.It is a strange feeling to want to leave and yet want to stay.

reviews.title: Black sand beach
reviews.text: Must see in South Iceland easy access beautiful views and great little sandwich shop with top line coffees (Kaffi)

reviews.title: Very cool to see
reviews.text: This black sand beach and basalt columns are great photo opportunities. Some weird things wash up on the beach . See my pics. They also have a little place to eat here if your hungry. The parking lot is not big enough for all the traffic, and there is no fees here either.

reviews.title: Very nice!
reviews.text: What everyone has said about the crowds is true. So if you go knowing that, it's not so bad. We went during low tide, so the waves weren't as bad, though we were still careful. The cave and basalt columns were crowded when we first got there. However, the crowd thinned and we were able to get some great pics, walk the beach to the rock formations and truly enjoy the view. It really is amazing and the black sand beach was stunning. Definitely go, just be prepared for the crowds.

reviews.title: Like no other beach I’ve seen!
reviews.text: This place is quite touristy but it’s definitely worth a visit. The beach has black sand and incredibly powerful waves. But it’s the rock formations that are truly amazing. The basalt columns are so beautiful and just around from that is a wonderful cave with these stunning rock formations.  Definitely not to be missed.

reviews.title: Eerily Amazing!
reviews.text: Wow! Incredible beach with so much to see! The rock formations and caves are impressive, as is the beach itself - the waves are so powerful! Make sure you walk to the end of the beach and climb over the rocks to go to the next beach over....you'll get a completely different view of the rocks in the water.

reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text: This was one of the sites on our 9-day trip that totally blew me away. The power of the waves, and the beauty of the rocks was amazing. This was one of the more crowded sites, but absolutely worth the stop. Walk all the way down to the curve in the rocks for less crowds. Free to park, paid WC.

reviews.title: I enjoyed this beach more
reviews.text: This one, for me, was more enjoyable than the one further down the road with the columns.  Not nearly as full of tourists.The town itself, is completely overrun with tourists, even when I was there in October and was the most unappealing stop on my vacation. The beach itself was worth the stop.

reviews.title: very like a small version of the twelve apostles in victoria australia
reviews.text: go first thing in the morning (7.30-8.00) before the tourist buses.  We first went 3pm the day before and we could not even get a car park much less get close to the beach

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: A lot of people complain that this spot has gotten too touristy, but I  think it is worth the stop. The basalt columns, black sand, Hidden caves and amazing landscape make putting up with the crowds worth it.

reviews.title: Amazing black beach
reviews.text: Beautiful. The basalt columns are really cool and the little cave is fun to stand in and admire. The waves are beautiful but strong so don’t get too close. Beautiful scenery especially in the evening close to sunset. Stunning.

reviews.title: Amazing Rock Formation
reviews.text: So much to experience in this one area; black sand beach, sea stacks, dark basalt columns and a stunning sea cave. Very popular tourist stop making it difficult to get pictures with no one in them.Rogue waves are common. Its hard to imagine that the next landfall south of this point is the Antartica. That's a lot of ocean.

reviews.title: Black beach with black rocks
reviews.text: Nice beach with black sand. Many tourists. Parking place is attached to the site. In late afternoon you can get some pretty nice photo shots. Not a must see if you are running out of time, as there are other black beaches on the island.

reviews.title: What You See Only in Television
reviews.text: Black sand beach? How would it look like?? Was curious before stepping in the zone and after that it was just amazing. They say it’s a dangerous place during high tide since the water enters the land to few hundred meters. So a proper tour guide is a must. We went by the day trip provided by Viator which is really convenient. Once in a life time visit.

reviews.title: beautiful at sunset
reviews.text: very picturesque with several unique rock formations and caves.  Going at sunset gives some beautiful photos.  Be careful of the sneaker waves which can soak you, or throw you off balance. Moderately busy but not as crowded as some places.

reviews.title: Stunning!! But stay awares
reviews.text: My favorite beach in Iceland, out of all that we visited!! I will return to south Iceland and visit this area again for sure.

reviews.title: Cold place with magical atmosphere
reviews.text: If you visit this cold island it's good to see its southern point with this black beach. It is a windy point with special atmosphere but interesting to see it. It's advisable to take a good quality raincoat and good shoes.

reviews.title: Basalt columns stair step here.
reviews.text: While this is the same as the black sand beach the sands here are some of the most unique I have ever encountered. Unlike fine sands these here are more coarse, almost like cat litter. While here we marveled at the basalt columns and climbed around for a time while watching the sun rise ever higher in the sky from morning. While searching the sea for some time we even caught sight of some kind of whale, which made the trip.

reviews.title: Implausible Experience..!
reviews.text: Undoubtedly the best sight to view in Iceland. Black Sand Beach with incredible basalt.It was raining the day we visited the beach, we hung out for a while in car for the rain to stop. To our shock the sky cleared in matter of 5 minutes. From the parking lot it is about 300 meters walk. Disappointed at first since the first section is swamped by people,  but we managed to find our little joy in finding places to photograph. Moments later we walked further to Reynisfjara Beach there were far less number of people which gave us time to absorb the beauty this place has to offer. Basalt, caves, black sand, tiny smooth black pebbles, gashing waves and the froth that waves was leaving every time it hit the sand...everything was a wonder in itself. And then you start to photograph the beach and one cant get enough of it. It rained again and this time we took shelter in the cave, which was a sight in itself. Towards the end of the beach one can just take a deep breath looking at the waves hitting the rocks and you know how the shapes are formed. We had such an incredible time at the beach and all the memories are just floating in front of the eyes.

reviews.title: Famous view with Basaltic structure on a black sand beach
reviews.text: Truly mesmerising. Really loved the place in spite of being crowded. But as you pass the cave with unusual 3D effect structure ... and walk towards the basaltic formations there is less people and the view gets very dramatic ... with waves splashing across rocks and sand.
