Great opportunity for photographers.The access is very easy , free parking, restaurant and bar nearby.

reviews.title: Absolutely amazing
reviews.text: Black sand beaches are rare to begin with, but one with such beautiful features of sea stacks, cliffs, caves, oh my!  Much worth a quick stop on a clear day when you can see it all and pause to enjoy it.

reviews.title: Amazing basalt and black sand beach
reviews.text: Not as stunning as the basalts of the “Giants Causeway” in Northern Ireland but they are still a sight to see. Beware of the traffic camera on the road in to the park. There is a restaurant here as well to grab a bite to eat.

reviews.title: Incredible experience
reviews.text: I love visiting Reynisfjara! Even though it was overcast and misty-- nature has a way of being stunning in any condition. The black sand beach and caves were a wonder. I could have easily spent the day here walking along the shore. Just beautiful. Even with the large number of tourists, you can find places and time where you can experience a peaceful sense of awe.

reviews.title: Like in Game of Thrones!
reviews.text: I went there early in the morning to be less crowded, and it was worth it! The view is spectacular, and when you get closer to those rocks, you can watch the incredible wildlife of Icelandic birds.

reviews.title: Unique beach experience
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with black sand , interesting geological structures, picturesque  views for photos!!!

reviews.title: Superb rock structures, great views
reviews.text: There is free parking close to the beach. After a short walk across black sand will get you arrive at some dramatic basalt rock formations which in places seem to defy gravity and a short walk past this is a cave which presents a weird 3D effect and great for photos. A little further on still and you arrive at some dramatic cliffs. Look out to sea for incredible sea stacks also caused by volcanic activity with views all the way to the Dyrholaey promontory.The place does get quite busy with tourists but is much quieter the further down the beach you walk and for dramatic views, it is a must see.

reviews.title: If you hadn't seen basalt columns yet, stop here
reviews.text: You can see basalt columns all over Iceland, but they have some of the best ones here.  You can walk on the beach right next to them.  The black sand beach is so pretty.  Bring a small bag with you and take some home.

reviews.title: Worth it!
reviews.text: Where can you see a glacier driving in, green pastures with grazing sheep, a black beach, Atlantic Ocean ALL in one place?  Here!  A great drive into this beach.  We arrived at sundown, and it was awesome!  Lighting is fabulous for photos (reddish-golden hues) that make the water, and black basaltic columns really pop!  We even got a rainbow by the two rock islands.  It was not crowded so very nice.  Go toward sundown for good lighting and photo ops!

reviews.title: Amazing but be prepared for a crowd
reviews.text: This place is like no other I've ever been. The rock formations are stunning. The white sea spray against the black sand is otherworldly. It's just breathtaking. The only thing that bothered me was the CROWD! My husband and I went at about 6-7 p.m. on a Sunday and it was very crowded. Most of the people seemed to be just tourists like us but then there were also weirdos like girls in prom dresses (literally) preening and trying to get the perfect Instagram photos. It ruined some of the atmosphere and provided a decent distraction. But it was still an amazing place.

reviews.title: what a view
reviews.text: mystical beach, worth a film setting, this is a must visit on your Iceland trip. free access, apart from toilet at 700 crona by credid card if you need it!

reviews.title: This place is awesome as part of our South Coast Day tour - Got to see a bunch of Puffin birds
reviews.text: This was an excellent stop as part of our South Coast Day tour.  We got a little bit of everything on the weather side, heavy rain, sunshine, sprinkles, high winds in the short period of time we were there.  The black sand is pretty cool and easy to walk on.  The surf was interesting to watch, sometimes the surf came in towards you while walking.  We also got see a bunch of Puffin birds in their nest above the caves and flying around.

reviews.title: A very neat black sands Beach with rock formations and caves.
reviews.text: This is one place that was a must on my travel to Iceland. It was an overcast day but the Black sand was made up of small black and red Lava rocks.  The ocean was quite rough which made it even more beautiful.  There were 2 rock formations, Dyrholaey and Reynisdrangar and 2 caves.  There were also beautiful basalt Columns.  This is the Atlantic ocean.

reviews.title: amazing black sand beach and incredible / unusual rock formations
reviews.text: Reynisfjara Beach is another "must see" on your drive around Iceland - it is only a 5 minute or so drive from The Dyrholaey Nature Reserve.  The walk along the beach is incredible, but take notice of the warning about rogue waves - they truly do come out of nowhere.  We saw one man getting totally drenched with no warning at all that a large wave was coming, so walk a "safe" distance away from the water.  The rock formations are unbelievable to see in person.

reviews.title: Watch out for Sneaker Waves
reviews.text: At Reynisfjara beach, we were warned of sneaker waves - and how these deadly waves have claimed the lives of tourists at Iceland's most dangerous beach.  This is a black sand beach backed by stacks of basalt columns at the foot of the mountain Reynisfjall.

reviews.title: Magnificent
reviews.text: Not far from Vik. If you want a black and beach you can see it in Vik. If you want to see reynisdangar or caves you need to go there. Magnificent view! And too mych people. If you don't want to see people you can go 200 meters along the beach and there will be nobody))

reviews.title: Beautiful quick stop
reviews.text: This is a beautiful black sand beach with some great rock features! Beautiful views and a quick stop unless you want to spend a long time taking photos. I would not miss this stop if you are in Vik, as the black sand is unique and the views are good. It does get busy, like most sights in Iceland. We saw some sneaker waves coming up that nearly caught people - be careful!

reviews.title: Loved this beach
reviews.text: Parking was right at the beach, this place had so many interesting things including the black sand, to the basalt columns that my teenagers climbed, to the cave, puffin nesting and diving in for fish, which I hear are there only until the end of August so we were lucky to see them at the end of August when we were there. I brought home some of the flat rocks that are all over this beach. Perfect for photographers.

reviews.title: More Of The Same - Spectacular
reviews.text: If it wasn’t so spectacular, it could almost get monotonous going from beach to beach... Just Spectacular!

reviews.title: A little disappointed
reviews.text: Loved the stop and the view.  There are other basalt columns all around Iceland that were nicer but these were our first.  It was a nice view of the beach but I was disappointed with the visitors and their selfie time climbing all over the cliffs and not considering others who just wanted to enjoy the landscape.

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: From the black beach to the very surprising rock formations, this place is a must see. No disapointment there!

reviews.title: Black beach with ton of tourist
reviews.text: This is a quite interesting site with rock and cliff formation on the beach. parking is close by but you want to walk on the beach to enjoy the beauty. Even there is a warning to stay away and careful about sudden waves, some people did not pay must attention. Just stay safe and enjoy this beauty.

reviews.title: Black beauty
reviews.text: Once upon a time ranked amongst the most beautiful nontropical beaches this site has beauty worth beholding. It has an amazing basalt rock formation in stacks. It has thousands of nesting sea birds seen along the formation. Amazing rock structure also can be visualised from the shore. It is easily accessible and a great photo stop

reviews.title: Possibly the most incredible beach in the world
reviews.text: Simply amazing beach. Free parking right next to the beach. This really is black sand beach. It is unbelievably black. As soon as you get to the beach there are a lot of amazing hexagon columns, right next to them is another cave with a completely different rock formation. Then further along the beach there were more different rock formations. At the end of the beach there were some big rocks at the edge of the water. There were also a lot of nesting puffins above the rock formations. And to make the beach even more special you can see the rock formations of Dyrhólaey in the distance. This is an essential visit. The first bit of the beach was very busy and there were people all along it so if you want a secluded beach this isn’t the one for you.

reviews.title: The highlight of Vik
reviews.text: Reynisfjara Beach is a must-see when visiting the Vik area. The black sand beach is beautiful and unique. You do need to stay away from the water as the waves are unpredictable and dangerous.

reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.text: Black sand, rock formations i.e. columns and cave are amazing. Free parking nearby. Many people but it is possible to take some good photos. Time to spend: 30 min

reviews.title: Gorgeous views
reviews.text: Nice beach with lovely views of the rock formations - different from the black beaches nearby but still worth a visit.

reviews.title: Stunning waves
reviews.text: We loved the Black Beach area. The waves are mesmerizing and the power of these waves incredible. Be careful of the waves. If the tide is low you can go further down the beach which is safe but make sure the tide is not coming in.  The waves come fast so you can get soaked if you are not careful. Lots of puffins in the area.

reviews.title: Very Beautiful, Very Crowded.
reviews.text: If you make the trek to Iceland and opt to leave Reykjavik (which you definitely should), you might as well stop here at this beach. It's very pretty with it's rock formations and black sand, but in my opinion, there are more beautiful places in Iceland and this one is so overcrowded with tourists taking photos. I came during semi-off season in September, and the beach was by far the most crowded place we visited including places in Reykjavik. You could not get a picture without someone else in it. If you drive out to see it, make sure to also stop at Gulfoss, Skogafoss, and Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon.

reviews.title: Puffins & beautiful basalt columns
reviews.text: This is one place in Iceland that I would consider a must-see.  The beach is beautiful.  The basalt formations are stunning.  And, during the summer months it is a great place to see puffins.  The beach is made up of larger black stones instead of sand.  It takes a bit of an effort to walk across, but it is worth the time.  You may recognize the location from movies or shows such as Game of Thrones.  They were filming something while we were there, but I'm not sure what it was.  Beware of the sneaker waves that can catch you off guard & take you out to sea.  I would give myself at least an hour to explore this area.  Honestly, I could spend most of an afternoon here enjoying the setting.  There is a small restaurant & bathroom on site too.

reviews.title: Stunning black sand beach
reviews.text: This is the most amazing black sand beach. To one side are the fascinating geometric basalt columns, together with a large cave which provided welcome shelter on a very wet and windy day; on the other side is the ocean, complete with atmospheric rock stacks but beware - at the entrance to the beach there are rather sobering signs which highlight the danger of the 'sneaker' waves and the fact that several tourists have lost their lives here being caught unawares and washed out to sea. You need to avoid being distracted by the beauty of the place (which is very easy) and not keeping an eye on the shore line. We loved it here - a photographer's paradise!

reviews.title: Different
reviews.text: I will use that word to describe this black sand beaches, but not too appealing to me for an special visit. If in the are do it.

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text: What a great experience! This black sand beach is epic—I really found it beautiful and captivating!  The black stones at the water’s edge are incredible. Free parking-but pay toilets-ugh.  Bring your camera!

reviews.title: beauty and geology
reviews.text: The beaches are lovely  and the stones rising from the ocean are so dramatic!  The puffins and other sea birds are added attractions!

reviews.title: Black beach, puffins, great views
reviews.text: The black beach is .... well black of course, it also has a number of caves and square profile forms of basalt in the side of the cliff, formed from when soft lava rock has been worn away. There is a perch above where loads of puffins are flying in and out (save teh cost of a puffin watching expedition). This is not a bathing beach due to the waves (sneakers) being very dangerous, it is also very windy.

reviews.title: Amazing!!!!
reviews.text: I loved it here. It's a definite must see in Iceland. The cave is breathtaking and the columns are fantastic. The beach itself is just the most magical place. Walk along to the end if you visit. Handy tip - get here early especially if you want photos. I was on this beach for about 2 hours, I loved it so much but after 12, there are coach loads of tourists and getting a picture without a shiny yellow jacket in it will be a challenge.

reviews.title: Unique and worth it
reviews.text: This is such a cool thing to see. I had been to the black sand beach in Santorini and it was ok, but this one was amazing. It really has black sand along with some black rocks in sections. And the rock formation lining the back of the beach is unique and cool to see.

reviews.title: The closest you can gget to view the fantastic crystalite basalt columns.
reviews.text: This beach is like a surprise package. Where you park your vehicle, there is noting visible except a mound and the beach. When you finally get around, the basalt columns show up and then its a show window of the most amazing formations of rock. There is a beautiful cave which has these formations allover the surfaces, like Gaudi's architecture. No surface is plain. A beautiful array of textures and grey tones.

reviews.title: Good visit
reviews.text: Great view of the ocean and the rock formations. Parking was reasonable and there was plenty of space on the beach to walk around. A cool experience.

reviews.title: Breezy beach with great sunset
reviews.text: Very cold and breezy but it was March.Good to see and got some great sunset photos.Basalt columns but maybe Ireland does them better.

reviews.title: You won’t see anything like this at home
reviews.text: What nature or whoever sculpts this stuff had done to the black basalt is like nothing we had seen. There’s the tormented spires that stymie understanding of just how they got built. And not far distant it turns into walls of basalt blocks neatly stacked until suddenly their direction turns and they go into swirls – as though some giant child you really don’t want to meet got tired of orderliness and decided to introduce a wholly new pattern. We were there on a rainy day but there were still fulmars adding some recognizable life to a grotesquely beautiful landscape. I was a dandy walk even in the rain.

reviews.title: Awesome Black Sand Beach!!
reviews.text: Stopped here to see the black sand beach and basalt columns.  This is a beautiful place (and a Game of Thrones filming location).  Very dangerous surf so keep back from the waves when visiting.  Fun to climb up on a column and take some pics!!

reviews.title: black sand beach
reviews.text: Strangely enough, Reynisfjara Beach in the Katla Geological Park, about 25 km west of Vik, reminded me of Hac Sa Beach in Coloane Island, Macau, except that Reynisfjara Beach is better kept..... The beach is of black sand and stones, which reminds you of the volcanic activity in the area and the proximity of Mount Katla... There are also geological rock formations that remind me of Hong Kong Geopark outside Sai Kung... and this beach is a good place to watch puffins, which must nest in the cliffs above the beach...

reviews.title: Picturesque coastline
reviews.text: Great place to see puffins flying around, although it is challenging to see from close. But the scenery is worth it.

reviews.title: Best black sand beach
reviews.text: This is a must see off the Ring Road in the south of Iceland, just about 20 minutes west of Vik. You can actually walk on the Black sand beach, with towering basalt columns next to you. You can even climb up and sit on a few of the pieces of basalt for a great photo opportunity. There are spectacular and interesting rock formations out in the water, but be aware that the crashing waves are very strong, so it’s recommended to stay a good distance from the shoreline. There are some small caves around as well, and in season apparently puffins frequently fly around here. My husband and I went on our honeymoon in September, so we were a little bit late for puffin viewing.

reviews.title: Black Stone Beach, Rock Structures, & Puffins
reviews.text: Black Sand Beach is listed as #1 in Vik for attractions, and this is the same place. It is more of black stone beach varying in all sizes, although there is some black sand as well. The waves here were quite strong so watching them crash onto shore as well as onto the large rocks farther down the beach was fascinating. You have some unique rock structures out in the water, basalt columns (like the Giants Causeway in Northern Ireland), and some jagged caves. All along the cliffs, there are puffins who swoop out over the beach to the water and back. We probably spent an hour here walking down the beach and looking at the puffins. I'd recommend a rain jacket here as Vik receives ~85" of rain per year. There is a cafe with sandwiches, drinks, and snacks as well as restrooms you can pay to use if you aren't buying anything. Vik is also 15 minutes east with a large store, restaurant, cafe, gas station, etc.

reviews.title: Your hair stands up!
reviews.text: One of the places I went and will forever be kept in my memory as a dark, creepy, dramatic place! All we heard was the sound of strong waves crushing. The way that the waves were building up in slow motion was unbelievable. You cannot miss this experience!

reviews.title: Beautiful!! But watch out for sneaker waves
reviews.text: You don’t want to miss the basalt columns on Reynisfjara beach. This can be a quick stop if you’re doing a day trip. However, keep in mind that this is a place to look at rocks, not a place to sit on a beach. There is a multitude of signs warning about sneaker waves, which can come up out of nowhere and catch you unaware, pulling you out into a rip tide. Don’t mess around with the ocean here—but DO go look at it an enjoy the incredible scenery. Also, while we were there the weather changed from sunny/blue skies to impenetrable fog in about 90 seconds. It was startling, but beautiful.

reviews.title: Eerie, beautiful and unforgettable
reviews.text: This is a must see.  Great place to unwind on a summer day. The cave-like structures create great photogenic moments in the Evening or morning sun.  By the way: one wouldn't expect a beach that is not made for sun bathing to be a good place for people watching, but this one certainly is.  There are always people who want to be seen no matter weather, location, etc. etc...

reviews.title: Fun black sand
reviews.text: Great spot for small kids. Can be windy and cold. Restaurant is located near by. Pictures are also great here with rocks to climb and carved out sides of the mountain.

reviews.title: Beach in Iceland
reviews.text: This was a beautiful sight!  The black beach was an incredible place to visit!  The basalt columns were very cool as well!  I am planning on returning this trip to enjoy again!

reviews.title: Columnar basalt, caves and pinnacles.
reviews.text: Columnar basalt towers out of the beach forming a huge cave in a church like arch. Just off the beach there are 2 pinnacles of rock. I was lucky to see a whale blow and broach just off shore. Great shore landscape and very beautiful in sun. Car park takes you quite close.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Absolutely stunning.This is a must go while visiting Iceland.black sand beach,basalt columns,rocks formation.Is windy and a little crowded but you will enjoy the real nature.

reviews.title: A beautiful site but oh so crowded!
reviews.text: As other reviewers say, this is a beautiful site and mother nature at its best. What bothered us is how the tourists are climbing all over the beautiful structures to get pictures of themselves sitting on the rock formations. Isn't it enough to just photograph the beauty? You really need to climb up on it? It was impossible to get a photo without other people in your photo so I had to step back very far away to capture this image. Parking in this area was very difficult. There are other beaches in this area that are easier to access, and a hike above will give you fantastic views!

reviews.title: Amazing structures!
reviews.text: If you visit Iceland, make sure this is one of your stops! It was so neat to see the basalt columns and the different directions the lava flowed at different times. Stunning!

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.text: This was the highlight of our trip to Vik.  The black sand beach, the puffins, other sea birds complimented by rock formations that are truly a marvel make this a worthwhile drive from Reykjavik.  The beach is split by the rocks so make sure exit to the black beach side that is prior to arriving in the town of Vik.  The wind was strong the day we visited, dress appropriately and realize conditions can change quite rapidly.

reviews.title: A stop is it worth
reviews.text: We had this stop on our tour across the ring road and it was amazing, I can’t tell you how awesome the Mother Earth in Iceland.

reviews.title: Beauty
reviews.text: one of my favorite destination spot.Such natural beauty and no park fees to enter.must see during summer.the sand in the beach is so different and texture is something my kids loved.awesome pic opportunities.during summer its breath taking

reviews.title: Another worthy stop
reviews.text: This is another good stop along the road.  Beautiful black beach with sea stacks out in the water.  Great photo ops.

reviews.title: Look out for puffins!
reviews.text: We saw some and it was awesome. Go for a bit and lay out on the beach. The texture is so interesting.

reviews.title: Absolute must see!
reviews.text: This beach would be amazing early or late with less tourists but even crowded with tourists it was amazing.  Between the basalt columns and black sand, it was spectacular.

reviews.title: My favorite place in Iceland
reviews.text: I loved the black sand, vestiges of rock, the fantastic caves, and watching the puffins flying in and out.  Worth the trip!

reviews.title: Go early or late
reviews.text: The experience at 7am was so much nicer than at 7pm, when there were multiple busloads of people, all trying to take a picture with the caves or the basalt columns (while not heeding any of the warnings about sneaker waves). It is beautiful, and more so when relatively empty :)

reviews.title: (Black sand beach) Nice to walk around
reviews.text: This is easily accessible. Lots of tourists. The sand is nice and it's a nice walk up and down the beach. There is a cave and cliffs - a very popular photo op. There is a restaurant onsite with bathrooms.

reviews.title: Beautiful geology
reviews.text: Gotta love nature. Great basalt columns. Wonderful rocks jutting up from the sea near the shore. Easy walk from the car park. No cost.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Worth a visit if in the area, but overrun by tour buses and camper vans throughout the day. So try to visit early or late in the day if visiting during summer.

reviews.title: Simply beautiful
reviews.text: So pretty.  This beach is popular but you can walk and be by yourself.  The sand is clean, the ocean very dangerous (so no swimming) but very, very picturesque.  A must see.

reviews.title: Beatiful but...
reviews.text: Ok let's start saying that the place is fantastic. The beach is black made of sand/pebbles. The rocks fantastic and on the horizon a great natural arch.The but it's only that it is so popular that there were too many buses.But the beach deserves a toir from the ring road.

reviews.title: A tourist hot spot
reviews.text: A popular tourist hotspot, and for good reason. The geography is drastic and stunning. About a 2.5 hour drive from Reykjavik, we arrived at the beaches at about 5:30 pm in the evening, and the beaches were still swarmed with tourists. We spent about an hour here, and we didn't even walk the full length of the beach. You could easily spend ~3 hours here if you wanted to explore. There is parking, and there is a visitor centre/cafe/restrooms on site (restrooms either cost money or are free if you purchase something at the cafe). Obey signs to be careful around the water; sneaker waves (wave that are disproportionately large in size and sneak up on you) have sucked several tourists out to sea.

reviews.title: Beautiful... but busy!
reviews.text: The beach itself is an amazing wonder of the world! Huge waves hit the black sand and striking cliffs. It is truly a place to see while in Iceland! Which is why it seemed half of the tourists population was there... if you walk further down the beach away from everyone you may get a moment of solitude! We climbed over one of the rock walls (carefully!) and were alone on a side. Even saw some puffins flying around!! My only complaint was that the bathrooms cost 200 krona :(

reviews.title: Another Awe Inspiring Icelandic site!
reviews.text: Part of an over ten hour tour of the south coast. After seeing pictures of this online my visit to Iceland would not have been complete without going here. Absolutely beautiful. The volcanic formed basalt columns, sharp rising cliff, black sand beach-all amazing. Pay attention to the warning signs at the beginning-this is a beautiful but dangerous beach if you do not pay attention to the guidelines. There is a small cafe and gift shop on site, but I preferred spending the time here on the beach. If you go to the town of Vik you will be able to get a better view of the three trolls formation.

reviews.title: Basalt and beach and islands
reviews.text: Awesome basalt rock formations on side of mountain.  Can wonder aimlessly on this wonderful beach.  Ver cool rock formations in ocean.  Too many tourists... ruins photos

reviews.title: Nice walk on the coast with spectacular rock formations
reviews.text: Ample parking, even though it's a fairly large tourist site.  Pebble rocks mostly to walk on, however, if you get closer to the water you can enjoy some sand.  Super cool rock features and short walk to reach the end.

reviews.title: Nice beach along the coast in Iceland
reviews.text: I came here as part of a day-trip with other tourists, we stopped by this beach and I walked along it, also towards the rock formation part. It is very nice, but very cold, much different to the sandy, hot beaches in Australia where I am from. Still, it is a landmark tourists should visit.

reviews.title: Nice beach and rock formation
reviews.text: Another beautiful spot in Iceland which one must visit and admire the beauty. But be mindful of mass tourism.

reviews.title: No one walks the Beach
reviews.text: This is another crowded tourist spot with tons of ppl taking pictures of rock formations. No one was exploring the rest of the beach. My husband and I took the opportunity to walk the length of the beach with our baby in solitude, it was quite lovely.

reviews.title: An absolute must visit!
reviews.text: Amazing scenery.  Yes there are alot of tourists but with good reason.The black sand beach is cool, but it's the basalt rock formation that's the real star, it was incredible, and climbable (which my kids loved, including my 18 year old who is usually too cool for stuff like that).  Interesting caves, birds nesting in the crevices including puffins (although to be honest more gulls than puffins).  Less than 10 minutes off the main road so very easy to get to, if you are in the area you absolutely must stop and see it.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: We stopped at the beach as part of our Southern Tour. The beach has beautiful black and (or whatever it is that you are walking on). Nice caves too.

reviews.title: Spectacular!
reviews.text: This beach is surreal with coal black sand and towering cliffs comprised of rectangular rock formations. Wear your hiking boots!

reviews.title: Black sand and basalt columns all in one!
reviews.text: This beach was so cool! We saw black pebble sand and basalt columns on this beach. This is also where we saw puffins hanging out on the cliffs!

reviews.title: Tourist beach, but beautiful
reviews.text: A friend and I spent some time at Reynisfjara Beach while staying in Vik. The locals refer to it as the beach for the tourists, so expect a crowded parking lot and beach, but it is definitely worth a stop... especially since there is not much to do in Vik. We would recommend coming at off times to avoid heavier crowds. The beach is unique with the black sand and rock formations. There are some caves and some rock formations that tourists can climb on to take pictures. There are crashing waves, and signs warn people from swimming as it can be dangerous. It is most beautiful on a clear summer day, when you can relax on the sand and feel the sun beaming on you.

reviews.title: Trolls turned to rock
reviews.text: We were lucky to have a beautiful sunny day for this amazing place.  The black beaches, basalt columns caves and of course Reynisdrangar (the big rocks), the story goes that there were three trolls who were trying to pull a boat ashore.  When the sun came up they were turned to stone.  Free parking with a wee restraint (toilets).  My children aged 10 & 11 really enjoyed this place.

reviews.title: Amazing place in an amazing town
reviews.text: Vik is not to be missed...one of our fave stops in all of Iceland. The variety of black sands and rock formations in this area are amazing, and bird life is plentiful and easy to view if you have binos or a scope. Take your time and try to avoid the crowds--midnight sun was great for us. I definitely want to spend more time in this area, and on this beach, on future visits.

reviews.title: Wonderful view of rock structures and beautiful beach
reviews.text: Just a wonderful beach with amazing topography. It's worth a stop on your trip through Vik to see the rectangular columns that line the beach. You might catch a glimpse of a puffin as you are in the area.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: 7 years ago we tried visiting this beach but couldn’t because it was puffin nesting season (late May, early June). This year we were able to visit in late June and it was worth it! We went about 9 pm and it had quite a few tourists. I definitely recommend going at odd hours if possible to avoid the busses. It was just a fun place to explore, take photos, enjoy nature, look for cool rocks, and watch for Puffins up high on the rocks. A must-see.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Worth the crowded parking lot! Walk away from the crowds for better perspective - and bring gloves. Did not eat here there is food, WCs, and picnic tables.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviews.text: We absolutely loved our time at this beach.  We were able to spot puffins and walk around to take pictures.  As Game of Thrones fan, it was fun to see where some scenes have been shot.  We also ate a late dinner at the restaurant on the beach - great fish/chips!

reviews.title: Gorgeous Volcanic Beach
reviews.text: Same Review for the Black Sand Beach.Practice saying the name!Come early or after 5pm to avoid tourist buses and walk the whole beach

reviews.title: Great Photos of a Unique Beach!
reviews.text: I have been disappointed visiting black sand beaches in other parts of the world, but this one was large and wide and actually sandy!  There are unique geologic views in all directions and I took so many pictures hoping to capture the beauty of this diverse place.  If you head west on the ring road and take the turnoff to the lighthouse area (but do not go up the steep dirt road), you can see this beach from a distance and you get a whole new perspective on the beach area.

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text: Totally different from everthing I have ever seen! The landscape is absolutely amazing and wowing! There is free parking and a visitor centre with foods and drinks!

reviews.title: Brace yourself for daytime crowds
reviews.text: We first arrived in the late afternoon but couldn’t even get into the car park for all the tour busses. We came again in the late evening (after 9pm) and it was still crowded but at least there was space to park. The amazing basalt cliffs are so worth seeing that it’s worth the struggle to take a selfie without hundreds of other tourists in the shot. You’ll need a minimum of 30 minutes.

reviews.title: Unlike Any Other Beach
reviews.text: Quite the natural wonder with the black sand (more like small pebbles), jagged rocky outcrops, and basalt columns.I would recommend going off hours as this spot is crawling with tourists and you likely won't get a nice pic of the sea stacks because everyone is climbing all over them. Regardless, you need to check it out!

reviews.title: Very special place
reviews.text: This is like no other beach I have seen. Black sand with tons of nice rocks. The surrounding mountain is just spectacular. Be careful with the waves though, don't go too close. Now and then someone had to run towards the inner side of the beach not to get wet.Free parking close by.A must visit if you are in the area!

reviews.title: Time stood still
reviews.text: During winter, the sun seems to rise and set on the same horizon...you will lost track of time easy...the black pebble beach provide such contrast to the sea and gave you an eerily soothing mood that you will not experience else where. Take your time to soak it in.

reviews.title: Just simply beautiful
reviews.text: The scenery is unbelievable.  Lots of tourists, but it's a must seen.  The road getting there is also beautiful.  The waves are dangerous, so don't come too close to the water because it'll pull you out to sea

reviews.title: Spectacular, Unique scenery
reviews.text: The black sand/pebbles, the trippy basalt columns, the dramatic seascape with the two iconic pillars rising out of the ocean..just really incredible. Cafe serves good food/coffee/hot chocolate too.

reviews.title: Viking Ship
reviews.text: Can't miss it from the Black Sand Beech.  It truly looks like a Viking Ship.  It's only 3 minutes off the Main Road so don't miss it.

reviews.title: Hidden gem
reviews.text: We went for a walk after dinner and happened upon this amazing beach! Just about had it all to ourselves. The scenery is spectacular. It was so different from our earlier experience at Dyrholaey which was super crowded. Maybe it was the time of day but we felt very fortunate to have discovered this hidden gem.

reviews.title: Fantastic rock formations along the coastline
reviews.text: Beautiful black sand beach with huge outcroppings in the water, and some amazing rock formations along the beach itself. Great backdrops for photos, but beware the power and reach of the waves.

reviews.title: Iceland’s own Giant Causeway
reviews.text: Fabulous long stretch of black sand with stunning cliff face and piped display of hexagonal rock columns. Extremely photogenic, don’t miss. 10 minutes from Vik. Facilities available.Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful.

reviews.title: Mystic beach in cloudy weather
reviews.text: Very special place made more so by rainy overcast weather. Lots of people, cars and buses but worth the visit. Basalt columns spectacular.

reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.text: Even though it was a cloudy day it was pretty with a lot of photo ops great rock formations a place to visit when in the Vik area.

reviews.title: Nice, but crowded
reviews.text: This is a picturesque black sand beach, close to Vik.  There is a parking lot, and a cafe.  There is also pay WCs.It’s worth a quick stop to snap some pictures, but good luck getting ones without people in them.

reviews.title: Great place to see nature at its best!
reviews.text: This spot is another one of Iceland's don't miss stops. It has many natural wonders, the basalt columns of the cliff, the immense waves breaking on the black stone beach, the puffins all show the power of nature. Listen to the signs regarding the waves - could easily see someone getting in trouble at high tide if trapped in the area just past the columns.

reviews.title: One of my favorite days in Iceland
reviews.text: My wife and I visited Iceland for an extended weekend and one of the days, we rented a car and drove to Vik.  We stopped off at a couple of waterfalls the were absolutely beautiful but my favorite experience of that day was Reynisfjara Beach.  It reminded me of a trip to the Grand Canyon, pictures can't capture what is so special about this place. (Even though I will include some!)  The basalt cliffs are just so massive and just rise straight up from the beach.  The beach isn't sand but tiny black pebbles that have been worn down over the millennia. Don't just stay in Reykjavik.  Get out and see Reynisfjara Beach and the sights along the way.  You will be so happy you did!

reviews.title: Not your average beach
reviews.text: This beach is definitely not your average everyday go-to beach. Not only is the color of the sand black instead of yellow, it is also Iceland’s most dangerous beach, due to its unforeseen gigantic waves. Although this beach and it’s scenery is to be enjoyed with caution, the stone carvings in the cliffs which the waves have created over the decades are definitely worth it. We really enjoyed ourselves, and if you’re nearby, a stop here is worthwhile!

reviews.title: I love this beach
reviews.text: This really is not your typical beach. From my understanding you will not be able to swim here because of the sneaker waves.  The waves were very large and fun to watch break into the shore.  They also have the basalt columns to climb on which is fun.  The basalt columns are pretty darn cool to see.  The landscape is beautiful around the beach.  It is definitely worth a stop.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Who doesn't love a black sand beach? Beautiful rock formations, crashing waves, and birds all around.  A great place to stop and site see if you are in the Vik area.

reviews.title: We liked it
reviews.text: Visited at 23:00 in June.  Plenty of light and people.  Amazing geologic formations.  Did not hike to the top of the hill - did not realize until the next day the trail head is on the other side of the mountain, in Vik.

reviews.title: MORE FOR THE COLOUR THAN ANYTHING ELSE
reviews.text: It was a bit miserable when we toured the area, not seeing it at its best. Apart from the black colour of the sand, the basalt formations behind the beach were as photographic. The chance to see the 'stacks' our in the waters was also good

reviews.title: Pretty place even spotted a puffin
reviews.text: The rocks in the water are pretty cool. Don’t go in the morning it’s covered with your buses. We stayed at the black beach suites so we were able to go back in the evening. The rocks are nice as well. We even spotted a puffin. The only puffin we saw during our 5 days in Vik.

reviews.title: Definite "Must See" (watch for rogue waves)
reviews.text: Very impressive with a "Game of Thrones" vibe. Gorgeous scenary with a resteraunt on site. WC=bathroom (200ISK). Excellent way to spend the day. Not safe for swimming. Limited access for wheelchair/strollers.

reviews.title: Puffins!
reviews.text: So glad we went to this beach. Our tour guide told is how we could tell the difference when spotting a puffin. The puffins wings flap twice as fast as the other birds in that area.

reviews.title: The Black Beach
reviews.text: Stunning views. Black cliffs. Rough waves. I’m pretty sure that in an episode of the Vikings History Channel series, Floki landed on this very beach when he reached Iceland. We came here on a tour, so we had limited time, but I wish we could have spent more. The basalt columns, caves, and maybe - if you’re lucky - a puffin. This location is iconic to Iceland. How could one not visit?

reviews.title: Worth the time to stop
reviews.text: Reynisfjara beach is worth the time for a stop while on the Ring road near Vik. Wonderful black beach and basalt columns and caves. Beach is really black pebbles not sand which is kind of neat. Will be crowed with tourists in the summer. Walk away from the area closest the parking lot and you can somewhat get away from the crowd. Come late or early in the day for less of a crowd. Huge waves are fun to watch, but do not try to wade or swim here, as waves can knock you down. Enjoy the area

reviews.title: Blew me away
reviews.text: This is black sand beach. Stunning! Do this with Dyrhólaey Rocks, because it’s close by. Amazing place, and yes, the waves really can get big and eat one up 😱

reviews.title: It's Iceland, not Hawaii...
reviews.text: Definitely worth a visit. Black volcanic sand beach, basalt columns and caves, and of course the sea. It's a windy place so be prepared. There's not much of a town but it's about the scenery. It's the southern route so it's a long drive, but scenic.

reviews.title: Very Popular
reviews.text: Called here on our way to Vik A very popular place to visit and a nice restaurant close to the beach, not overly expensive and a good selection of food

reviews.title: A magical beach .....
reviews.text: This is an amazing beach with beautiful black sand,  basalt block on the caves where all the tourists stand and incredible rock formations spitting out of the sea. The key is to walk away from the tourists to enjoy some incredible photo shoots opportunity. We walked the beach and given that the tourists tend to be on a tight schedule, we had the beach to ourselves. The waves can be dangerous so follow the warning signs. There is also a restaurant with bathrooms if needed and there is a lot of parking. Try morning or late afternoon to avoid the load of buses full of tourists.

reviews.title: Greta basalt columns at the beach & beautiful black sand
reviews.text: Big free car park with a toilet, cafe & snack hut with the famous Icelandic Plysur (hot dog)The basalt columns down to the black sand are amazing but congested with people taking selfies! The sea crashes into the black sand & pebbles & you have a great view to the sea stacks.Visit early morning or late evening to avoid the crowds

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: A beautiful and spectacular beach with black sand, basalt rocks and spectacular rock formations.The beach can be dangerous, because of the waves that can swollow you and take you to the sea. At least 5 warning signs tells you that on the way from the parking to the beach.As in many of the biggest attractions in Iceland, it is difficult to take pictures without having a lot of people in it. But it would be unfair to call it crowdy, because the beach is so big.

reviews.title: One of the "must sees" of Iceland.
reviews.text: Stunning rock formations. It is worth to take your time and explore the area, especially in the direction to the Vik. Time it correctly and watch out the deadly sneaker waves!

reviews.title: Must go! Great scenery and hexagonal rock formations!
reviews.text: Lovely beach with black sands and great scenery and the hexagonal rock formations was amazing! Quite unforgettable scenes from there!

reviews.title: The most beautiful place on Earth!
reviews.text: I am in love with this place! I didn't expect it is so beautiful - the mysterious atmosphere, huge waves, black sand, specific caves and stones - everything sums up to a beautiful experience. Have a walk and look on the ground - the sand and little black rocks are amazing. Also, for the Game of Thrones fans - it was featured in some of the episodes.

reviews.title: Worth a detour
reviews.text: Impressive place to visit when in the Vik area. I like the black beach and the rock formations - it’s a very impressive place. Need to be wary of the waves ! We went on a grey misty day - very atmospheric !

reviews.title: Volcanic Beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with caves, rock formations, and really cool basaltic columns.  They say it is a black sand beach, but it is more like gravel.  It did make it a little challenging to walk along the beach.  Columns are totally fun to climb and play around on.  Lots of sea birds to view as well.  There was a cute little restaurant right next to the beach as well for hungry visitors.

reviews.title: watch out for sneaker waves
reviews.text: it's a beautiful beach, but crowded and too cold to swim. it can also kill you, so maybe young kids should avoid the surf line.

reviews.title: Gorgeous!
reviews.text: We were fortunate to visit this beach on a sunny, almost windless day. Our tour director told us that we probably wouldn't last more than a few minutes on a very windy day. It's difficult to even describe this place and difficult to capture its uniqueness in photographs. The basalt columns, the fine black sand, the ferocity of the ocean all add to the otherworldliness of this place. This beach was also seen in Season 7 of Game of Thrones!

reviews.title: Amazing views.  Saw puffins too.
reviews.text: The rock formations are amazing.  The sea is beautiful and the landscape, its volcanos reaching for the sea, make you realize that you have have found a truly remarkable place.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: No pictures justify the beauty of this place. Go early to avoid the swarming tourists and the best light. Wear comfortable shoes to be able to climb on to the rocks.

reviews.title: Spectacular spot; do not miss!
reviews.text: This is a truely beautiful bit of scenery, what Iceland is all about.Unique is just one adjective to decribe this piece of geography.

reviews.title: Cool but black beaches are better
reviews.text: On the bucket list. As cool as well like black beaches. But you should visit it as well. Restrooms available. 200ISk

reviews.title: Cold but beautiful!
reviews.text: Worth a visit if you're road tripping around Iceland, or are staying in the area.Even though the weather was not great during out 7 day vacation, the 2 days we got to leave the hotel were amazing!!We went in April and it was beyond cold, making being near the beach even worse. The weather was a mix of monsoon and blizzard for most of our trip but when the sky broke, we added Vik onto our Golden Circle Trip.Vik:I will say, although I loved seeing this, I wouldn't make a special trip just to see this with nothing else planned. Vik was 3 hours away from our hotel and made for a very long night. It is so beautiful to see the landscape unfold onto black sands with raging waves; however, there is not much to do in this exact spot. On the way to here though you can stop off and see the fallen aircraft. I forget what it's name is right now.Now, when we went it felt like 10 degrees out so after about 20/25min, we couldn't take the cold anymore. It was piercing and burning your skin. DRESS WARMLY! It's honestly the only advice I can give you. We dressed bundled up and were still frozen because of the time of year and the wind. Having said that, if you go in nicer weather or can withstand cold better than we could, you are not rushed out & can stay for as long as you want. You also do not need to pay to get in to see this which is nice. Because we really only spent 20min here, is it worth a whole special trip just for it? I don't really think so...BUT, if you are seeing other things, then hell yea, go. Its stunning!!Parking:There is parking in walking distance to the beachFood:There are towns nearby from that offer some restaurant choices that you can eat in. We went to one, I cant recall the name, and waited about 30min before being sat. It was a cool little place and the food was good and moderately priced. We were exhausted thought from a long day and left at around 9pm.Bottom Line: Worth the experience if you do other things in this area as well.

reviews.title: Beautiful views with beach and basalt columns
reviews.text: This was my favorite site visited that day. The beach was made of very fine black sand. We had fun climbing on the columnar basalt formations around Halsanefshellir Cave. The views from the beach to the ocean were great, and crashing waves added to the drama. We had to watch for sneaker waves which are dangerous and have claimed multiple lives at this beach.

reviews.title: Landscape for movies
reviews.text: I have seen volcanic ash beaches elsewhere in the world, but this one combines different elements that make it seem like the ideal movie set landscape. And if you are not a director is still a prime location for photo shooting. You need to drive some 5km from the main road to reach it. Parking is free and there is a cafe on the end of the parking lot. The sand is black and is overshadowed by a cliff some 300m high with basaltic steep rocks, couple of caves and some large rocks on either side of the beach. do not get too close to the water since there are warnings about the sudden waves that might drag you in. 30min should be enough for your photo session.

reviews.title: Beautiful but packed.
reviews.text: This beach is truly stunning even on a rainy day. Parking is close to the beach access and there’s plenty of it, as well as two food establishments. The only downside was all of the people. It’s a very busy site making for hard to capture photos.

reviews.title: Must-Do
reviews.text: This isn't a place for the kids to run wild. The incoming waves can be dangerous, but not a problem if you don't get too close. The cove and the rock formations are definitely worth the stop. Great photos to be had here.

reviews.title: Basalt stacks are a must see!
reviews.text: We came here on our Grayline South Iceland tour and were able to spend about 30-45 minutes here at this beach. I wish we had had more time to explore further down the cliffs and the sand because it was so gorgeous and there were lots of little caves that I wanted to peak my head into. The basalt stacks are the main draw of this beach, and you will feel like you're at Dragonstone if you watch Game of Thrones. The water here at this beach is dangerous with large waves and strong tides so if you're going to go close to the water make sure you're vigilant and careful. I went close and ended up getting soaking wet because I didn't expect the tide to come up as far as it did. Also a great beach to take some sand if you want that as a souvenir (I took a bunch). A very cool beach!

reviews.title: Smashing beach. Saw puffins here
reviews.text: Went at 10am. Cliffs are worth a visit on their own to see the rock formations. Round the basalt rocks the puffins were flying.

reviews.title: An awesome beach with spectacular rock formations
reviews.text: This is one awesome black sand beach with many strange rock formations including the Halsanefshellir Cave, the Basalt Sea Stacks and the Dyrholaey (door hole island) all in one stretch. The wave was powerful so beware and do not get too close to the water. Weather not so clear on my day of visit so everything looked greyish. It must feel much better on a bright clear day. It was quite windy so dress up for the walk.

reviews.title: A wonderful ocean view.
reviews.text: A wonderful ocean view.  A great site for taking pictures.  A nice place to take time to relax and enjoy the view.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Automatic five stars just because I’ve never seen a black beach before. I’m from New Jersey so the beach is nothing new to me but I’ve never seen sand like this. Not only did the sun glisten off the sharp black sand but the waves and rock formations added to the beauty. The sand was so soft and silky. The basalt columns made for a great photo opportunity. When people say be aware of the waves they aren’t kidding. They can be very powerful even when close to the shoreline.

reviews.title: Seriously amazing!
reviews.text: Just be prepared for the wind and unpredictable weather occasions. It is extremely dangerous to go near water, so follow the instructions. It looks stunning, you will enjoy every minute spent here! rock formations are unbelievable!

reviews.title: Beautiful Nature
reviews.text: Stunning rock formations, an eerie lack of color, winds powerful enough to take your glasses and hat flying, and waves so powerful and humbling-- Reynisfjara Beach was a very unique experience. Do take noted precautions regarding the waves-- the sheer power of each wave is unlike anything I have ever seen. The rock formations are very intricate and it is exciting to be able to get so close as to touch the different textures of each formation. Our stop here felt about 15 degrees F colder than any of our other stops, so I would recommend an extra jacket or layer to stay warm here. Also, be aware there is a fee to use the restroom at this stop.

reviews.title: Interesting rock formations
reviews.text: Worth a stop, interesting rock formations.  The power of the ocean can really be felt by the breaking waves.

reviews.title: Unlike Anything I've Ever Seen
reviews.text: The rock formations here are spectacular.  While the beach was crowded and windy, it was still quite beautiful.  I was able to get a lot of photos even with all of the people visiting.

reviews.title: A great way to see the North Atlantic Ocean
reviews.text: This was a fun location to spend some time at. The cliffs and rocks were very unique and cool. It was also fun to actually touch the Atlantic ocean at the high latitude, seeing water the temperature was.

reviews.title: Powerful waves (of tourists)
reviews.text: Even on a clouded day in May this beach was swarming with people disregarding all danger sign that warned against the waves that have claimed lives before. The power of the waves (even the normal ones) is stunning and the rock formations very special.

reviews.title: So Busy
reviews.text: We drove the ring road clockwise and made this our last stop before Reykjavík. Because it is so close to where a majority of people stay, it was so incredibly crowded, taking away from the beauty. Dozens of photographers lined up along the beach, a music video being recorded and a professional photo shoot all took away from the natural landscape. Still loved the giant waves rolling in and the lava rock columns, but should have waited until after midnight when the crowds die down.

reviews.title: Stunning Black Beach
reviews.text: This is the same as the Black Sand Beach. It is vast, powerful waves crashing into the black sand, stunning columns and an amazing cave. I am so glad to come here. It was one of my highlights on my visit to Iceland.

reviews.title: Stunning but better photographed from the beach in Vik
reviews.text: Stopped here on our way to Vik. Breathtakingly beautiful rock formations called Reynisdrangar, but can be better photographed from the beach in Vik.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: Bucket list! You hav e to visit this Beach if you visit Iceland, 1h 45 m drive from Reykjarvik. Big Waves around 8-10 m hit the bich when we was there. A couples of People get hit of the Waves and get really wet. This Waves are very Dangerous so be careful. The Black Columns and "Troll rocks" is just fantastic.

reviews.title: Amazing & dramatic
reviews.text: One of our top 3 sights in Iceland. Dramatic and beautiful. Sea cave with basalt stone pillars and a wide beach, but heed the warnings about rogue waves.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: This beach is one of the best beaches I saw while in Iceland. The sand, water, cave, and rock formations in the ocean were spectacular.

reviews.title: Basalt Columns and sneaker waves
reviews.text: It's about a 3 hour drive from Reykjavik, but definitely worth a visit. the columns are visually stunning and you get to check out a very cool cave or two. Be careful of the waves, they really do sneak up on you!

reviews.title: Unbelievable experience!!
reviews.text: A must see when in Iceland...you won't regret it.  We took a bus tour from Reykjavik, and while the tour took the whole day, we got to see some of the most memorable sites.  Well worth it!

reviews.title: Don’t miss this beach
reviews.text: This beach has really cool black sand and pebbles as well as geometric basalt rock formations. Just a few minutes west of Vik, the views are great and there are fun rocks to climb and caves to check out. Be careful of the waves, there are warning signs at the entrance but some people still get too close and are surprised by sneaker waves.

reviews.title: Very unique beach that you can't miss
reviews.text: Just down the road from Dyrhólaey, Reynisfjara is the unique black pebble beach with sheer cliffs and geometric basalt columns. Be careful of the powerful tides and waves - people have been dragged out to sea here from not being alert! Parking: Large lot at the base of cafe/gift shopTrail(s): >2-3km walk along beach to end. Smooth black pebble beach is easy to walk along.Traffic: Golden Circle stop - heavy traffic.The smooth pebble beach is comfortable to walk on

reviews.title: Gorgeous Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: My folks and I really enjoyed visiting this beach. The combination of rocky black sand and blue water is really quite stunning, as are the basalt columns of the cliff overlooking the beach. I definitely recommend stopping here!

reviews.title: Sunset on the beach
reviews.text: This black sand beach is beautiful. The water is extremely rough and the contrast of the black sand with the crashing white waves is amazing. You landscape is magnificent too. There’s a cave you can walk into and some cool rock formations when you get to the beach.

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: This is another area that the Game of Thrones shot at if you're into that sort of thing. It was a rainy day so we didn't have an issue with it being too crowded. We took cover in the basalt rock cave.

reviews.title: Black Beach
reviews.text: This is a must go place when you visit Iceland. Southeast of Reykjavik you will find a stunning scenery of rock formations in the sea that almost look alien.

reviews.title: Gorgeous!!
reviews.text: You can walk along the rocks and enjoy the view, you can travel down closer to the beach and be fascinated by rock columns, etc. Highly recommended

reviews.title: Very crowded
reviews.text: The cliffs are beautiful, but let's be honest - the volume of people at this place was ridiculous, even in the middle of winter. I can't even imagine what it would be like in the middle of summer. I would definitely steer clear of this place.

reviews.title: Iceland Coastline
reviews.text: Beautiful black sand beach with the rocks jutting out of the water. Quite a site and there are no shells, just round shiny  black and grey rocks.

reviews.title: Very nice scenery with a lot of other people
reviews.text: The black beach offers a nice scenic view and the basalt columns are fascinating. It does get super crowded though and everybody tries to take their picture sitting on the columns.

reviews.title: Soaring basalt cliffs
reviews.text: This is a beautiful black sand beach, but definitely NOT of the sunbathing/swimming kind. Here you can appreciate the powerful waves of the ocean, admire the soaring sea cliffs with sea birds, look for perfectly polished pebbles and rocks, and examine the stunning geology of the basalt columns. Do be careful of small children and heed the warning of the signs...the waves are like nothing you've ever experienced regardless of when you visit and you WILL be swept if you're not paying attention. NEVER turn your back to the ocean!

reviews.title: Amazing geology
reviews.text: This is a lovely beach with lots of geology and rock formations to admire. The geological formations are formed by the volcanic activity on the island. It is a lovely walk along the beach and I would recommend doing it on a day when there isn't so much wind so that it is easier to see the scenery.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and caves
reviews.text: Beautiful cave, beach and rock formations along the black sand beach. Only 1m walk from the car park which meant if this is your last stop on a full days south coast adventuring you don't have far to walk!Free parking and cafe onsite by the car park. Toilets are available but you do have to pay (which you can do by card)

reviews.title: Striking and dramatic beach
reviews.text: This striking volcanic beach was well worth the drive from Reykjavik- dramatic black sand, crashing waves, soaring cliffs, large caves and the utterly unique basalt columns all make for a beach unlike any other. As others have noted, be sure to read the warning signs and exercise caution at the water's edge.

reviews.title: Black sand beach
reviews.text: Drive road 215 all the way to the end, trough the small village, to the big parking area with a small restaurant. The black sand beach was crowded by tourists, but it's so huge that everyone could do their own thing. Nice to get out of the car and have a short walk and take some pictures.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Quickly stopped in here in between Skaftafell and Hella. The beach is beautiful and the columns are incredible. Just be careful of sneaker waves! Cafe at the beach also available.

reviews.title: Black Sand Beach
reviews.text: A scenic beach on black sand where Dilwale movie was shot- a nice cave and troll freezes in the sea - but the waves can be dangerous

reviews.title: Reynesfjara, Black beach, South Iceland.
reviews.text: Reynisfjara is situated about 160 kms from Reykjavik and can also be covered in a day trip from the capital.It is all the more popular because of its association with the famous series ‘Game of Thrones’. The black sandy beach has an outer-worldly setting, with its white foamy waves crashing in all its might against the black shoreline, the foam and the spray rising up in the air.  Strong gusts of winds blows at you from the ocean and brings with it the moisture and the spray. The black monoliths which stand out from the sea about 500 meters into the water seems to preside over the whole show.  The black beach is majestic and surreal in its appeal. Nature around here is made up of shades of Black and white. No wonder, Reynesfjara is considered  one of the most beautiful beaches in Iceland.We stayed for close to an hour when suddenly  it started to drizzle and in a few minutes large drops of  rain pelted at us from the sky. It was time to rush for cover. Though   Hálsanefshellir  can provide some quick shelter, we decided to pack up and leave. Up near the car park, their is a well decked cafeteria with rest rooms and hot beverages for the weary traveler, which we made good use of. I was driving a Jeep Cherokee and mind you it is a wonderful car to have in such rugged and wild terrain . So my suggestion would be to pick up a sturdy car, preferable an SUV if you plan to do a similar road trip in Iceland.

reviews.title: Go at low tide
reviews.text: If you can manage to get to the beach at low tide, go around the two caves and climb over the rocks. This will treat you to a climb through a small natural rock arch and then a view of the sea formations from the other side! Beware of the water (people die each year from the massive undertow of the sneaker waves), so if tide is coming in, don’t chance it. Instead you can drive around to the town of Vik and get a picture that way, just not as up close and impressive!

reviews.title: A black sand beach with sneaky waves
reviews.text: Not much to say about it.  It was a black sand beach and with warning signs about sneaky waves.  These waves could wash you away back into the ocean.  They showed the number of people who lost their lives last year.  It is part of the tour to and just one of many places in Iceland.

reviews.title: beautiful
reviews.text: this was my favorite tour, always wanted to see black beaches, it was spectacular,the rock formations so unique. the sand so textured,amazing to touch. it was spectacular,true beauty

reviews.title: Very impressive rock formations
reviews.text: Don’t miss if you’re in the area. Nice beach to walk along and fab cave and rock formations. Didn’t go into the cafe but it’s well positioned by the beach

reviews.title: A photographic wonderland
reviews.text: We visited in November, in the midst of a downpour. Even so, there were quite a few tourists here, so I'd recommend visiting in the off season (winter) if you want to avoid crowds. The beach is stunning with its polished black lava rocks and hypnotic, threatening, pounding surf.  (PLEASE be careful and don't turn your back on or wade into the water - it's a riptide that will suck you out to sea. During our 30 minutes here we saw several clueless tourists nearly get knocked off their feet, and my own boots got wet from an unexpectedly high rising tide.)The lava flow formations and basalt columns are fascinating.Worth the 2.5-hour drive from Reykjavik, especially if you allow yourself enough time to make it part of a south-coast tour.

reviews.title: Great looking beach but not for swimming
reviews.text: The late March day we visited the beach was windy, overcast and cold. Even then the place was quite busy and crowded. The sea was quite rough so we maintained a respectful distance to the crashing waves but even on such a day the place was quite photogenic. Avoiding the crowd was a challenge but we still managed a few decent photos but avoided climbing the famous basalt columns. A must see place if  you are in Vik.

reviews.title: Not such a magical experience
reviews.text: I would either visit early morning or late evening as during the day this beach gets run over with coaches. Parking is nearly impossible  near the restaurant. The restaurant is not worth it. However, the beach is wonderful if you walk a bit from the main entry point and the basal columns.

reviews.title: Stop on the southern Iceland tour
reviews.text: Black sand beach and some impressive rock formations. Make sure you look up at the cliffs to see the variations in rock colours and their structure. Well worth visiting

reviews.title: Great and unique beach!
reviews.text: This place is well-known in Iceland and can be very crowded.I recommend you to come early in the morning if you want to take clear photos or use very long exposure to 'eliminate' the people there.

reviews.title: Really Interesting
reviews.text: I really recommend coming here. The geology is absolutely stunning, and you can walk along the black beach past the popular basalt columns to see other formations and get a view of the formations off the coast. So much black, along with the wiping wind and crashing waves made this area a memorable experience for me.

reviews.title: Wonderful beach, photographer's dream
reviews.text: As you get to the beach you see the rock formations and basalt columns formed as a result of vulcanology.  A bit irritating to find (as a keen photographer) a group of British schoolkids all sitting on the columnar forms while their teacher explained their formation - the kids, though, were absorbed in the phones and looking out to sea.  Shame they were polishing with their nether regions the things that they should have been polishing their intellects on - and they didn't half get in the way of those of us who like taking photographs.  Oh well; Iceland trip?  Box ticked.  Columnar basaltic forms?  Box ticked.The waves were wonderful; not seen anything like those on a beach since living in Orkney some years ago.  Good for the soul.

reviews.title: Stunning black lava beach!
reviews.text: Even in horrible weather this beach is stunning. Caves and rock formations on beach and offshore are amazing. Another "must see".

reviews.title: One of the must-see stops on the island
reviews.text: No trip to Iceland can be complete without a stop on this famous beach. The place is just out of this world. The weather and waves can get scary in a heartbeat, but this just contributes to the magic of the place.

reviews.title: Beautiful Site
reviews.text: For a very senior citizen, this was a hard hike, but the reward is there.  Nature created beautiful sculpture overlooking the black sand beach and out in the water.

reviews.title: Simply amazing
reviews.text: I loved this place. Having a love for geology this is a fascinating and intricately detailed place to visit. The sands are wonderfully black (when wet) and the sound of the surf breaking along with the hills overhead is a perfect accompaniment.  A word of warning, the beach is very busy with people and coaches are arriving and departing all the time. If you are looking to take more professional photos then you will have to be patient and lucky to get shots without throngs of people.

reviews.title: Wowee
reviews.text: A mini giants causeway on a volcanic sand beach. Absolutely freezing in the month of March but nonetheless stunning.

reviews.title: Worlds most beautiful beach (for Goths)
reviews.text: This is probably the best most memorable place I've visited in Iceland.Black sand with giant waves and giants causeway style rock formations as well as others all very stunning.And the breathtaking cave incredible!Beware of the sneaky waves turn you back on them for too long and they will try and snatch you! Do not get too close the undercurrents will drag you off before anyone can react!Definitely be coming back here!

reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: It was rammed with bus tours! But one thing we have learned on our trip to Iceland is that people that go on bus tours generally only walk about 100 yards. Persevere, power through the crowds and take in this black beach with geometric basalt cliffs.

reviews.title: Lovely beach....
reviews.text: .....and perfect vuews, it's just a shame it's so busy that you can't get a photo without someone else being in it!!

reviews.title: Very cool!
reviews.text: When I went it had been snowing and it was super windy. It was actually the worst weather of my trip. And it's half the reason I love it, it was so dramatic. There's a cafe and toilets nearby, just don't got too close to the beach or get stuck in any of the caves.

reviews.title: If Tim Burton directed your summer holiday
reviews.text: The little coastal town of Vik is sort of in the middle of nowhere, so sadly not many people get to see this incredible black sand beach. It's quite strange to see, as I'd never seen anything like it before. With the crashing waves and the jagged rocks out in the ocean, it's quite a dramatic scene. There's a cafe nearby so you can go in and get warm after you've built a gothic-looking sandcastle, perhaps.

reviews.title: Stunning!
reviews.text: A stunning black sand beach with fascinating rock formations all around but beware the sneaker waves (saw plenty of selfie-taking people get their feet wet!)

reviews.title: It's beautiful and dramatic--you should stop here for sure
reviews.text: If you are on the ring road, and why wouldn't you be, you are probably on your way here anyway.  Other than the number of other people also on the beach, this place is just fantastic.  Crashing waves, dramatic sunsets, basalt columns, black beach rocks, it's got it all.  There is a restaurant nearby, and it's a free attraction.  One of the must see spots in Iceland.

reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.text: This is a black sand beach with an extraordinary cave (where a couple were having wedding photos taken whilst it was freezing and blowing a hooley) and some interesting off shore rock formations. Great location for photos. The waves are very dangerous and a couple of people were swept off their feet in spite of the warnings. Plenty of parking and a good café too.

reviews.title: Photo Opportunities
reviews.text: Stopped here as part of a photography workshop for early morning sunrise.  Beautiful basalt rock cliffs and caves bordering the black sand beach with sea stacks out in the water.  Parking, small cafe and WC at location.

reviews.title: Great ocean
reviews.text: The location is at the black sand beach. Is very windy as is beside the ocean.. the sand is black volcano sand.. with the special stone formations. Be careful of the waves though as is might goes very high most of times.

reviews.title: Stunning Beauty
reviews.text: Loved visiting this popular Black Sand Beach near Vik, Iceland with beautiful rock formations just off shore.  Yes, there will be lots of people but the beach is large and you only have to walk a bit to find some privacy.  There is a cave and basalt pillars which are also photo opportunities.  If your lucky enough to catch a sunset on a clear day you won't be disappointed!

reviews.title: Extremely beautiful, Extremely busy
reviews.text: A definite must see if visiting the south coast and every tour company in Iceland agrees.  It is truly something unique and beautiful.  The only problem is that when you go you are likely to be surrounded by tons of other people.  That’s the reason I can’t give it an excellent rating

reviews.title: Black sand beach....nature's wonder
reviews.text: Visited Reynisfjara beach on 7th of March 2018. This is one of my favourite places in iceland. The fine black sand on the shore is amazing and a nature s wonder. We visited it during sunset and it was so serene and a visual treat.

reviews.title: black pearl beach is so amazing
reviews.text: the scene from Game of Thrones with black basalt columns and black lava beach... and strong waves crashing in ... was crazy beautiful

reviews.title: Beautiful beach but very busy
reviews.text: The beach was lovely, but was incredibly busy and also got there on very windy afternoon. With better weather would be more beautiful, however there are prettier places within iceland than this beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: If you are visiting the southern coast of Iceland, definitely make this a must-stop on your itinerary. It was beautiful! The basalt columns are incredible and make for some really amazing pictures. Walk around the corner to the cave too; it's really amazing. Great coastal views here too. Loved it!

reviews.title: Cool black beach
reviews.text: Nice visit to a black beach. Not a place to sunbathe but interesting texture and my kids even did sand angels. It is less windy in a cave which allows to sit and enjoy the view away from the wind.

reviews.title: Black beach
reviews.text: A stunning black beach with basalt columns and caves well worth visiting.Plenty of parking and a cafe next to the beach.

reviews.title: I CAN SEE FOR MILES AND MILES AND MILES!
reviews.text: The same day my son watched Bon Iver perform in London we walked the beach featured in the Bon Iver video 'Holocene'. It was a really windy day which added to the drama, The views are amazing. There are warning signs posted to alert you about sneaker waves, so you can spend an hour watching the idiots getting soaked trying to dodge the waves! Wrap up well, and wear Gore Tex if you're an idiot!

reviews.title: Multi faceted wonder
reviews.text: Visited on a self-drive day trip to see the nearby waterfalls and Dyrholaey. There is a black sand beach in Vik but this one is before Vik and is signposted as Reynisfjara. The car park is free and there is a restaurant on site but be aware it ain't cheap (£5 for a coffee and £7.50 for a small portion of chips). The beach itself is stunning and though it will be busy most times it is large enough to not be intrusive in my view. The waves are spectacular and fun to dodge, just don't turn your back on them, as they bite. Take waterproof boots/shoes if you want to get near the shoreline. The rock formations are stunning and if you are lucky the weather conditions can compliment the views. Definitely worth a visit as part of any tour.

reviews.title: Beautiful in a blizzard, has to be amazing in good weather!
reviews.text: It was difficult to really enjoy this beach in the midst of horrible weather, but, even so, it was worth the trip. The sea was very rough and a little eerie in the half light, with the rock formations looming in the distance.  Add sunlight and birds and it has to be amazing

reviews.title: Be aware of the sneaker waves ! take a waterproof shoes
reviews.text: The black sand beach is a charming place where you can see the amazing basalt columns along with the sea sight and rock formations (Vik trolls)The sand is always wet due to sneaker waves that usually reach 50% of the bay's area so I would recommend a waterproof shoes to get a more comfortable experience

reviews.title: Island is beautiful
reviews.text: Must see place. Very tranquil, and just outstanding views from top to bottom. We saw The Gullfoss, Geysir and of course the Blu Lagoon

reviews.title: Absolutely stunning
reviews.text: The pictures really don't do this place justice.  You must go there and experience the beauty for yourself.  It was very crowded with tourists so perhaps find a time before of after all of the tour buses arrive, but definitely worth the stop.

reviews.title: One of the most mystical and beautiful places on earth. Truly dangerous waters -- stay way back.
reviews.text: The basalt columns, fascinating caves, and black sand beach made this instantly one of my favorite places on earth. The ocean has never seemed more mighty and powerful than it was here on a windy winter day in February. Do not underestimate the undertow and sudden distance-crossing roaring "sneaker" waves. Several tourists have died here.

reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.text: Worth the visit. Easy access, interesting scenery. It is totally worth the driving there. They have a coffee shop with food and bathroom near the parking lot which is very convenient.

reviews.title: A place of Gods
reviews.text: This placed has got something special for me the moment I seen it in pictures. Being there at dawn, feeling the ocean, the wind and then seeing the sun rising behind the trolls rocks made me feel I am living in a kind of fantasy world. The beauty and power of nature is amazingly combined at Reynisfjara Beach. It was very windy when we've been there, and the force of the wind blowing from the shore to the ocean was getting really strong as we were stepping closer to the end of the beach. Be very precaution when you are there and don't try to climb the basalt rocks.

reviews.title: One for the eyes...
reviews.text: This is a tourist trap without doubt, but don't let that put you off. The beach is easily accessed off Route 1 via the 215 road. Very weather and tide dependent. We parked the car close to the end of the 215 road. This left us with a 200m walk to the beach. The black sand is very striking. You are able to walk close to the cliffs and even climb the basalt stacks. From here you are then able to take in the scale of the place, with the waves coming in.This is an easy stop off to break up a drive.
